title: Rating a verse in F260's practice dialog erases its schedule in the Verses trainer
block:
#### P3-F260-01 — Rating a verse in F260's practice dialog erases its schedule in the Verses trainer

- **Severity: critical** (skeptics: critical / critical; unchanged). Rule (a): the shipped UI silently overwrites a person's stored data (the Leitner box, due date, last review and streak of a verse) in normal use, with no dev tools.
- **Exposure.** An adult has trained a verse in Verses and later rates the same verse in F260's practice dialog, reached by tapping a memorised verse (`apps/f260.html:1648-1650`) or a "Practice again" chip (`apps/f260.html:1343-1346`). Each rating resets one verse. F260 is shown to the five adults and to guests (`apps.json:4`); Verses is also shown to the kids (`apps.json:12`), but they cannot reach F260. Only a verse whose text was pasted into F260 once (kept in `f260.verses`) shows Reveal and the ratings. Without it, the dialog shows only the paste box (`apps/f260.html:1897-1903`). The Verses report records the same precondition (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:165`). Since GAP-VERSES-1 finds text on about 1 card in 10, the precondition narrows the exposure but does not lower the severity.
- **Related.** Not a Phase 2 duplicate: `f260.recall` is not in the `audits/02-shell.md` register, and P2-SYNC-18 is a stale-map write-back, while this happens with a fresh map. Also filed from the Verses side as P3-VERSES-01. That ID is now a pointer to this one, and the roll-up counts the defect once, here.

**What happens now.** F260's "Got it" and "Not yet" both write `recall[prId] = { s, t: Date.now() }` (`apps/f260.html:1915`), a new object that never reads the previous entry, and save the whole map through `hub.set` (`apps/f260.html:902`). Verses keeps `box`, `due`, `last` and `streak` in the same entry (`apps/verses.html:294-298`) and reads a missing box as 1 and a missing due date as "due now" (`apps/verses.html:219`; its comment at `apps/verses.html:218` calls `{s, t}` rows "pre-Leitner"). Measured by the investigator on a box-4 verse:
- before: `{s:'got', box:4, due:'2026-09-29', last:'2026-09-22', streak:3}`;
- after one "Got it" in F260: `{s:'got', t:1790080807298}`;
- the Verses summary went from due 3, boxes `[2,2,6,15,40]` to due 4, boxes `[3,2,6,14,40]`.

F260 shows "★ Got it" while it does this.

**Expected.** F260 merges its fields, `recall[id] = {...recall[id], s, t}`. Better, an F260 rating advances the Leitner fields the way Verses does (`apps/verses.html:294-296`), so the two trainers share one schedule.

**Why it matters to the household.** Spaced repetition is weeks of reviews. A well-learned verse silently drops back to daily review with its streak at 0, and the F260 "Got it" is not even counted as a review in Verses.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:902, 927, 1915, 2077`; `apps/verses.html:193, 218-219, 290-298`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/recall.json` (`rowBefore`, `rowAfterF260GotIt`, `versesBefore`, `versesAfter`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/recall-practice-reveal-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/recall-verses-after-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-1-verses-after-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-2-verses-after-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/recall.mjs"`. It prints `Verses before : {due:3, boxes:[2,2,6,15,40]} | row {s:'got', box:4, due:'2026-09-29', …}`, then `F260 Got it → row {s:'got', t:…}`, then `Verses after : {due:4, boxes:[3,2,6,14,40]}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-1.mjs"` on the iPad (typical seed, demo clock, WebKit, Eli), using only the seeded Verses rows and the shipped UI, no API writes of recall rows:
  - Control, a rating in the Verses UI: 33-0 became `{s:'got', box:4, due:'2026-09-29', last:'2026-09-22', streak:3}`.
  - Path A, tap the memorised Genesis 1:27 in F260, Reveal, Got it: 1-0 went from `{…box:5, due:'2026-10-02', last:'2026-09-18', streak:4}` to `{s:'got', t:1790080811252}`.
  - Path C, the "Practice again" chip for John 17:3, Got it: 36-1 went from `{s:'not', box:1, due:'2026-09-22', …}` to `{s:'got', t:1790080818455}`.
  - Verses afterwards: summary `{due:3, boxes:[3,2,5,15,39]}`; the card read "WEEK 1 · VERSE 1 · Box 1 Genesis 1:27"; Due today listed Genesis 1:27 and John 17:3 as "Box 1 never reviewed", though both had just been rated "Got it" in F260. Only 1-0 and 36-1 changed.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-recall-practice-wipes-verses-box-2.mjs"` on the iPhone PWA with different verses and both ratings: it seeded 12-1 at box 5 and 20-0 at box 3, then rated 12-1 "Not yet" and 20-0 "Got it" in F260.
  - Rows after: `{"12-1":{"s":"not","t":1790080807647},"20-0":{"s":"got","t":1790080812999}}`.
  - Verses: `{due:3, boxes:[2,2,7,14,39]}` → `{due:5, boxes:[4,2,6,14,38]}`; "WEEK 12 · VERSE 2 … Box 1 Psalm 1:1-2", due today.
  - "Got it" sent a box-3 verse to box 1 with streak 0; "Not yet" sent a box-5 verse to box 1, where Verses would demote it by one box (`apps/verses.html:295`).

**Corrected claim.** Confirmed, with detail added:
- Both F260 ratings replace the entry, from either entry point (a memorised verse or a "Practice again" chip).
- `last` is lost as well as `box`, `due` and `streak`, so Verses shows the verse as "never reviewed" and still due today: an F260 "Got it" does not count as a review.
- On the seeded data, one F260 "Got it" dropped a box-5 verse (due 2 Oct) to box 1, due today.
- A stale-map variant (F260 open while Verses rates) would fall under P2-SYNC-18 and was not tested.

title: Undo after Done (or any untick) leaves "Read today ✓", adds a streak day and silences the 8 pm nudge
block:
#### P3-F260-02 — Undo after Done (or any untick) leaves "Read today ✓", adds a streak day and silences the 8 pm nudge

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: medium / medium; unchanged). Not critical: no household data is lost; the tick itself is removed and the total goes back to 187. Not high: Done works. What goes wrong is a secondary flow, an untick or Undo after a mis-tap, which then misleads the Today card, Home, the streak and the 8 pm check.
- **Related.** P2-CHAT-04 (chat flips a tick; Phase 2 noted in passing that chat also leaves `f260.log` alone) and P2-HOME-02 (the summary carries no date).

**What happens now.** Ticking a day sets `log[dayKey()] = true` (`apps/f260.html:1662`). Nothing clears it on an untick, although the code defines `log` as "days with at least one reading checked" (`apps/f260.html:917`). Undo only clicks the reading's mark again (`apps/f260.html:1597-1600`). The summary reads `readToday: !!log[today]` (`apps/f260.html:1507`), and the 8 pm job checks the same log (`worker/src/reminders.js:93-96`). After Done → Undo on Eli's `38-2`:
- correctly reverted: the tick is false, 187 readings, the title is back to "Acts 6";
- still counted as read: the Today card says "Read today ✓" and "13-day streak" (it was 12 before Done); `f260.summary` has `readToday: true` and `streak: 13`; Home says "read today ✓ · 13-day streak";
- the evening job returns `{profile:'eli', readToday:true}`, so the nudge is skipped.

**Expected.** After an untick, remove `log[today]` when no reading ticked today remains, and let the summary follow. A day on which another reading was ticked stays logged.

**Why it matters to the household.** A mis-tap followed by the Undo the app offers credits a day with no reading and switches off that evening's reminder, so the streak stops being trustworthy.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:917, 1503, 1507, 1597-1600, 1660-1662`; `worker/src/reminders.js:93-96`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`undo`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-undo-keeps-read-today-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-undo-keeps-read-today-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-undo-after-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-undo-home-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-undo-keeps-read-today-2-after-undo-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" undo`. It prints `A undo evening job: {"profile":"eli","readToday":true}` and `A undo {before:"Today", afterDone:"Read today ✓", afterUndo:"Read today ✓", logToday:true, readToday:true, tick:false, streak:[12,13,13], home:"… read today ✓ · 13-day streak …"}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-undo-keeps-read-today-1.mjs"` (typical seed, demo clock, WebKit iPhone PWA, Eli). Before Done: "Today", "Acts 6", logToday false, streak 12, total 187. After Done: "Read today ✓", "Acts 7", streak 13, total 188. After Undo: "Read today ✓", "Acts 6", "13-day streak … 2 of 5 this week", logToday true, readToday true, streak 13, total 187, tick false. Reopening F260 gave the same, so nothing rebuilds the log from the ticks. The forced evening job returned `{"profile":"eli","readToday":true}`; Home read "Today's reading 2/5 Acts 6 Week 38, day 3 · read today ✓ · 13-day streak".
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-undo-keeps-read-today-2.mjs" demo`: the evening job gave `readToday:false` before Done and `readToday:true` after Done → Undo; the screenshot shows the READ TODAY ✓ chip beside an unticked 2/5 ring. Control, Mom, who had already read that day: `log[today]` stayed true through a tick and an untick, which is correct and must survive any fix.

**Corrected claim.** Accurate, with two additions:
- The cause is the shared tick handler (`apps/f260.html:1660-1662`), so unticking the day directly on the plan list has the same effect as Undo.
- From code only, not observed: if the phantom day pushes the streak past the best, `f260.best` is raised (`apps/f260.html:1503`) and never lowered. It did not happen here because the best was 53.

title: The day after two rest days, the streak reads 0 and "Start a new streak" until the person reads
block:
#### P3-F260-03 — The day after two rest days, the streak reads 0 and "Start a new streak" until the person reads

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: medium / medium; unchanged). Nothing is lost: the log and the best stay, and the streak returns the moment Done is tapped. But every streak surface is wrong for the whole day: the Today card, the Next up hero, Home through `f260.summary`, and chat's `f260_status`. Not high, because the reading flow works; not low, because a Monday-to-Friday reader meets it every week.

**What happens now.** `streakInfo` starts its walk at today (`apps/f260.html:1386`), so an unread today adds to the gap. Read Saturday, rest Sunday and Monday, open on Tuesday: the gap reaches 3, the walk stops before Saturday, and the streak is set to 0 (`apps/f260.html:1392`). The quiet "Pick up where you left off" state keys on streak 0 and 3+ days since the last reading (`apps/f260.html:1530, 1558`), and Home drops the streak when it is 0 (`index.html:1169`). Before reading: "Pick up where you left off", "Start a new streak · last read Sep 19 · best 53", `summary.streak` 0. After Done: "🔥 12-day streak", `summary.streak` 12. The streak was never broken.

**Expected.** Treat today as pending: when today is unread, start the walk from yesterday. The hub's own prayer streak already does this (`index.html:837-844`, the step back at `index.html:841`), as do Apple Fitness and Books.

**Why it matters to the household.** The owner asked that waiting a day or two not reset the streak, and the heatmap label promises it: "2 rest days between readings keep the streak" (`apps/f260.html:594`). The rule holds only after the person reads; until then every surface, Home included, tells them it is gone.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:594, 1385-1395, 1507, 1530, 1558, 1585-1587`; `index.html:837-844, 1169`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`streak`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-streak-today-counted-missed-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-streak-today-counted-missed-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-streak-before-read-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-streak-after-read-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-streak-today-counted-missed-2-webkit-B-before-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" streak`. It prints `C streak {lastLogDays:[…"2026-09-19"], before:["Pick up where you left off","Start a new streaklast read Sep 19 · best 53","summary.streak=0"], after:["Read today ✓","🔥 12-day streakbest 53 · 3 of 5 this week","summary.streak=12"]}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-streak-today-counted-missed-1.mjs"` (WebKit iPhone PWA, Eli's log set to read Sep 19 and nothing after). Before: "Pick up where you left off", "Start a new streak last read Sep 19 · best 53", hero quiet, `summary.streak=0`, Home without a streak. After Done: "🔥 12-day streak", `summary.streak=12`, Home "· read today ✓ · 12-day streak". Probes on the lifted `streakInfo`: Sat read, Sun and Mon rest, Tue unread → streak 0 and no rest days; the same with Tue read → 7 with Sep 20-21 as rest days; Sun read, Mon rest, Tue unread → 7 with today itself counted as a rest day.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-streak-today-counted-missed-2.mjs"` in WebKit and Chromium with identical output. Scenario A (read Sat, open Tue) as above. Scenario B, a Monday-to-Friday reader (read Fri 18, open Mon 21 08:40): "Pick up where you left off", "Start a new streak last read Sep 18 · best 53", `summary.streak=0`, Home without a streak. Control C (one rest day): "🔥 11-day streak", `summary.streak=11`.

**Corrected claim.** Accurate, with refinements:
- The wrong state lasts all day until a reading is ticked, not only the morning.
- It happens only when both rest days are used; with one rest day, the unread today quietly becomes the second rest day and the streak still shows.
- In the failing state the heatmap shows Sunday and Monday as plain gaps rather than rest days, because the rest days are cleared when the walk finds no read day, contradicting the label at `apps/f260.html:594`.
- The most common trigger is broader than the example: anyone who reads Monday to Friday sees "Start a new streak" every Monday until they tap Done.
- Not a duplicate of P2-HOME-02 (a stale summary from yesterday), though both leave Home showing the wrong streak.

title: After 260/260, unticking a reading keeps the plan "finished", which mutes the 8 pm and Sunday nudges
block:
#### P3-F260-04 — After 260/260, unticking a reading keeps the plan "finished", which mutes the 8 pm and Sunday nudges

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). No data is lost; only a derived flag is stale.
- **Exposure.** Someone who has ticked all 260 readings unticks one (for example a mis-tap on the plan). The Sunday nudge is affected only once two or more are unticked.

**What happens now.** The 260th tick sets `finished = dayKey()` and shows the "Plan complete" modal (`apps/f260.html:1672`). The untick branch (`apps/f260.html:1673`) never clears it, and the summary writes `finished: !!finished` whatever the total (`apps/f260.html:1508`). Only Reset (`apps/f260.html:1765`) or a restore (`apps/f260.html:1119`) clears it. The 8 pm job skips anyone with `summary.finished` (`worker/src/reminders.js:96`), and the Sunday check returns `why:'no_summary'` (`worker/src/reminders.js:114`). Measured: after unticking 52-1, `finished` stayed "2026-09-22" and `summary.finished` true with a total of 259; ticking it again did not bring the modal back.

**Expected.** When the total drops below 260, clear `finished` and `summary.finished`, so the nudges resume; finishing again can show the moment again.

**Why it matters to the household.** A reader with an unread reading gets no evening nudge and no Sunday catch-up, and the finish date shown later stays the date of the first finish.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:928, 1119, 1341, 1508, 1543, 1672-1673, 1703, 1765`; `worker/src/reminders.js:96, 108, 114`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`end`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-finished-flag-sticks-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-finished-flag-sticks-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-plan-complete-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-finished-flag-sticks-1-after-untick-ipad.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" end`. It prints `E end {pctAt259:"100% complete", modalOnLastTick:true, finished:"2026-09-22", untick:"2026-09-22 summary.finished=true total=259 …", retickShowsComplete:false}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-finished-flag-sticks-1.mjs"` (iPad portrait, Eli seeded at 259/260). Last tick: modal shown, `finished:'2026-09-22'`, total 260. After unticking 52-1 and 52-2: `finished` and `summaryFinished` still set, total 258, "99% complete", Today offered "Revelation 2-3". Running the Worker's own `eveningJob` on those rows: `notifyReached:false`; on a control copy with `finished:false`: `notifyReached:true`. `behindFor`: `{behind:0, why:'no_summary'}`, control `{behind:2, days:15}`. Re-ticking: no automatic modal, but the hero's "See your year" still opened it.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-finished-flag-sticks-2.mjs"` with real taps on the plan's circles (iPhone PWA). After unticking 52-1: `finished` "2026-09-22", summary `{total:259, finished:true}`. `behindFor` as written: `{behind:0, why:'no_summary'}`; with `finished` cleared: `{behind:1, days:12}`, below the push threshold of 2. Re-tick: no automatic modal; "See your year" and the week-52 `[data-complete]` button still present.

**Corrected claim.** The stale flag muting the reminders is the defect, not a lost celebration:
- The app's own display recovers after the untick (the percentage and Today follow the real total; the "100%" at 259 is P3-F260-10).
- The year-complete view can still be opened by hand from the hero's "See your year" (`apps/f260.html:1543, 1703`) and from the week-52 row (`apps/f260.html:1341, 1632`).
- The Sunday check matters only once 2 or more readings are unticked (`worker/src/reminders.js:108`).

title: Opening F260 once enrols a guest or Mea in the 8 pm and Sunday reading nudges
block:
#### P3-F260-05 — Opening F260 once enrols a guest or Mea in the 8 pm and Sunday reading nudges

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). No data is lost or exposed; the effect is unwanted reminders for someone who only looked, and it needs that person to have turned push on.
- **Related.** P2-SYNC-05: the same boot write (`apps/f260.html:938`). That ID is an existing history overwritten on a slow pull; this is every first open by a person with no data, with no slow pull.

**What happens now.** With no start date for the current week, boot writes `weekStart[curWeek] = today` (`apps/f260.html:938`), and the first render saves `f260.summary` (`apps/f260.html:1506-1509`). The 8 pm job walks every profile that has any F260 row (`worker/src/reminders.js:82-99`), and the Sunday job keeps every profile of kind `adult` (`worker/src/reminders.js:56`), which includes guests (`worker/src/index.js:170`). Push preferences default to on (`worker/src/reminders.js:25`). Grandma Jo (a guest) and Mea had 0 F260 rows; opening F260 once, with no tap, POSTed `f260.weekStart` and `f260.summary`, and the evening job then checked `guest-grandmajo:false` and `niece:false`.

**Expected.** Viewing the plan writes nothing; the first row is written when the person ticks a reading or changes a setting.

**Why it matters to the household.** A grandparent who peeks at the plan once starts getting "No reading checked off today yet" every evening, and "N readings behind" on Sundays.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:938, 1506-1509`; `worker/src/reminders.js:25, 56, 59-64, 82-99, 110-135`; `worker/src/index.js:170`; `index.html:1161-1170`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/guest.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-first-open-enrols-guest-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-first-open-enrols-guest-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/guest-guest-grandmajo-first-open-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-first-open-enrols-guest-2-guest-grandmajo-home-after-ipad.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/guest.mjs"`. It prints `guest-grandmajo | rows before [] | written by opening: ["f260.weekStart","f260.summary"]` and `8 pm F260 nudge now checks: [… "guest-grandmajo:false" … "niece:false"]`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-first-open-enrols-guest-1.mjs"`. Evening job before any open: `["christian:true","dad:false","eli:false","mom:true"]`. For both Grandma Jo and Mea: rows before `[]`, opening POSTed `[f260.weekStart, f260.summary]`, `weekStart {"1":"2026-09-22"}`. Evening job after: the list gained `"guest-grandmajo:false"` and `"niece:false"`. The behind job listed both with `why:"week_too_young"`. Home card before opening: "Today's reading 0/5 Start with Genesis 1-2 Week 1 of 52 Open F260"; after: "Today's reading 0/5 Genesis 1-2 Week 1, day 1 Open F260".
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-first-open-enrols-guest-2.mjs"` on the iPad and saw the same POSTs, the same evening list, and `…"guest-grandmajo:week_too_young",…"niece:week_too_young"` from the behind job; from Sunday 27 September the job would judge them 5 readings behind.

**Corrected claim.** Opening F260 once, with no tap, puts a guest or Mea on the 8 pm list and, from the fourth day of the week, on the Sunday "behind" list, because the behind job's adult filter lets guests through. A push is delivered only if the person has turned notifications on for a device; local delivery was not proven (the demo has no push subscriptions). **Home does not gain a card**, as the investigator had written: the "Today's reading" card is already shown to everyone who can see F260, and only its text changes.

title: A device in another time zone files the reading under its own date
block:
#### P3-F260-06 — A device in another time zone files the reading under its own date

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). No reading is lost: `done` keeps the tick and only the `f260.log` date key moves by a day.
- **Exposure.** Travel outside Eastern time, or a phone set to another zone, and a tick between that zone's midnight and New York's midnight. The household's known trip (Pigeon Forge, TN) is in Eastern time.

**What happens now.** `dayKey` uses the device's local date (`apps/f260.html:932`), and a tick sets `log[dayKey()]` (`apps/f260.html:1662`). The Worker works in America/New_York (`worker/src/reminders.js:13, 89-96`). Eli's phone set to Europe/London taps Done on a New York Tuesday evening: the log gets 2026-09-23, not 22. The family's New York iPad then shows F260 "Today" (unread) for Tuesday, and on Wednesday shows "Read today ✓" although nothing was read that New York day.

**Expected.** The day key follows the household's zone (America/New_York), as the Worker does, or the New York date is stored beside it.

**Why it matters to the household.** Two devices show a different "read today" for the same row at the same moment, and a nudge can be wrong in both directions.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:932, 1507, 1662`; `worker/src/reminders.js:13, 89-96, 247-253`; `worker/wrangler.toml:25`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/time.json` (`tz`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-1-london-after-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-1-ny-tue-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-1-ny-wed-ipad.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/time.mjs"`. It prints `B London phone: Europe/London ["Wed, Sep 23",…] log {"2026-09-22":false,"2026-09-23":true}`, `B New York iPad F260: ["Today","Tue, Sep 22",…]` and `B evening job (NY date): {"profile":"eli","readToday":false}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-1.mjs"` with the tap at 19:30 New York (00:30 London). The phone read "Wed, Sep 23" and then "Read today ✓" (streak 12 → 13); the server had log22 false, log23 true. The evening job at 20:00 NY: date 2026-09-22, Eli `readToday:false`. The New York iPad at 20:01: "Today", "Tue, Sep 22", streak 12; on Wednesday 08:40: "Read today ✓", streak 13.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-other-timezone-logs-next-day-2.mjs"` with a tap at 20:30 NY and one at 19:30 NY. Both filed 2026-09-23; the New York iPad showed "Today" for Tuesday; the Tuesday 20:00 job gave `readToday:false` and the Wednesday 20:00 job `readToday:true`.

**Corrected claim.** One step of the investigator's chain was wrong. The scheduled evening job runs once, at 20:00 New York (`worker/src/reminders.js:253`; crons at 0 and 1 UTC, `worker/wrangler.toml:25`). A tap at 20:30 comes after that night's nudge, which was due; the investigator's `readToday:false` came from forcing the job at 20:31. A nudge for a reading already done needs the tap between the other zone's midnight and 20:00 New York (19:00-20:00 NY for London in September). The misfiled key also suppresses the next New York day's nudge even when nothing is read that day.

title: Done on next week's first reading starts that week, and Undo does not give the week back
block:
#### P3-F260-07 — Done on next week's first reading starts that week, and Undo does not give the week back

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). An edge case: the current week must be complete, Done must land in the next week, and the person must then Undo. No reading is lost, and the week stepper can move back.

**What happens now.** Done on a reading in a later week calls `setCurrent(w)` (`apps/f260.html:1592`; the comment there says this is intended), which writes `weekStart[w]` when empty (`apps/f260.html:1684-1689`). Undo only clicks the reading's mark (`apps/f260.html:1597-1600`). Mae's week 37 was complete; Done ticked 38-0, moved the week 37 → 38 and set `weekStart[38]` to today. Undo removed the tick, but the week stayed 38 and `weekStart[38]` stayed, surviving a reopen.

**Expected.** Undo also restores the previous current week and removes the start date it just created.

**Why it matters to the household.** Mae's plan says she started week 38 today when she has not, and when she really starts it, its "started" date and "done in N days" count from the mistaken tap.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:1327, 1397, 1589-1600, 1684-1689`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`ahead`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-1-before-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-1-after-undo-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" ahead`. It prints `B ahead {week:[37,38,38], ws38:[null,"2026-09-22","2026-09-22"], tick:false}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-1.mjs"` (iPhone PWA, Mae). Before: week 37 at 5/5, hero "Week 37 done / Start week 38 / Acts is next · started Sep 18", pace "6 days ahead · projected finish Jan 2027". After Done: week 38, `ws38:'2026-09-22'`, pace "1 week ahead". After Undo and after a reopen: week 38, `ws38:'2026-09-22'`, tick false, `summary.week` 38 with 0 done, hero "Next up / Acts 2-3 / Week 38 · Day 1 · … · started Sep 22", ring 0/5, pace back to "6 days ahead".
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-ahead-undo-keeps-week-2.mjs"` and saw the same; the earliest week start stayed 2026-01-12, and `#curWeekLbl` showed 38.

**Corrected claim.** **Pace is not affected**, as the investigator had written: `paceInfo()` uses only the earliest week start and the number of readings (`apps/f260.html:1397`), and it read "6 days ahead" both before Done and after Undo. The real effects are the hero ("Next up · Week 38 · started Sep 22" instead of "Week 37 done · Start week 38"), the Today ring (0/5), the Home summary (week 38, 0 done) and the kept `weekStart[38]`. Unticking in the plan or pressing "Start week" also leaves the week in place, so only the Undo asymmetry is new.

title: The heatmap's "today" cell takes the Today card's styles and breaks the grid
block:
#### P3-F260-08 — The heatmap's "today" cell takes the Today card's styles and breaks the grid

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). A read-only progress visual; no data or flow is affected. Skeptic 2 noted medium as arguable for the Kitchen iPad in landscape, where 11 days vanish.

**What happens now.** Today's heatmap cell gets the class `today` (`apps/f260.html:1515`), so it also matches the Today card's unscoped `.today` rules (`apps/f260.html:117, 153, 156`), where only a gold ring was meant (`apps/f260.html:95`). On the phone it is 35×33 with 16 px padding and a border, against 25×12 for the other cells. At 1024 px and wider it gets `grid-column: 1/-1` and becomes a 332×44 bar across the heatmap, breaking the Monday-to-Sunday rows.

**Expected.** One small gold-ringed cell, like the others.

**Why it matters to the household.** On the Kitchen iPad in landscape and on desktop, the 12-week history is misdrawn: days shift and some disappear.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:92-96, 117, 153, 156, 499, 1515`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/layout.json` (`devices.*.heat`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/layout-heat-today-desktop.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/layout-heat-today-iphone-pwa.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-2-ipad-landscape.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-2-ipad-landscape-counterfactual.png`, `audits/screens/f260/today-typical-desktop-light.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/layout.mjs"`. It prints `iphone-pwa heat today {w:35,h:33,display:"grid",padding:"16px 16px"} other {w:25,h:12}` and `desktop heat today {w:332,h:44,gridColumn:"1/-1"}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-1.mjs"` on four devices. iPhone PWA: today 35×33, `display:grid`, padding 16px, a 1.33 px border, 8 row positions instead of 7. iPad portrait: 39×37, padding 18px. iPad landscape and desktop: 332×44-45, `gridColumn '1 / -1'`, and the other cells split into 72 at 24×12 and 11 at 0×12. Control with the class renamed: 25×12, a 12×7 grid on all four devices.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-heatmap-today-class-collision-2.mjs"` with a counterfactual that removes the class: the same sizes; on wide screens the cells after today fall into an implicit 0 px column (`{w:0, x:336}`) and past days move down a row; with the class removed, 25×12 everywhere.

**Corrected claim.** Accurate and slightly understated. At 1024 px and wider, including the Kitchen iPad in landscape (1180 px), 11 other day cells collapse to 0 px wide, so part of the history disappears. On iPad portrait the cell is 39×37 with 18 px padding; 16 px padding applies only at 480 px and below. The print rule at `apps/f260.html:499` also matches the cell, with no visible effect.

title: Reading mode hides the "This week" reflections card it means to keep
block:
#### P3-F260-09 — Reading mode hides the "This week" reflections card it means to keep

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). The card comes back on leaving reading mode, and each day's HEAR panel stays reachable.

**What happens now.** `.readmode .side{display:block}` and `.readmode .side > :not(#reflect){display:none}` (`apps/f260.html:184-186`) exist to keep `#reflect` visible. The later rule `.readmode .side, .readmode .week:not(.reading){display:none}` (`apps/f260.html:427`), with the same specificity, hides the whole side column, `#reflect` included (`#reflect` sits inside `.side`, `apps/f260.html:577, 608`).

**Expected.** The week's reflections card shows above the week in reading mode.

**Why it matters to the household.** The reader loses the week's Apply and Respond notes at the moment they are reading.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:184-186, 427, 577, 608, 1725-1733`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/journal.json` (`readingMode`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-reading-mode-hides-reflections-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-reading-mode-hides-reflections-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/journal-reading-mode-two-done-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-reading-mode-hides-reflections-2-iphone-readmode.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/journal.mjs"`. It prints `readingMode {"reflect":"hidden by .side","sideDisplay":"none",…}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-reading-mode-hides-reflections-1.mjs"` with the journal locked, on the iPhone PWA and desktop: before, `#reflect` 398×117 (desktop 374×172); in reading mode, `side:none`, `#reflect` 0×0, `hiddenBy:'.side'`. The matching rules in source order end with the line-427 rule, which wins.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-reading-mode-hides-reflections-2.mjs"` with the journal unlocked and one Apply line (WebKit iPhone), then Chromium desktop with it locked: in reading mode the card is 0×0 with its one item still in the DOM; after Done it is back at 398×223.

**Corrected claim.** Holds exactly, and does not depend on the journal's state (locked or unlocked) or the engine. Also noted: `#readBtn` and `#reflectBtn` sit inside `.side`, so they are hidden in reading mode too; only `#readExit` leaves it.

title: "100% complete" with one reading left, and "0%" after the first
block:
#### P3-F260-10 — "100% complete" with one reading left, and "0%" after the first

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). A label only; the count, the meter and the real finish (which needs 260, `apps/f260.html:1672`) are right.

**What happens now.** `Math.round(n / 260 * 100)` (`apps/f260.html:1494`) gives "100% complete" at 259 readings, while the Today card still offers "Revelation 20-22" with its Done button, and "0% complete" beside "1 of 260 readings".

**Expected.** Floor the value, or cap it at 99 below 260 and show at least 1% once a reading is done.

**Why it matters to the household.** "100%" with a reading left looks like the plan is done, and "0%" after the first reading looks like it was not counted.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:1214, 1490-1495, 1672`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`end.at259.ui`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-percent-rounds-to-100-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-percent-rounds-to-100-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic-259-of-260-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-percent-rounds-to-100-2-259-of-260-ipad.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" end`. It prints `pctAt259 "100% complete"` and `todayAt259 "Revelation 20-22"`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-percent-rounds-to-100-1.mjs"` for n = 1, 2, 258, 259: at 259, `{pct:'100% complete', doneCount:'259', todayTitle:'Revelation 20-22', meterWidth:'99.615385%'}`; 258 → 99%; 2 → 1%; 1 → "0% complete" with the meter at 0.384615%.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-percent-rounds-to-100-2.mjs"` for n = 1, 2, 258, 259, 260 with the same results; at 260, "Plan complete".

**Corrected claim.** None. Only n = 259 rounds up to a false 100% and only n = 1 rounds down to 0%. The book journey bar (`apps/f260.html:1524`) uses the same rounding but no book can reach a one-left case that shows 100%.

title: Pace reads "2 week behind" / "2 week ahead"
block:
#### P3-F260-11 — Pace reads "2 week behind" / "2 week ahead"

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). Grammar in one status line; the number, colour and projected finish are right.

**What happens now.** The plural is chosen from the raw difference in days (≥ 14), but the number shown is `Math.round(diff / 7)` (`apps/f260.html:1403, 1405`). Between 10.5 and 14 days ahead or behind, the Next up hero's pace line (`#heroPace`, `apps/f260.html:599`) pairs "2" with "week": "2 week behind · projected finish Jan 2027".

**Expected.** Choose the plural from the rounded number.

**Why it matters to the household.** A visible grammar slip in the line that tells a reader how far behind they are, shown to anyone 1.5 to 2 weeks off pace.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:599, 1396-1409, 1546-1548`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/logic.json` (`pace`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-pace-week-plural-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-pace-week-plural-2.json`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/logic.mjs" pace`. It prints `D pace behind11 … diff -11.2 → "2 week behind · …"` and `ahead11 … diff 10.8 → "2 week ahead · …"`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-pace-week-plural-1.mjs"`: diff -13.2 and -12.2 → "2 week behind"; 10.8 and 12.8 → "2 week ahead"; 14.8 → "2 weeks ahead"; 5 mismatches in 10 cases.

title: The unlock dialog says "encrypted on this iPad" on every device (from the visual check)
block:
#### P3-F260-12 — The unlock dialog says "encrypted on this iPad" on every device (from the visual check)

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; unchanged). Wrong wording; unlocking works everywhere.
- **Related.** One of three parts of the storage-copy problem, none counted twice: this unlock sentence; the Erase and Restore confirms (P3-F260-15, from the critic); and the footer, Restore sheet and empty-state wording (UX-F260-1).

**What happens now.** The unlock text is a constant (`apps/f260.html:1133-1134`): "Your HEAR journal is encrypted on this iPad. Enter your passcode to read or write it." It shows on the iPhone and on desktop too.

**Expected.** Copy that is true on every device: the journal is encrypted with the person's passcode and follows them to their devices.

**Why it matters to the household.** People act on this copy when deciding what Erase or a lost device means (P3-F260-15, UX-F260-1).

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:902, 1022, 1133-1136, 1787`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/screens/f260/journal-unlock-typical-iphone-pwa-dark.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-1-iphone-pwa.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-1.mjs"`: on the iPhone PWA and desktop, set a throwaway passcode, lock, reopen Journal, read `#passText`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-1.mjs"`: the iPhone (UA "iPhone OS 26_0", width 430) and desktop (UA "Macintosh", width 1440) both showed "Your HEAR journal is encrypted on this iPad…". The only other "iPad" string is the Face ID help (`apps/f260.html:1787`).
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-vis-unlock-dialog-says-encrypted-on-this-ipad-on-an--1-2.mjs"`: the same text on the iPhone, desktop and Kitchen iPad; the vault was on the server in Eli's person scope (`{present:true, v:2, hasPass:true}`), and the desktop unlocked it with the phone's passcode.

**Corrected claim.** The copy is wrong on the iPad too: the vault `f260.journal.vault` is saved through `hub.set` to the person scope (`apps/f260.html:902, 1022`), held on the server and unlocked from a second device with the same passcode, so "this device" would still be wrong. The set-mode sentence "It never leaves this device" (`apps/f260.html:1136`) refers to the passcode itself and is accurate (`audits/01-leads.md:98`). The Face ID help "needs iPadOS 18 or newer" (`apps/f260.html:1787`) is iPad-only wording on the iPhone.

title: A device with the journal still unlocked overwrites a vault that another device erased or re-created; the journal then opens nowhere (from the critic)
block:
#### P3-F260-13 — A device with the journal still unlocked overwrites a vault that another device erased or re-created; the journal then opens nowhere (from the critic)

- **Severity: critical** (skeptics: critical / critical; the critic filed critical). Rule (a): the shipped UI alone loses household data. In the start-over case the vault left on the server pairs the new passcode's key wrap with ciphertext made under the old key. Neither passcode opens it, and the entries written after starting over are lost on every device. No dev tools are needed; the narrow trigger goes on the Exposure line, not into the severity.
- **Exposure.** The same person has the journal unlocked on one device and uses Settings → Erase journal, or Erase and then a new passcode, on another; the unlocked device then saves a HEAR field. The unlock window is long: auto-lock defaults to 15 minutes (`apps/f260.html:920`) and "Never" is offered. The Erase copy invites the mistake, because it says it deletes "from this device" (P3-F260-15). Restoring a backup made under an older vault key is a likely further trigger (code only, not run).
- **Related.** p2Ref **P2-SYNC-20**, a failed save that pairs a new iv with the old ciphertext on one device. This finding has a different trigger (a second device) and a new failure mode (a vault row with no `pass`, which throws on unlock). It is also a vault-specific case of the stale-writer pattern in P2-SYNC-01 and P2-SYNC-18. P3-F260-15 is the Erase copy that invites it.

**What happens now.** `persistJournal()` encrypts the journal with the data key it holds in memory and writes `iv` and `ct` into whatever vault row the hub cache holds at that moment (`const blob = vaultBlob() || {}`, `apps/f260.html:1015-1022`). It never checks that the row still carries the key wrap it unlocked. While the vault is open F260 defers every remote merge (`apps/f260.html:2089`), so the stale device keeps its old key and its open panel, even after the SDK's own 30 s pull (`apps/hub.js:342`) has put the erased or re-keyed row into its cache. Any focusout on a HEAR field saves (`apps/f260.html:1864-1868`).
- **Erase only (E1).** The phone erases, and the server vault becomes null. The iPad, still unlocked, saves one typed line, and the server vault becomes `{ct, iv, v}` with no `pass`. `vaultState()` reads any row as "locked" (`apps/f260.html:1001`), so every device shows "Unlock journal" with no way to set a new passcode. The right passcode gives "Something went wrong: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'blob.pass.salt')": `unlock` reads `blob.pass.salt` outside its try (`apps/f260.html:1038`), and the form prints the raw message (`apps/f260.html:1168`). Only another Erase recovers the journal.
- **Erase and start over (E2).** The phone erases, sets a new passcode and writes a new entry. The iPad's save then leaves `{ct, iv, pass, v}`: the phone's new `pass` wrap with the iPad's old-key ciphertext. The new passcode and the old one both give "Wrong passcode.", and the phone's new entry is lost. The iPad's own new line becomes unreadable too once the iPad locks.

**Expected.** A device holding an older vault never saves over one that was erased or re-keyed. `persistJournal` compares the cached row's `pass.salt` (or a vault id) with the one it unlocked; on a mismatch it locks, drops its stale key and tells the person. A vault row without `pass` is never written, and unlock handles one without throwing.

**Why it matters to the household.** The whole journal becomes unopenable on every device, and the entries written after starting over are gone. The only message is a raw JavaScript error, and the only way forward is another Erase.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:920, 998-1001, 1015-1025, 1036-1039, 1056, 1164-1168, 1769, 1864-1868, 2085-2090`; `apps/hub.js:342`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-vault-stale-device.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-vault-stale-E1-phone-unlock.png` (the raw error in the unlock dialog), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-vault-stale-E2-phone-unlock.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-2-E1-phone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-2-E2-phone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/critic-vault-stale-device.mjs"` runs both variants; pass `E1` or `E2` for one. Typical seed, WebKit, Eli on a new phone device and on the Kitchen iPad, throwaway passcodes 2468 and 9753. The phone sets a passcode and writes Apply on 38-0; the iPad unlocks with the same passcode and leaves the entry open; the phone runs Settings → Erase journal → Erase (E2 then sets passcode 9753 and writes on 38-1); the iPad pulls, types a Respond line and taps away; the phone reopens F260 → Journal → enters the passcode. Observed:
- E1: `serverAfterErase null`; `serverAfterIpadSave {keys:[ct,iv,v], hasPass:false}`; `phoneUnlockResult {err:"Something went wrong: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'blob.pass.salt')"}`.
- E2: `serverAfterNewPass {keys:[ct,iv,pass,v]}`; `serverAfterIpadSave {keys:[ct,iv,pass,v]}`; `phoneUnlockResult {err:'Wrong passcode.'}`; `phoneOldPassResult {err:'Wrong passcode.'}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-1.mjs"` in modes E1, E2 and C0 (a fresh instance each; WebKit; Eli on a new iPhone PWA and the Kitchen iPad; throwaway passcodes 1357 and 8642). Unlike the critic's script it never forces a pull on the iPad; it waits 40 s for the SDK's own background pull, and every step is a real UI action.
  - E1: the server vault went `[ct,iv,pass,v]` → null → `{keys:[ct,iv,v], hasPass:false}`. Before its save the iPad's cache already held null while its open entry still showed "Phone entry: share a meal." The phone showed "Unlock journal" with no confirm field; the right passcode gave the `blob.pass.salt` error.
  - E2: after the phone's new passcode the vault had salt `KMfT2uYdpb` and ct `cQ9GBRWmwF`; after the iPad's save it had the same salt with ct `kwJ2DDvy9l`, the iPad's ciphertext under the old key. On the phone the new and the old passcode both gave "Wrong passcode."
  - C0 (the iPad saving right after the erase) ended like E1, because the tombstone reached the iPad's cache before `persistJournal` ran.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-vault-stale-device-overwrites-1-2.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit, passcodes 1357 and 8642, entries on 38-2 and 38-3; it waits 36 s for the interval pull, then types on the iPad and taps into another field, then locks the iPad and tries to reopen).
  - E1: `v2_afterErase null`; `ipadCachedVault null` while the iPad still showed "Original entry from the phone."; `v4_afterIpadSave {keys:[ct,iv,v], passSalt:null}`. The iPad itself, locked and given the old passcode, and the phone given the right one, both showed the `blob.pass.salt` error; the phone's dialog read "Unlock journal" with the confirm field hidden.
  - E2: `v3_afterNewPass {passSalt:'eitZvvkXwK'}`; after the iPad's save the salt was still the phone's and the iv had changed. The iPad's old passcode, the phone's new passcode and the phone's old passcode all gave "Wrong passcode."

**Corrected claim.** Accurate, with three refinements from the skeptics:
- The stale device needs no forced pull. The SDK's 30 s pull brings the erased or re-keyed row into its cache; F260 keeps its old in-memory key because merges wait while the vault is open, and `persistJournal` writes over whatever row is cached.
- In E2 the stale device's own new line is lost as well once it locks.
- The other ordering, a stale device writing back the whole old vault before its pull and so quietly undoing the erase, was not isolated, and neither was the restore-of-an-old-backup trigger. The raw error text is WebKit's; Chromium words it differently.

title: Face ID unlock is one synced slot: other devices show a Face ID button that fails, and enabling it on a second device breaks the first (from the critic)
block:
#### P3-F260-14 — Face ID unlock is one synced slot: other devices show a Face ID button that fails, and enabling it on a second device breaks the first (from the critic)

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: medium / medium; the critic filed medium). No data is lost or exposed: the data key stays wrapped and the passcode always unlocks. What breaks is an opt-in, experimental secondary flow: a Face ID button and an "On." status that are wrong on every device but one, and a second device's set-up that silently breaks the first. That is the medium clause, "a secondary flow broken or misleading".
- **Exposure.** A person who uses F260 on two devices that do not share one passkey store and turns on the experimental Face ID option. Examples: the shared Kitchen iPad signed into another family member's Apple ID alongside the person's own iPhone, iCloud Keychain turned off, or a desktop browser with Windows Hello. On two Apple devices on one Apple ID with iCloud Keychain on, the passkey and its PRF secret should sync and the button may work (see Unresolved); the single-slot overwrite below holds in every case.
- **Related.** Not a Phase 2 duplicate: no P2 ID covers F260's WebAuthn unlock. OK-F260-2 records that the backup drops this wrap; the live vault row does not.

**What happens now.** `enableBio()` creates a platform credential (`authenticatorAttachment: 'platform'`, `apps/f260.html:1076`) and stores its wrap of the data key as `blob.bio`, one slot inside the vault row (`apps/f260.html:1083`), which syncs through `hub.set` (`apps/f260.html:902`). `bioEnabled()` reads that synced row (`apps/f260.html:1060`), so every device of the person shows "Use Face ID" in the Unlock dialog (`apps/f260.html:1141`), and Settings says "On. The Unlock dialog offers Face ID / Touch ID" (`apps/f260.html:1786`) with Enable disabled, including devices that do not hold the credential. Tapping the button there fails with "Cancelled or not allowed — use your passcode." To set Face ID up on the second device, the person must first tap "Turn off", which deletes the wrap for every device (`apps/f260.html:1091`); Enable then replaces the first device's wrap, and the first device's Face ID fails the same way. The code itself treats the wrap as device-bound: `backupText` strips it with the comment "the biometric wrap is bound to this device" (`apps/f260.html:1097`), and the hint promises an option "on this device" (`apps/f260.html:1787`).

**Expected.** Keep the biometric wrap per device, keyed by credential id (for example `bio: {<credId>: {...}}`) or in device-local storage. Show "Use Face ID" only where this device's credential exists, and let one device's Enable or Turn off leave the others alone.

**Why it matters to the household.** The Unlock dialog offers a button that fails on every device but one, Settings says "On." where it is not, and setting up the second device silently breaks the first.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:902, 1060, 1071-1091, 1097, 1141, 1784-1788`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-faceid.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-faceid-wrap-synced-single-slot-2-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-faceid-wrap-synced-single-slot-2-2.json`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/critic-faceid.mjs"`. Chromium, with one CDP WebAuthn virtual authenticator per device (ctap2, internal transport, PRF, user verification), typical seed, Eli on the Kitchen iPad and a new phone device, host localhost, throwaway passcode 2468. The iPad sets a passcode, enables Face ID in Settings, locks and taps "Use Face ID" (the control: it unlocks). The phone's Settings shows "On."; the phone locks, taps HEAR, then "Use Face ID". The phone unlocks with the passcode, taps Turn off, then Enable; the iPad locks and taps "Use Face ID". Observed: `padAfterEnable {hint:'On. The Unlock dialog offers Face ID…'}`; `padFaceIdControl {faceIdButtonShown:true, after:{dialogOn:false}}`; `phoneLockedSetting {hint:'On. …'}`; `phoneFaceIdFromIpadWrap {faceIdButtonShown:true, after:{dialogOn:true, err:'Cancelled or not allowed — use your passcode.'}}`; `serverBio2 {sameAsIpad:false}`; `padFaceIdAfterPhoneEnabled {after:{dialogOn:true, err:'Cancelled or not allowed — use your passcode.'}}`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-faceid-wrap-synced-single-slot-2-1.mjs"` (fresh instance, Chromium, a virtual platform authenticator with PRF per device, passcode 1357), which also reads each authenticator's credentials and the server vault row. The iPad's wrap `c3EC1v…` matched the iPad authenticator's only credential; the phone's authenticator held none. On the iPad Face ID unlocked; on the phone Settings read "On." with Enable disabled, and Face ID failed with "Cancelled or not allowed — use your passcode." The phone's Turn off set the server wrap to null; its Enable wrote `uyerGc…`, after which the iPad's Face ID failed the same way while its passcode still worked.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-faceid-wrap-synced-single-slot-2-2.mjs"` (fresh instance, Chromium, passcode throwaway). It reproduced every step: the iPad's wrap `4QO36BxNY4bj50K8`, the phone's 0 credentials and failed Face ID, Turn off → `serverBioId null`, Enable → `YRElDzipD+IFaYVh` (`replacedIpadWrap true`), then the iPad's Face ID failing. An extra step copied the iPad's credential into the phone's authenticator to model a synced passkey; it failed with "This device did not return the key material (PRF) needed", a rig limit, because CDP cannot export the hmac-secret.

**Corrected claim.** Confirmed, with its scope narrowed by both skeptics. `authenticatorAttachment: 'platform'` does not by itself make the credential device-bound on Apple hardware: with `residentKey: 'preferred'`, iOS and iPadOS create an iCloud Keychain passkey whose PRF secret may sync to the person's other devices on the same Apple ID, where the single wrap would likely work. The failing button therefore shows when the devices do not share a passkey store (different Apple IDs, iCloud Keychain off, or a non-Apple browser). In every case there is one synced `blob.bio` slot, so one device's Enable or Turn off replaces or deletes the wrap for all of them.

title: The Erase and Restore confirms say "this device", but both act on every device (from the critic; was half of UX-F260-1)
block:
#### P3-F260-15 — The Erase and Restore confirms say "this device", but both act on every device (from the critic; was half of UX-F260-1)

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: medium / medium; the critic filed medium). Not critical under rule (a): the loss follows an explicit confirm titled "Erase the whole journal?" that says "can't be undone", so it is not silent. The defect is that consent to a destructive action is asked with a false statement of its scope, so the journal is also lost on devices the person meant to keep it on. That is a misleading secondary flow.
- **Exposure.** Any adult or guest with F260 on more than one device who uses Erase or Restore; the likeliest case is clearing a journal off the shared Kitchen iPad while meaning to keep it on the phone. In the forgotten-passcode case the copy points to (`apps/f260.html:1136`), the other copy shares the same passcode wrap and could not be read anyway, except where Face ID is enabled on the other device (P3-F260-14), which Erase also wipes.
- **Related.** Re-filed from UX-F260-1, which keeps the footer, Restore-sheet and empty-state wording; P3-F260-12 is the unlock sentence. None is counted twice. P3-F260-13 is what happens when another device is still unlocked at the moment of the Erase. Not a Phase 2 duplicate.

**What happens now.** The Erase confirm reads "Every HEAR entry and the passcode will be deleted from this device. Reading progress stays. This can't be undone" (`apps/f260.html:1769`). `eraseJournal()` drops the vault row (`apps/f260.html:1056`) through `hub.remove` (`apps/f260.html:903`); the key is not in F260's local-only list (`apps/f260.html:897`), so the tombstone syncs, the server vault becomes null, and every other device shows "No passcode yet". Restore's confirm says "The journal and reading progress currently on this device will be replaced" (`apps/f260.html:2022`), and `restoreBackup` replaces the synced vault and every progress row through the same `save`/`drop` (`apps/f260.html:1108-1121`). Erase is also the only remedy the app offers for a forgotten passcode (`apps/f260.html:1136`).

**Expected.** The confirms say the journal (or, for Restore, the journal and progress) is erased or replaced on all of the person's devices. Acting on one device only is not possible under the sync model.

**Why it matters to the household.** Someone clearing the shared iPad, or giving up on a forgotten passcode "on this device", loses the journal everywhere, having been told otherwise at the moment of consent.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:897, 902-903, 1056, 1108-1121, 1136, 1769, 2020-2023`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/journal.json` (`eraseDialog`, `eraseServer`, `phoneAfterErase`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-1-erase-dialog-ipad.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-1-phone-after-erase.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-2-phone-after-erase.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/journal.mjs"`. Its Erase section erases on the iPad, then reads the server row and the phone's `#vaultHint`: `eraseDialog` contains "from this device", `eraseServer {"vaultValue":null}`, and `phoneAfterErase` reads "No passcode yet…".

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-1.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit). Eli set a throwaway passcode on a second phone and wrote an Apply line (`serverAfterPhoneWrite {keys:[v,pass,iv,ct]}`); the Kitchen iPad, as Eli, read "Journal is locked…", opened Settings → Erase journal and saw the dialog above; `serverAfterErase {value:null}`; after 3 s the phone's hint read "No passcode yet — you'll be asked to set one the first time you open a HEAR panel.", and its HEAR opened "Set a journal passcode". The Restore confirm was read from code (`apps/f260.html:2022` against `apps/f260.html:1110-1121`).
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-erase-dialog-misstates-scope-7-2.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit; the first attempt crashed on a stale frame after a reload, the rerun completed). Same dialog and `serverAfterErase {value:null}`; the reopened phone read "No passcode yet…", held no ciphertext in its cache and opened "Set a journal passcode". The phone also showed the footer "saved on this device" and the set-passcode text "It never leaves this device".

**Corrected claim.** Accurate, with two refinements. An open phone picks the erase up on its next pull only while its journal is locked; an unlocked phone keeps showing the journal (it still read "Journal is unlocked" after 71 s) until it locks or F260 is reopened, because merges are deferred (`apps/f260.html:2089`), which is the window P3-F260-13 exploits. The critic's "2 s later" holds for a locked phone only.

title: Reset's confirm does not say it also deletes the Verses review schedule (`f260.recall`) (from the critic; was half of UX-F260-2)
block:
#### P3-F260-16 — Reset's confirm does not say it also deletes the Verses review schedule (`f260.recall`) (from the critic; was half of UX-F260-2)

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: low / medium; the critic filed medium). The split was settled by the tie rule ("How to read this"). The medium clause, "a secondary flow broken or misleading", fits the corrected claim: Reset's confirmation, the one place consent is asked, leaves out the loss of every verse's review schedule in another app. It is not the low clause's "edge case": restarting the plan for a new year is what Reset is for, and every verse the reader marks again then starts over in box 1. Not critical under rule (a): the person asks for a reset and the dialog does name "memorized verse".
- **Exposure.** An adult who has trained verses in Verses and later resets F260, most plausibly to restart the plan in a new year.
- **Related.** Re-filed from UX-F260-2, which keeps the "cannot be undone" part. P3-F260-01 is the other way F260 loses these Leitner fields. Not a Phase 2 duplicate.

**What happens now.** Reset tombstones `f260.done`, `mem`, `log`, `weekStart`, `weekDone`, `best`, `miles`, `recall` and `finished` (`apps/f260.html:1765-1766`). `f260.recall` is F260's own practice key, and Verses keeps each verse's Leitner `box`, `due`, `last` and `streak` in the same rows (`apps/verses.html:155-169, 292-298`). The confirm lists "Every checkmark, memorized verse, milestone, week date and the reading streak" and "Your HEAR journal entries stay" (`apps/f260.html:1764`); it never mentions Verses, review or boxes. After Reset, Verses shows "Nothing to train yet" with boxes `[0,0,0,0,0]`; that part comes from the disclosed clearing of the memorised verses, because Verses trains only the ids in `f260.mem` for adults (`apps/verses.html:221-223`). The undisclosed loss shows when a verse is marked memorised again: it starts in box 1, due today, whatever box it had reached.

**Expected.** Either Reset keeps each recall row's `box`, `due`, `last` and `streak`, or the dialog names the loss ("…and your Verses review boxes"), ideally with the undo proposed in Improvements.

**Why it matters to the household.** Months of spaced-repetition progress on each verse are deleted without being mentioned at the moment of consent, and a well-learned verse comes back as a daily review.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:1098, 1119-1121, 1763-1767`; `apps/verses.html:155-169, 218-223, 292-298`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/recall.json` (`resetDialog`, `reset`, `versesAfterReset`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/screens/f260/reset-confirm-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-1-dialog-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-1-verses-after-rememorise-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-2-verses-after-remark-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/recall.mjs"`. Its reset step records the dialog text (no mention of Verses), the server rows before (`recall 65`) and after (deleted), and Verses afterwards ("Nothing to train yet", boxes `[0,0,0,0,0]`).

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-1.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit iPhone PWA, Eli). The seed has 64 recall rows in boxes `{1:2, 2:2, 3:6, 4:14, 5:40}`; the probe 1-0 was `{box:5, due:'2026-10-02', last:'2026-09-18', streak:4}`. The dialog text has no mention of Verses (`dialogMentionsVerses false`). After Reset, `recall`, `mem` and `done` were null and `verses` (7 texts) was kept; Verses showed "Nothing to train yet", boxes `[0,0,0,0,0]`, its own 13-day streak kept. After 1-0 was marked memorised again in F260, Verses showed boxes `[1,0,0,0,0]`, 1 due today. Rated low.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-reset-silently-wipes-verses-schedule-8-2.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit iPhone PWA, Eli; three memorised verses seeded at boxes 5, 4 and 3). Before: rows `{recall:66, mem:66}`, Verses boxes `[2,1,7,15,41]`; 36-0 at `{box:5, due:'2026-10-03', streak:6}`. After Reset through the UI: `recall` and `mem` null; Verses "Nothing to train yet". After the same three verses were marked memorised again: Verses `{due:3, boxes:[3,0,0,0,0]}`, "WEEK 36 · VERSE 1 · 2 MORE AFTER THIS". Rated medium.

**Corrected claim.** Narrower than filed. Clearing `f260.recall` is deliberate (it is in the drop list, and the row is F260's own key that Verses extends), and Verses' empty screen after Reset comes from the disclosed clearing of the memorised verses. The defect is the dialog: it omits that each verse's review box, due date, last review and streak are deleted, so a verse marked memorised again restarts at box 1, due today (box 5 → box 1 in both runs). Verses' own ratings log and day streak survive, and a backup made beforehand restores `recall` (`apps/f260.html:1098, 1119-1121`). The seed has 64 recall rows; the investigator's run recorded 65.

title: Tapping into an old HEAR entry or week note and away, without typing, re-dates it to today and adds a journal-streak day (from the critic)
block:
#### P3-F260-17 — Tapping into an old HEAR entry or week note and away, without typing, re-dates it to today and adds a journal-streak day (from the critic)

- **Severity: medium** (skeptics: medium / medium; the critic filed medium). No entry text is lost or changed, so it is not rule (a). The entry's date stamp (shown as "Saved <date>", shown on its Journal card and used to sort "Newest first") and the journal streak become false: a secondary flow, the journal's history, misleads.
- **Exposure.** Any unlocked entry on any device: an adult rereads an older entry and taps into a field to scroll or select text (on an iPhone that raises the keyboard), or moves from one field to the next.
- **Related.** Not a Phase 2 duplicate. P2-SYNC-19 and P2-SYNC-20 are related only because each no-op focusout also re-encrypts and uploads the whole vault.

**What happens now.** The focusout handler saves whenever a HEAR field or week note loses focus, without checking whether its value changed (`apps/f260.html:1864-1868`). `saveJournal` stamps `j.t = Date.now()` whenever the entry has any text (`apps/f260.html:1828`) and re-encrypts and uploads the vault (`apps/f260.html:1829`); `bumpJournalStats` then marks today as a journal day (`apps/f260.html:1818`). `saveNote` does the same for week notes (`apps/f260.html:1842`). An entry written on Tue 22 Sep and only focused on Thu 24 Sep changed from "Saved Sep 22, 2026" to "Saved Sep 24, 2026"; its Journal card reads "Sep 24, 2026", `jstats.days` gained 2026-09-24, and the Journal tab shows a "2-day journal streak" with nothing written on the 24th.

**Expected.** Save only when a field's value differs from the stored entry, and keep the date of an unchanged entry; count a journal day only when something was written.

**Why it matters to the household.** The date is the record of when a reflection was written. It is silently overwritten, "Newest first" reorders by the false date, and the journal streak counts days with no writing.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:1814-1848, 1864-1868, 1939-1945`.
- Runs: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-dates.json` (`A`), `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-1.json`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-2.json`.
- Screenshots: `audits/evidence/p3/f260/critic-dates-A-redated-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-1-journal-iphone.png`, `audits/evidence/p3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-2-journal-iphone.png`.

**Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/critic-dates.mjs" A`. WebKit iPhone PWA, Eli, a browser clock installed at the demo instant, throwaway passcode 2468: write Apply on 38-0, set auto-lock to Never, fast-forward 48 h, click `#jf-38-0-a` then `#jf-38-0-h` without typing, and read `.jsaved`, the Journal card date and `hub.get('f260.jstats').days`. Observed: `written {saved:'Saved Sep 22, 2026', jstatsDays:['2026-09-22']}`; `after {saved:'Saved Sep 24, 2026', a:'Share a meal with a neighbour.', jstatsDays:['2026-09-22','2026-09-24']}`; `journalCard 'Week 38 · Day 1Acts 2-3 Sep 24, 2026'`; `journalStat '1 entry · in plan order ✎ 2-day journal streak'`.

**Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
- **Skeptic 1** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-1.mjs"` on the normal path instead of a vault left open for 48 h: write on Tue, close the app, open a new context on Thu 24 Sep 08:40, unlock with the passcode. A control step (open and close the panel without touching a field) changed nothing. Tapping Apply, then Hear, then the Plan tab gave "Saved Sep 24, 2026" with the text unchanged, `jdays ['2026-09-22','2026-09-24']`, a new vault iv (`NKGSTPAibRIk14Hu` → `Itn3z70d3mdSn3g3`), the card "Sep 24, 2026", "2-day journal streak", and the same days on the server.
- **Skeptic 2** ran `node "audits/tools/phase3/f260/verify-critic-hear-focus-redates-entry-3-2.mjs"` (fresh instance, WebKit iPhone PWA, passcode 1357, auto-lock unchanged): write on Tue, fast-forward 48 h, reload, unlock. The control reading with the panel open left the date, days and ciphertext unchanged; tapping into Apply and Hear and then the Journal tab re-dated the entry to Sep 24, rewrote the ciphertext (`9MBaTQBWa9…` → `KOSFWznuyhmMGS0y`) and added 2026-09-24 to the server's `f260.jstats`.

**Corrected claim.** Confirmed for HEAR day entries and week notes, on the normal path (reopen, unlock, tap a field, tap away), not only with auto-lock set to Never. Follow-ups are removed from the claim: their focusout (`apps/f260.html:1468`) restamps only the hidden `ft` field (`apps/f260.html:1451`), which nothing displays, and adds no journal day; it only uploads the vault again.

title: A week read ahead on the plan list and started later reads "done in -1 days" and "started" after it was finished (from the critic)
block:
#### P3-F260-18 — A week read ahead on the plan list and started later reads "done in -1 days" and "started" after it was finished (from the critic)

- **Severity: low** (skeptics: low / low; the critic filed low). Cosmetic: a nonsense duration in one week's summary and its copied text, and a start date later than the finish. No data is lost and the daily flow works.
- **Exposure.** A reader who ticks a later week's readings on the plan list (for example over a weekend) and starts that week on a later day. Reading ahead through the Today card does not trigger it, because Done calls `setCurrent` first (`apps/f260.html:1592`).
- **Related.** Not a Phase 2 duplicate: P2-SYNC-05 and P2-SYNC-17 are first-pull overwrites of `weekStart`. P3-F260-19 is the other way a week gets a false start date.

**What happens now.** Ticking all five readings of a later week on the plan list sets `weekDone[w]` to today (`apps/f260.html:1670`) but never sets `weekStart[w]`. When the person later starts that week, `setCurrent` stamps `weekStart[w]` with that later day (`apps/f260.html:1686`). `summaryText` then computes `daysBetween(start, done) + 1`, which is -1 for a two-day gap and truthy, so it prints "done in -1 days" (`apps/f260.html:1327-1329`); "Copy summary" copies the same text (`apps/f260.html:1335`). The week header (`apps/f260.html:1354`) and the hero meta (`apps/f260.html:1529`) read "started Sep 24" for a week finished on Sep 22. A longer gap gives a larger negative.

**Expected.** A week's start is never later than its finish: set `weekStart` when the first reading of a week is ticked, or clamp the duration to at least 1 day.

**Why it matters to the household.** A visible nonsense figure in the week summary and in the text a reader copies to share, and a false start date in the header.

**Evidence.**
- Code: `apps/f260.html:1327-1329, 1335, 1354, 1529, 1592, 1657-1674, 1684-1689`.
