title: Only `--accent-deep` has an "on" colour; every other filled surface picks white or `--on-accent` by hand (medium)
block:
#### GAP-TOK-2 — Only `--accent-deep` has an "on" colour; every other filled surface picks white or `--on-accent` by hand (medium)

- **Areas:** design.css, the shell, F260, Verses, the park map.
- **What happens.** `--on-accent` is the only "on" token (apps/design.css:92), and it is tuned for `--accent-deep`. Everything else is hand-picked:
  - **The badge.** `.ds .badge` paints `#fff` on `var(--danger)` (:515-516). But `--danger` (= `--terra`) is re-tuned light in the dark palettes. So the Larder "N to eat this week" badge on the Apps grid (index.html:703; 12 px bold) is 4.51 in Hearth, 5.66 Parchment and 4.94 Frost, but **2.61 in Midnight, 2.55 in Forest and 2.61 for Hearth on a dark OS**.
  - **The switch knob** is `#fff` on `--ok`: 1.97-2.02 in dark (P4-TOK-02).
  - **F260** defines `--on-solid: white` (apps/f260.html:26). It uses it on `--olive` for the daily Done (:144; 4.50 in Hearth, exactly at the edge) and on `--terra` (:392).
  - **Verses** pairs `--on-accent` with `--olive` for "Got it" (apps/verses.html:59; 4.40, VIS-VERSES-3).
  - **The park map** puts white on its wait tiles (apps/dollywood-live.html:500-501).
  - **Across the light palettes**, `--on-accent` on the hue mid-tones is: gold 3.22 / 4.27 / 3.96, terra 4.41, olive 4.40, teal 4.74.
- **Expected.** Each fill token has a paired, theme-tuned "on" token that passes 4.5:1 in every palette, and no component hardcodes `#fff`.
- **Why it matters.** The badge is the Apps grid's at-a-glance cue, on the Larder tile, that food must be eaten. In the dark palettes, and in System at night, a household member cannot read it. This meets the rule's "text a household member needs … on a primary surface": at least medium.
- **Evidence:** `token-pairs.json` pairs "#fff on --danger", "#fff knob vs --ok track" and "on-accent on --olive/--gold/--terra/--teal"; apps/design.css:459-460, 515-516; apps/f260.html:26, 144, 392; apps/verses.html:59; index.html:703.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/pairs.mjs`.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - Phase 2's unnumbered VIS item "The accent and tile icons are not lifted for dark" (medium; `audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`) recorded the badge at 2.61. New here: Forest 2.55, Hearth on a dark OS, and the missing token as the root cause.
  - VIS-VERSES-3.

section: What design.css defines versus what the apps use (TOK)
title: Profile and app colours are single light-theme hex values that never re-tune; as foregrounds in Midnight and Forest, 17 of 19 fall under 3:1 (medium)
block:
#### GAP-TOK-3 — Profile and app colours are single light-theme hex values that never re-tune; as foregrounds in Midnight and Forest, 17 of 19 fall under 3:1 (medium)

- **Areas:** the shell, design.css, hub.js, the park map, the build guide.
- **What happens.** design.css re-tunes every hue family per palette (for example `--olive` #5B8143 → #9DC183 in Midnight). The person and app colours, though, are each one hex, stored in:
  - the profile row (worker/seed.sql:4-11);
  - the 10 guest swatches (`SWATCHES`, index.html:449);
  - the 9 apps.json tile colours;
  - the fallbacks `#8A6A4B` (apps/hub.js:461; index.html:450; ×9 in the park map's JS).

  hub.js writes the colour inline as `--accent` (apps/hub.js:80).

  As a foreground (tile glyph, ring, avatar ring, timer ring) it sinks in the dark palettes (Table TOK-J):
  - glyph on its own tile under 3:1 for 17/19 in Midnight and Forest, 8 of 9 app tiles;
  - ring on `--surface` under 3:1 for 7/19 (Eli 2.57, David 2.14, TV 1.95).

  9 of the 19 entries use one of 7 hex values that are not design.css values at all.
- **Expected.** Profiles and apps reference a hue family or a person-palette token whose fill, ink and foreground values are defined per theme. The accent then lifts in the dark palettes the way the hue tokens do.
- **Why it matters.** Pre-readers find apps by icon and colour, and System goes dark every night. The TV and the dark palettes lose the per-person colour cue.
- **Evidence:** `appcolours.json`, `tokens-resolved.json` (the default `--accent` is the theme's `--mocha`; a profile's accent is fixed), apps/hub.js:80, 461; index.html:449-450; `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/tokens.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/appcolours.mjs`.
- **Re-measure.** The counts agree exactly. They use the tile gradient's 22 % stop, its worst case (apps/design.css:607). At the 15 % mid-tone the counts are 13/19 in Midnight and Forest and 3/19 in Parchment.
- **Related (not re-filed):** the Phase 2 unnumbered VIS item (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`), which covers the rings and 6 of 9 tile icons at 1.95-2.93.
  - New here: all 19 colours × 5 palettes, including Forest; 8 of 9 tiles at token level; the 7 hex values (9 of 19 entries) outside design.css; and the data-model root cause (a hex per person and per app).

section: What design.css defines versus what the apps use (TOK)
title: There are no weight, z-index, opacity, breakpoint, press-scale, fluid-type or composite-glass tokens, so each area invents its own (medium)
block:
#### GAP-TOK-5 — There are no weight, z-index, opacity, breakpoint, press-scale, fluid-type or composite-glass tokens, so each area invents its own (medium)

- **Areas:** all 11.
- **What each area invents** (Table TOK-F):
  - **Weights:** literal weights in all 11 areas: design.css 20 (600 ×10, 700 ×7, 400 ×3), shell 26, F260 87 (800 ×16), Prayer 52, park map 40, Kid Verse 16.
  - **z-index:** nine unrelated ladders, from design.css 1/20/50/60 to Prayer 10-40.
  - **Breakpoints:** **16 distinct values**, or 18 counting min/max direction; none is shared by every area.
  - **Fluid display sizes:** one-off `clamp()`s (shell ×6, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse, Verses); nothing beyond `--fs-hero`.
  - **Press scales:** .86 to 1.06 across areas.
  - **Glass filter:** `saturate(1.4)` is retyped 25 times outside design.css (F260 6, Tally 6, Larder 2, Prayer 2, the Dollywood template 9).
  - **Glass shadow:** its five-part box-shadow is restated in the shell (index.html:261), Timer (:36), Prayer (:283-300), the Larder (:32-45) and Tally ×3.
  - Only the Dollywood template has composite glass tokens (`--lv-glass*`, apps/dollywood.html:215).
- **Expected.** design.css defines weight, layer, opacity, breakpoint, press and fluid display scales plus composite glass tokens, and the areas reference them.
- **Why it matters.** Without shared layers, overlays from different areas can collide; without shared weights, hierarchy drifts from app to app. Hand-copied glass diverges from the recipe the moment the recipe changes.
- **Evidence:** `literals-summary.json`, `literals-<area>.json` (fontWeight, zIndex, glassFilter hits with lines), `tokens-inventory.json` → `byCategory`, `remeasure.json` → `breakpoints`, `saturate14`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/literals.mjs`.
- **Corrected** from the investigator's "21 distinct breakpoints". Its own list and its own `literals-summary.json` give 16 values (18 with direction); no reading gives 21.

section: What design.css defines versus what the apps use (TOK)
title: design.css cannot scope the accent to one component, because the derived accent tokens resolve once on `:root` (low)
block:
#### GAP-TOK-6 — design.css cannot scope the accent to one component, because the derived accent tokens resolve once on `:root` (low)

- **Areas:** design.css, Kid Verse, Prayer, Verses.
- **What happens.** `--accent-soft/-tint/-deep/-glow`, `--glow-accent` and `--focus` are declared on `:root` (apps/design.css:86-102) and inherit as computed values. A component that sets `--accent` therefore has to restate each derived token by hand. Three areas tried:

| Area | Derived tokens restated | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Kid Verse | none | The Done ★ paints Ezra's teal: local `--accent` rgb(180,134,27), fill rgb(14,91,86) (P3-KIDVERSE-14) |
| Prayer | one of three (`--accent-soft`) | On the Family list the nav text is slate-deep rgb(57,67,101) on teal-soft rgb(220,236,234), while Pray now and + stay slate (VIS-PRAYER-4) |
| Verses | three (apps/verses.html:56-58) | Correct, but its `.btn-primary` glow and focus ring still use the person's colour |

- **Expected.** A scoping hook: a selector that re-declares the derived tokens, so that setting `--accent` on a component re-derives soft, tint, deep, glow and focus.
- **Why it matters.** Two of the three attempts in the codebase got it wrong, and every future per-component colour will hit the same trap.
- **Evidence:** `accent-repoint.json`, `accent-repoint-kidverse-ezra.png`, `accent-repoint-prayer-eli-family.png`, apps/design.css:86-102, apps/kidverse.html:55, 137, apps/prayer.html:39, apps/verses.html:56-58.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TOK/verify-accent-repoint.mjs`.

title: Build guide map labels render below 11 px at the default whole-park view: section names 6.1 px on the iPhone (5.5 px in Safari), listing numbers 6.8 px on every device, contour heights 9.5 px at every zoom
block:
#### P4-TYPE-01 — Build guide map labels render below 11 px at the default whole-park view: section names 6.1 px on the iPhone (5.5 px in Safari), listing numbers 6.8 px on every device, contour heights 9.5 px at every zoom

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** a measurable text-size failure (below 11 px) on a secondary surface. The text is map annotation, not the main content or a primary action. The design-system clause makes decorative or secondary failures low.
  - **Why not higher:** the same information is elsewhere. Section names are on the chips above the map, listing numbers are in the Listings tab and the marker pop-ups, and pinch or + zoom brings section names to 15 px.
  - **Exposure:** everyone who opens the build guide sees the whole-park view first. The iPhone is worst (section names 6.14 px in the PWA, 5.51 px in Safari); on the iPad portrait they are 10.23 px. Listing numbers are 6.82 px on all five devices. The build guide is adult-only.
- **Areas:** dollywood (build guide). The park map ships the same code. Its measured screens showed none of these three groups, because the illustrated basemap hides `#seclabels` and `#contour` (`apps/dollywood-live.html:526`); see Unresolved 1.
- **What happens.**
  - **The cause** is the template's `apply()`, which runs after every pan and zoom (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:799-802`, exported to `apps/dollywood.html:802-805`). `k` is metres per CSS px (`mpp()`, `template.html:788`), so the map's own drawing scale is 1/k.
  - **Listing markers** are scaled by `ms = k × (k > 0.75 ? 0.62 : k > 0.45 ? 0.8 : 1)` (`template.html:800`). Their 11 px numbers (`[data-flavor=hub] .mk .onum`, `apps/dollywood.html:281`) therefore draw at 11 × 0.62 = 6.82 px. Only at k ≤ 0.45, zoomed far in, do they reach 11 px.
  - **Contour heights** are set to `9.5 × k` user units (`template.html:801`), which draws at a constant 9.5 px at every zoom.
  - **Section names** are set to `15 × min(k, 1.1)` user units (`template.html:802`). Once zoomed in they draw at 15 px. At the whole-park view k is above 1.1, so they draw at 16.5/k px: 6.14 px on the iPhone PWA (CTM 0.3723), 5.51 px in iPhone Safari (0.3341) and 10.23 px on the iPad portrait (0.6199).
  - **In the screenshot,** "WILDWOOD GROVE", "ENTRANCE & PLAZA" and the haloed marker numbers are small, faint text on the whole-park map (`audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1-iphone-pwa.png`).
  - **Why it went unrecorded:** the rig's type inventory records HTML text only, so none of these labels is in `type.json`. P3 recorded only the cross-section axis labels (VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4).
- **Expected.** House style: never below 11 px. Map labels should keep a constant on-screen size at or above 11 px, as the park map's family labels already do with `${11*k}` (`template.html:1339, 1349`; they measure 11.0 px at every zoom), or be hidden below a zoom threshold instead of shrinking.
- **Why it matters.** On a phone the section names and listing numbers are how the map is read, and at 5.5-6.8 px they cannot be read.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/hidden-text.json`. Build guide map, iPhone PWA: `text.seclab` 6.14 (9 labels), `text.onum` 6.82 (44), `text.clab` 9.5 (22). iPad portrait: 10.23, 6.82, 9.5. Cross-section: `svg#prof > text` 4.46 on the iPhone PWA, 9.1 on the iPad.
  - Skeptics: `verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1.json` and `-1-iphone-pwa.png`, `verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-2.json` (all in `audits/evidence/p4/TYPE/`).
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-live-guide-svg.json` (text box height against an HTML reference span: 0.93-1.08).
  - Code: `apps/dollywood.html:111, 131, 133, 277, 281, 802-805, 936`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:788, 799-802` (read-only).
  - Phase 1 captures: `audits/screens/dollywood/map-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`, `audits/screens/dollywood/cross-section-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub" && node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/hidden-text.mjs --only dollywood`. The console shows `map iphone-pwa svg min eff 6.14`. Per-label detail is in `hidden-text.json` `runs[].docs[frame].svg`: `text.seclab` 6.14, `text.onum` 6.82, `text.clab` 9.5.
  - Skeptics: `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/verify-build-guide-svg-labels-under-11-1.mjs` (five devices) and `… -2.mjs` (four + taps and a section chip).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote their own WebKit probe (local instance, typical household, Eli, System light), reusing only the navigation from `audits/tools/areas/dollywood.mjs`. For every visible SVG `<text>` it took the computed font size × √|det(getScreenCTM())|, the glyph box height and the app's own `window.MK` and `window.MS`, on five devices.
    - Section names: 6.14 px on the iPhone PWA, **5.51 on iPhone Safari**, 10.23 on the iPad portrait. They pass on the iPad landscape (14.92) and desktop (13.15).
    - Listing numbers: 6.82 px on all five devices. Contour heights: 9.5 on all five.
    - Axis labels: 4.46 px on both iPhones, glyph box 5.7; 9.1 on the iPad portrait, 13.42 on the iPad landscape, 11.78 on desktop.
    - Zoomed to a section: section names 15 px everywhere; listing numbers 8.8 px on phones and 11 px on the iPad and desktop.
    - Every value matches `apply()`. A grep of `audits/*.md` and `audits/03-apps/*.md` found no earlier record of the map's section, marker or contour labels.
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the label CSS and `template.html:788, 800-802`, then wrote their own WebKit script (iPhone PWA and iPad portrait, Eli, System light). It measured six states: the default view, each of four + taps, and a section chip.
    - iPhone. Default (MK 2.686): 6.14 / 6.82 / 9.5. After one tap (MK 1.79): section names 9.21. Two taps: 13.82. Three taps: 15. Four taps (MK 0.53): listing numbers 8.8. Section chip (MK 0.59): 15 / 8.8 / 9.5.
    - iPad. Default (MK 1.61): 10.23 / 6.82 / 9.5. One tap: section names 15. Two taps: listing numbers 8.8. Four taps (MK 0.32) and the section chip: listing numbers 11.
    - They confirmed it is not a rig artefact: the size arithmetic does not depend on which face loads.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** `.seclab` 16.5 × 0.3723 = 6.14 (iPhone) and 16.5 × 0.6199 = 10.23 (iPad); `.onum` 11 × 0.62 = 6.82 on both; `.clab` 9.5 on both; axis 12 × 0.372 = 4.46 (iPhone PWA) and 12 × 0.758 = 9.1 (iPad). Agrees.
- **Corrected claim.** Accurate at the default whole-park view, with four refinements:
  - It is worse in iPhone Safari (430×740): section names are 5.51 px there.
  - "Everywhere" overstates it. Section names reach 15 px once zoomed in: one + tap on the iPad, three on the iPhone. Listing numbers step from 6.82 to 8.8 to 11 px, and reach 11 only at k ≤ 0.45. A section chip on the iPhone still leaves them at 8.8 px.
  - Contour heights are a deliberate constant (9.5 × k): a floor violation by design, not a scaling slip.
  - The axis-label facet (4.46 px) is VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4 and is not re-filed. It adds only a reconciliation: 4.46 px is the font size, and P3's 5.7 px is the glyph box height.
  - The fix belongs in the sibling template's `apply()` (the 0.62 / 0.8 marker factors, the `min(k, 1.1)` cap, the 9.5 base), then a rebuild and export. `apps/dollywood.html` is generated.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-DOLLYWOOD-3 (the toolbar's 10.5 px caps and the off-scale sizes), VIS-DOLLYWOOD-4 (the axis labels).

title: No iPad type tier: body, secondary, button and tab text is the same size on the 820 px iPad as on the 430 px iPhone, in every area (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### GAP-TYPE-1 — No iPad type tier: body, secondary, button and tab text is the same size on the 820 px iPad as on the 430 px iPhone, in every area (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens.**

title: No text-size preference and no Dynamic Type hook; F260's page zoom is the only control, and it leaves its 9.5 px label at 10.92 px (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### GAP-TYPE-2 — No text-size preference and no Dynamic Type hook; F260's page zoom is the only control, and it leaves its 9.5 px label at 10.92 px (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens.**
  - Every size is a px literal or a px token, and `html` sets `text-size-adjust: 100%` (`apps/design.css:293`).
  - NOT FOUND IN CODE, in `index.html`, `apps/*.html`, `apps/design.css` and the template: `font: -apple-system-body` or any `-apple-system-*` text style, `rem`-based font sizes (F260 and Prayer use `rem` only for max-widths, `apps/f260.html:44`, `apps/prayer.html:50`), or a hub text-size preference. As far as the code shows, iOS Larger Text never reaches the hub; this was not tested on a device.
  - F260 alone offers Large text, as `body.big { zoom: 1.15 }` (`apps/f260.html:50, 2034`; person scope `f260.big`). It zooms the layout as well as the text:
    - 17 → 19.6 px and 25 → 28.8 px;
    - the WEEK ring label 9.5 → 10.92 px, still under 11 (the re-measure read it from the rendered box: 28.11 × 9.5 → 32.33 × 10.92, a ratio of 1.150);
    - on the iPhone it wraps the meta line (VIS-F260-10), and it stops at the F260 frame.
- **Expected.** Grandparents are in the audience, and nothing important may hide behind small type. A person-scope text-size preference, like the theme, should scale the type hub-wide, and ideally follow the OS setting.
- **Why it matters.** A grandparent who needs larger text cannot get it outside F260, and inside F260 some text is still below the floor.
- **Evidence:** `apps/design.css:293`; `apps/f260.html:50, 2034`; `hidden-text.json` (f260 large-text: body zoom 1.15, smallest `span#todayRing > span.rn > small` at 10.92); `remeasure-live-f260-zoom.json`; `code-scan.json` (px or `--fs` tokens only, no `rem`).
- **Reproduction:** `grep -rn "apple-system-body\|-apple-system-headline\|font: *-apple" index.html apps/*.html apps/design.css` (no output); `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/hidden-text.mjs --only f260`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-F260-10 (the wrap). No earlier phase recorded the missing hub-wide setting (a grep of `audits/*.md` for "Larger Text", "text size" and "apple-system-body" finds nothing).

title: TV board: the kiosk block uses its phone-sized steps for information text; names, star counts, times and bylines are 18 px and the date 12 px (investigator rating: medium; extends P2's UX-HOME-2, not re-filed)
block:
#### VIS-TYPE-1 — TV board: the kiosk block uses its phone-sized steps for information text; names, star counts, times and bylines are 18 px and the date 12 px (investigator rating: medium; extends P2's UX-HOME-2, not re-filed)

- **Owner.** Phase 2 already recorded the defect: UX-HOME-2 ("On the TV the board's news is its smallest text", medium, investigator only; `audits/02-shell.md:556-558`) and the VIS note "TV text is below 10-foot sizes" (`:5973-5977`). This item adds measurements and the token-level cause. It is not a second defect.
- **New facts.**
  - Re-measured live in System and Midnight, as eight size tiers (Table TYPE-6). Only the clock, verse refs and greeting are 10-foot sizes.
  - As iPad equivalents at 3 m on a 55-inch set: 18 px reads like 7.9 px on an iPad at 40 cm (9.35 px on a 65-inch), the 26 px feed lines like 11.4 px, the 22 px reminders like 9.7 px, and the 12 px date like 5.3 px.
  - The cause is the kiosk block (`apps/design.css:286-289`). It sets `--fs-sm` to 18, which the board uses for its information text (`index.html:153, 163`), and it does not re-map `--fs-xs` at all (`apps/design.css:417`). On a kiosk viewport 1050 px tall or less, the feed lines shrink further, to 22 px (`index.html:175`).
  - P2's own glance heuristic found that on a 65-inch set everything except the date reaches its bare-threshold test (H2), while on a 55-inch set the date and the 18 px text fail it (`audits/02-shell.md:543, 557`). The severity therefore depends on the set, which is not known (Not verified).
- **Expected (house style).** The kiosk is a 10-foot UI. Its smallest information text should subtend at least what the iPad floor does at arm's length, about 28-32 px at 1080p, and the date and names should never use the 12 and 18 px steps.
- **Why it matters.** The kids look for their stars and the parents look for who prayed, from across the room.
- **Evidence:** `remeasure-live-tv-board.json`; `remeasure-tvmath.json`; `report.mjs tv`; `audits/screens/tv/board-typical-tv-light.png`; `index.html:142-163, 175`; `apps/design.css:286-289, 417`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TYPE/report.mjs tv`.
- **Related:** UX-HOME-2 (owner), P2-VIS-02 (the board's overflow; must be solved by layout, not by smaller type).

- **What happens.**
  - **The pane headings.** The hub flavour remaps `.tabbody h2` to `--font-display` (`apps/dollywood.html:223`). The live flavour remaps only `.pop h2` (`apps/dollywood-live.html:223`). title: Kid mode keeps adult-sized controls wherever a control is sized in fixed px: the Larder (7 selectors at 44-52 px), the park map (every default-view control under 64, four under 44) and the shell's sidebar tab (195×48 on the iPad landscape and desktop)
block:
#### P4-SHAPE-01 — Kid mode keeps adult-sized controls wherever a control is sized in fixed px: the Larder (7 selectors at 44-52 px), the park map (every default-view control under 64, four under 44) and the shell's sidebar tab (195×48 on the iPad landscape and desktop)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a measurable target-size shortfall against the kid-mode goal, where every control still clears the 44 px house minimum except the park-map items, and those are already filed for everyone (VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5). That makes it cosmetic or an edge case, not a broken core flow. It matches P2 PROF's low rating for the same class of defect in the shell.
  - **Not counted here:** a kid's tap on the Larder ✓ removes a family item for everyone. That data risk is owned by P3-LEFTOVERS-13 (critical); the small target does not raise this finding.
  - **Exposure:** Ezra and Kiara, on the apps they can see (CLAUDE.md lists the Larder and the park map for kids). The sidebar tab applies at 1024 px and wider: the iPad landscape and desktop.
- **Areas:** leftovers, dollywood-live, shell.
- **What happens.**
  - **The cause.** For kids, design.css sets `--tap: 64px; --tap-lg: 84px` (`apps/design.css:281`, under the comment "Kids: bigger targets", `:279`). Only rules that read `var(--tap)`, or that carry their own kid rule, change. Anything sized in literal px keeps the adult size.
  - **The Larder** sizes its controls in px: `#name` 52, `select, #date` 44, `.log` 52, `.mic` 52, `.done` 48×48 (`apps/leftovers.html:47, 52-53, 55, 58, 83`). It has no `data-kind="kid"` rule; its only `data-kind` rules are for the kiosk (`:18, :96`). For Ezra every control matches Mae's exactly:
    - ✓ 48×48;
    - `#size` and `#date` 263×44;
    - `#name` 378×52;
    - mic 52×52;
    - Log 88×52;
    - Copy for Hearth 181×52.
    That is 12 of 12 controls under 64 on the iPad portrait and 10 of 10 on the iPhone: 7 distinct selectors.
  - **The park map.** The template has no `data-kind` rule at all. In Ezra's default view:
    - the sheet handle is 820×22 (430×22 on the iPhone);
    - the sheet tabs are 197×46 (100×46 on the iPhone);
    - Find me and Whole park are 54×54, and North 50×50.
    In the Nearby pane, the segment is Nearby 67×32 and Waits 57×32, Set my spot is 96×36, and the Queue-Times.com link is 92×15. That is 12 of 12 under 64, with the handle, the segment, Set my spot and the link under 44.
  - **The shell.** It is a `.ds` area, but its tab rule hardcodes `min-height: 56px` (`apps/design.css:560`), and `min-height: 48px` in the sidebar at 1024 px and wider (`:573`). The kid tab is therefore 104×56 on the iPhone and 140×56 on the iPad portrait, both already recorded by P2, and **195×48 on the iPad landscape and desktop**, which is new. The other kid shell controls measure 64-117 px.
  - **Control group.** Kid Verse (smallest 84), Verses (84), Timer (smallest 64; Start 84), Tally (+ 168, − 116, Reset 64) and Prayer (Prayed 161×64) all clear 64. Prayer keeps its own CSS and still clears it, through its own `.kid .prayed{min-height:64px;min-width:64px}` (`apps/prayer.html:421`). So the dividing line is fixed px against `var(--tap)`, not own CSS against `.ds`.
- **Expected.** House style: "44x44pt minimum tap targets; larger in kid mode." CLAUDE.md promises "bigger targets" in kid mode. Every control a kid can reach should size from `--tap` (64) or `--tap-lg` (84).
- **Why it matters.** The kids are 4-5 years old. The kid scale was built for them, but it stops at the apps that size in px, and on the Larder the smallest kid target is also the one that changes family data.
- **Evidence.**
  - Skeptics: `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.json`, `-1-leftovers-ipad-portrait.png`, `-1-shell-ipad-landscape.png`; `verify-kid-targets-own-css-2.json`, `-2-leftovers.png`, `-2-shell-landscape.png`.
  - Investigator: `verify.json` V4; `analyze.json → areas.leftovers.targets.kid`, `areas['dollywood-live'].targets.kid`, `areas.shell.targets.kid`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure.json → runs.kid` (40 entries).
  - Code: `apps/design.css:279-283, 560, 573`; `apps/leftovers.html:18, 47-58, 83, 96`; `apps/prayer.html:421`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/leftovers/kid-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`, `audits/screens/dollywood-live/kid-family-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From the repo root:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → `verify.json` V4 (profile ezra).
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.mjs` (13 area/device cases, typical seed) or `… -2.mjs` (park seed, Ezra against Mae).
  - The full per-area list: `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/analyze.mjs` → `analyze.json → areas.<area>.targets.kid.list`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran `verify-kid-targets-own-css-1.mjs` (WebKit, typical seed, Ezra, light). It swept every visible interactive element whose centre hit-test lands on it, in 13 area/device cases, and it opened the park map's Nearby and Family panes. It saw:
    - `data-kind=kid` and `--tap` 64px everywhere;
    - the Larder 12 of 12 under 64 (iPad) and 10 of 10 (iPhone), nothing under 44;
    - the park map 7 of 7 on its first screen, plus the segment, Set my spot and the link in Nearby (5 under 44 with the handle);
    - the shell tab 195×48 (iPad landscape, desktop), 140×56 (iPad portrait) and 104×56 (iPhone);
    - Kid Verse, Verses, Timer, Tally and Prayer at 0 under 64.
    It deleted its two park-map PNGs, which were over 1 MB.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran `verify-kid-targets-own-css-2.mjs` (WebKit, park seed). It listed every button, link, input, select and role control for Ezra and for Mae on eight areas and four shell devices, and recorded body `.ds` and the resolved `--tap`. Ezra's Larder and park-map sizes were identical to Mae's (12 of 12 under 64 in each; 5 under 44 on the map). The shell and the control group matched skeptic 1. It confirmed that the template has no `data-kind` rules.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** exact on every size (Larder `.done` 48×48, `#size`/`#date` 263×44, `#name` 378×52, `#mic` 52×52, Log 88×52, Copy 181×52; shell tab 140×56 and 195×48; `#lv-handle` 820×22, tabs 197×46; Kid Verse 338×84; Tally 168 / 116 / 162×64; Timer `#go` 298×84).
- **Corrected claim.** The claim is right in substance, with four corrections:
  - **The cause.** It is fixed-px sizing that skips `var(--tap)`, not "own CSS". Prayer keeps its own CSS and clears 64; the shell is `.ds` and misses it.
  - **Timer.** Its smallest kid control is 64, not 84; 84 is its Start.
  - **The Share toggle and card ×.** The park map's Share toggle (50×30) and card × (36) were not in the default kid view, and no skeptic reproduced them. On a touch device the switch's hit area is its 60 px label row and the × is 44×44 (P4-SHAPE-03), so for a kid both are under 64 but not under 44.
  - **What is new.** The cross-area cause, the 48 px kid sidebar tab, and the Larder's measured kid sizes.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 PROF "kid-mode shell controls are below the 64 px kid size" (`audits/02-shell.md:1084`) owns the 104×56 and 140×56 tab bar and the 44 px viewer top bar.
  - VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5 owns the map's controls under 44 for everyone.
  - UX-LEFTOVERS-2 owns "kids get the full adult page".
  - P3-LEFTOVERS-13 owns the ✓ data loss.
  - Any park-map change belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html`.

title: Prayer's toast action is a 36×22 target: Undo after "Mark answered" and "Open it" after an add, offered for 6 seconds
block:
#### P4-SHAPE-02 — Prayer's toast action is a 36×22 target: Undo after "Mark answered" and "Open it" after an add, offered for 6 seconds

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a measurable target-size failure (under 44×44) on a secondary safety-net action. The button works, and no data is lost if it is missed: the request is in the Record with the note just typed, and "Put back on the list" reopens it. That path erasing the note is P3-PRAYER-04, not re-counted here.
  - **Not raised:** the re-measure noted a case for medium, because this Undo is the only one-tap recovery after "Mark answered". This section keeps the skeptics' low, because it is not the primary action of a daily flow and nothing is lost.
  - **Exposure:** every adult who marks a request answered or adds one.
- **Areas:** prayer.
- **What happens.**
  - The toast is one element for every message (`apps/prayer.html:563`). Its button is styled `.toast button{background:none;border:none;…font-size:14px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;padding:0}` (`:260-261`), with no minimum size.
  - The button's height is the body line height, 1.55 × 14 px = 21.7 px (`:46`), and its width is the word: 36 px for "Undo".
  - `toast()` hides it after 6,000 ms (`:1142-1149`). It carries "Undo" after "Moved to the record." (`:1331`) and "Open it" after "Added to the family list." (`:1319`).
  - The only listener is on `#toastAct` (`:1426`). A tap 8 px above or below the word's centre still lands on the button; at 14 px it lands on the `#toast` div, which does nothing.
  - The toast is 236×49 on the iPad portrait. On the iPhone PWA it is 215×72.5, because the message wraps onto two lines (VIS-SHAPE-4).
  - Undo itself works: the status goes back to active.
  - An aside, not filed separately: the rotation-count chips have `min-height:44px` but no `min-width` (`:187`), and measure about 43×45.
- **Expected.** 44×44 pt minimum everywhere (house style; CLAUDE.md, Adding an app, step 6), and above all on an undo, since the house style prefers undo to a confirm.
- **Why it matters.** A grandparent who marks the wrong request answered has 6 seconds to hit a 22 px word.
- **Evidence.**
  - Skeptics: `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-prayer-undo-target-1.json`, `-1-iphone.png`; `verify-prayer-undo-target-2.json`, `-2.png`.
  - Investigator: `verify.json` V3 `{undo: {w:36, h:22, padding:'0px'}, toast: {h:49}}`; `verify-prayer-undo-toast.png`; `analyze.json → areas.prayer.targets.adult.list` (`button#toastAct` 36×22 on the `themes/prayer/mark-answered-*` jobs).
  - Re-measure: `remeasure.json → runs.undo`; `remeasure-prayer-undo.png` (820×260, 1×).
  - Code: `apps/prayer.html:46, 187, 254-261, 563, 1142-1149, 1319, 1331, 1426`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/prayer/mark-answered-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify-prayer-undo-target-2.mjs`, the real flow: open Prayer as Eli, tap a Today request, Mark answered, fill in the note, Save. It measures `#toastAct`: 36×21.7, padding 0.
  - Or `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V3, which calls the app's own `toast('Moved to the record.','Undo',fn)`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran `verify-prayer-undo-target-1.mjs`: the real UI flow on the iPhone PWA (light and dark) and the iPad portrait (light). It saw:
    - `#toastAct` 36×21.7, padding 0, font 14 px, `min-width`/`min-height` auto;
    - points 6 px outside each edge all hit `#toast`, so there is no extended hit area;
    - the toast 236×49.3 on the iPad and 215×72.5 on the iPhone;
    - rotation chips 42.8-43.9 × 45.1-45.5 in a probe built from the app's `.chip` class.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran `verify-prayer-undo-target-2.mjs`, the same real flow, in WebKit on the iPhone PWA and iPad portrait and in Chromium on the iPhone PWA. It saw:
    - an identical 36×21.7 in all three, with the height equal to the line height, so it does not depend on the engine or the font;
    - a hit at ±8 px and a miss at ±14 px;
    - Undo restoring the request.
    It searched the P2/P3 reports and P3's `layout.json`: no earlier record of the toast target.
  - **Re-measure (independent code):** `#toastAct` 36×21.7, padding 0, no border, radius 0, inside a 236.1×49.3 pill toast at `--e3`. Exact.
- **Corrected claim.** Confirmed as stated, with two refinements:
  - The 49 px toast height is the iPad figure; on the iPhone PWA the toast is 72.5 px, because the message wraps.
  - The rotation chips are about 43×45, not 42×44: a 1 px width miss.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - VIS-PRAYER-3 covers only the category Rename (59×31) and Remove (57×31) and the Pray-mode Close.
  - P3-PRAYER-04 covers "Put back" erasing the note.
  - P3-PRAYER-09 covers Undo doing nothing after a remote change.
  - The shared toast takes no action at all (`hub.toast = (msg, ms = 2200)`, `apps/hub.js:431`), so there is no shared undo toast for Prayer to use.

title: Park map: five control rules under 44 px beyond the five P3 recorded, namely the sheet handle (22), About the data (29), the layer-toggle rows (29), the kids' height stepper (40×40) and the directions-bar buttons (40)
block:
#### P4-SHAPE-03 — Park map: five control rules under 44 px beyond the five P3 recorded, namely the sheet handle (22), About the data (29), the layer-toggle rows (29), the kids' height stepper (40×40) and the directions-bar buttons (40)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** measurable target-size failures on secondary controls of a park-day tool. Every control still works when tapped, and nothing is lost, so this is cosmetic or an edge case. The parent finding VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5 was also ruled low.
  - **Exposure:** anyone using the park map on a park day, one-handed while walking. Everyone, kids included, uses the handle.
- **Areas:** dollywood-live. The build guide, built from the same template, has 27 selectors under 44, which VIS-DOLLYWOOD-2 already owns (35 instances on the phone, 15 on the iPad).
- **What happens.**
  - **The investigator's count.** The rig found 18 interactive selectors under 44 in the park map's own document, 19 with an inline link, measured by element box.
  - **Adjusted for real hit area on a touch device,** the count is 13 selectors, about 8 CSS rules (skeptic 1: 16 by element box, 14 counting label rows, 15 applying `pointer:coarse`, 13 with both).
  - **Already recorded by VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5** (8 of the 18 selectors):
    - Set my spot 95.9×36 (`.lv-row-top button`, `template.html:432`);
    - the meeting bar's Done 58.4×36 and Go 43.2×36 (`.lv-meet button`, `:517`);
    - Nearby 66.9×32 and Waits 56.5×32 (`.lv-seg`, `:522`);
    - the who-chips and filter chips, 72-104 × 34 (`.lv-chips button`, `:503`).
  - **New** (the file's line numbers are `template.html`):
    - **The sheet handle, 430×22 (820×22 on the iPad).** `.lv-handle{height:22px;min-height:22px!important}` (`:424`). The sheet header can be dragged (`apps/dollywood-live.html:1473`), but the handle is the only thing a tap can use to resize the sheet.
    - **About the data, 402×29.4.** `.about summary{…padding:6px 0}`, with no minimum (`:201`).
    - **The layer-toggle rows, 402×29.** The checkbox is 15×15 (`.tog input`, `:62`), but the hit area is the `label.tog` row (`.tog{…padding:4px 0}`, `:61`), and that is 29 px.
    - **The kids' height stepper, 40×40.** `.lv-kid .st button{width:40px;height:40px;min-height:40px}` (`:511`).
    - **The directions-bar buttons, 40 tall.** `.lv-route button{min-height:40px}` (`:476`). Skeptic 1 measured the end × at 55.6×40; skeptic 2 checked this in code only.
  - **Flagged by element box, but not failures on touch:**
    - The Share-my-spot and kid-beacon switches are 50×30 inputs (`:435`) inside `label.lv-item.lv-share` rows that measure 402×60 on the iPhone and 792×60 on the iPad (`:1429`, exported at `apps/dollywood-live.html:1301`).
    - The card × is 36×36 with a mouse (`:115`) and 44×44 under `@media(pointer:coarse)` (`:130`).
    - The Queue-Times.com link is inline in a sentence.
- **Expected.** 44×44 pt minimum everywhere (house style; CLAUDE.md, Adding an app, step 6). The template's own "44 px targets" comment (`template.html:209`) describes only the hub (build-guide) flavour; the live flavour makes no such promise, and the hub rule applies to both.
- **Why it matters.** The park map is used one-handed while walking, and the small controls are the ones most often missed. The handle is how the sheet is opened.
- **Evidence.**
  - Skeptics: `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-parkmap-targets-18-1.json` (with `counts`), `-1-map-iphone.png`, `-1-family-iphone.png`; `verify-parkmap-targets-18-2.json`, `-2-family-iphone.png`, `-2-layers-iphone.png`.
  - Investigator: `analyze.json → areas['dollywood-live'].targets.adult.list` (selectors, minimum sizes, devices, jobs).
  - Code: `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:61-62, 115, 130, 201, 424, 432, 435, 476, 503, 511, 517, 522, 1429` (read-only).
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/dollywood-live/meet-overflow-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify-parkmap-targets-18-1.mjs` (park seed, Eli, iPhone PWA / iPad portrait / desktop, 11 states). Read `counts` in its JSON: 16 / 14 / 15 / 13.
  - Or `… -2.mjs`: the Nearby, Waits, Family, Style and card states, recording each control's hit box and `pointer:coarse`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** walked 11 states on three devices, measuring every visible control and, for an `<input>`, its enclosing label. Every size in the finding reproduced within 1 px. It found that the switches pass through their 60 px rows, and that the card × is 44×44 wherever `pointer:coarse` matches (the iPhone and iPad), so the real count on touch is 13 selectors.
  - **Skeptic 2** walked Nearby, Waits, Family, Style (scrolled to the bottom) and a listing card, recording the element box, the effective hit box and `pointer:coarse`. It sorted the sub-44 items into those already in P3 (the five rules), about five new rules (handle, About, layer rows, stepper, directions bar) and false positives (the switches, the × on touch, the inline link). The meeting bar's Go stayed hidden in its run, so it checked the directions bar in code only.
  - **Re-measure (independent code, main screen only):** `#lv-handle` 820×22 on the iPad portrait; 7 kid selectors under 64 on the main screen, 1 of them under 44. A consistent subset.
- **Corrected claim.** The measurements are right; the count of 18 overstates the problem:
  - By real hit area on a touch device, 13 selectors, about 8 rules, are under 44.
  - 8 of the 18 restate VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5's five rules.
  - The genuinely new material is about five rules: the handle 22, About 29, the layer rows 29, the stepper 40×40 and the directions bar 40.
  - The Share and beacon switches and the card × (on touch) are not failures, and the inline link is exempt.
  - The build guide's 27 duplicates VIS-DOLLYWOOD-2.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-5 (the five rules); VIS-DOLLYWOOD-2 (the build guide); UX-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-7 (the stepper takes one tap per inch; this finding adds only its size). Fixes belong in the sibling template.

title: The shared `hub.toast` is capped at half the viewport, so ordinary messages wrap to two or three lines on the iPhone in the shell, Kid Verse and Verses (added after the completeness critic)
block:
#### P4-SHAPE-04 — The shared `hub.toast` is capped at half the viewport, so ordinary messages wrap to two or three lines on the iPhone in the shell, Kid Verse and Verses (added after the completeness critic)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. Every message is still shown in full, at the same contrast and for the same time; it is narrower and two or three lines tall, and a three-line pill covers more of what is behind it (in Kid Verse, the Read it to me button for about 2.2 s). No flow breaks and no contrast or target threshold is failed.
  - **Exposure:** every iPhone (430 px) and, for messages longer than about 30 characters at 14 px, the iPad in portrait. On screens 1024 px and wider the toast fits one line.
- **Areas:** shell, kidverse, verses (the three documents that call `hub.toast`); the kiosk nudge reaches every hub.js document but only for the display profile.
- **What happens.**
  - `hub.toast` (`apps/hub.js:431-434`) builds a `.ds > .toast#hub-toast` in whichever document calls it. `.ds .toast` is `position: fixed; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); … max-width: calc(100% - 32px)` (`apps/design.css:588-591`). A fixed box with `left: 50%` and an auto width shrinks to fit the remaining 50 % of the viewport, so it can never be wider than half the screen, whatever `max-width` says. `max-width: calc(100% - 32px)` shows the intent was the full width minus margins.
  - On the 430 px iPhone (PWA and Safari) the computed `left` is 215 px, and every toast wider than 215 px on one line is clamped to exactly 215 px (WebKit, measured 700 ms after it appears):
    - shell "That app is not available for this profile." (`index.html:715`): 215×67, 2 lines (one-line width 294);
    - shell "Notifications on for this device.": 215×67, 2 lines (241);
    - shell "Hub updated — it will use the new version next time it opens.": 215×87, 3 lines;
    - Verses and Kid Verse "This device cannot read aloud.": 215×67, 2 lines (235);
    - Kid Verse "You already have today's star — come back tomorrow!": 215×87-96, 3 lines (387-436), over the Read it to me button.
    - Short messages stay on one line ("Checked with the house." 197, "Could not save that." 169, "Great listening!" 153).
  - On the iPad in portrait the cap is 410 px, so only the 61-character messages wrap (410×67, 2 lines, with 788 px available). On the iPad in landscape and the desktop, `left: calc(50% + 110px)` at 1024 px and wider (`index.html:340-341`) leaves enough room for one line.
  - With the counterfactual centring (`left: 16px; right: 16px; margin-inline: auto; width: max-content`, no translate) every one of these fits one line on the iPhone except the 61-character strings, which take 2 lines at 398 px.
- **Expected.** A toast sized to its message up to the viewport minus the margins: one line for a short message, like the iOS banner it imitates.
- **Why it matters.** Toasts are the hub's only confirmation surface, and the iPhone is the device the family carries. A narrow two- or three-line pill near the tab bar is harder to read at a glance, and for a kid it covers the next button.
- **Evidence.**
  - Critic: `audits/evidence/p4/CRITIC/toast-wrap.json` (iphone-pwa: `w` 215 with 2-3 lines; ipad-portrait: 241-367 on 1 line, 410 on 2 lines) and `audits/evidence/p4/CRITIC/toast-shell-iphone-pwa.png` (1x: the two-line "Grandma Jo can now tap their name on any device." pill on Me).
  - Skeptic 1: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-1.json`, `-2-1-shell-iphone.png`, `-2-1-verses-iphone.png` (the two-line "This device cannot read aloud." pill in Verses).
  - Skeptic 2: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-2.json`, `-2-2-shell-iphone.png`, `-2-2-kidverse-iphone.png` (the three-line star message over Read it to me).
  - Code: `apps/design.css:588-591`; `apps/hub.js:248, 431-434`; `index.html:340-341, 715`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/CRITIC/toast-wrap.mjs | grep iphone-pwa`: every message longer than about 30 characters prints `"w":215` with `"lines":2` or `3`. The skeptics' scripts, which fire only messages each document really sends: `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-1.mjs` and `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-shared-toast-half-viewport-wrap-2-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** called `hub.toast` with real message strings in the shell (`#me`) on the iPhone PWA and Safari, the iPad in both orientations and the desktop, and inside the Tally, F260, Kid Verse and Verses frames on the iPhone PWA and iPad portrait, and measured each box, line count, natural one-line width and the counterfactual layout. Two identical runs; the numbers above, and the critic's (215×67 on 2 lines, 241×46 on 1 line on the iPad, 215×87 on 3 lines, a 410 cap on 2 lines), match exactly.
  - **Skeptic 2** grepped every `hub.toast` caller (shell 30+, Kid Verse 11, Verses 4; F260, Tally, Timer, the Larder and Prayer 0; F260 and Prayer have their own toasts) and fired only messages each document sends, on the iPhone PWA and Safari, the iPad portrait and the desktop, as Eli (shell, Verses) and Ezra (Kid Verse). Same cap and wraps. The cap is ordinary CSS shrink-to-fit sizing of a fixed box with `left: 50%` and `right: auto`, the same on iOS Safari; the Windows fallback fonts only move the exact wrap point, so it is not a rig artefact.
- **Corrected claim.** The mechanism and the numbers are right; the critic's area list was too wide. Timer makes no `hub.toast` call (its "Timer done" toast belongs to the shell), the Larder, Tally and F260 reach it only through the kiosk nudge (`apps/hub.js:248`), which fires for the display profile on the 1920 px TV, where it fits one line, and Prayer has its own toast (VIS-SHAPE-4). Wrapping starts at about 29-30 characters at 14 px, not 25. F260's own `.toast` rule (`apps/f260.html:416-417`) also matches `#hub-toast`, which explains its slightly different height; not investigated further.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-SHAPE-4 (Prayer's own toast, the same centring; this settles its Unresolved 3), SHAPE token gap 14 (the toast contract), P4-SHAPE-02 (Prayer's toast action), CONS-MOTION-3 (three toast systems). Nothing in the P2 or P3 reports records the wrap.
- **Token gap.** A toast layout rule in the shared component: `left: 0; right: 0; margin-inline: auto; width: max-content; max-width: calc(100% - 2 * var(--margin))` (or a `--toast-max` token), no `translateX`, with the desktop offset for the sidebar applied as `left: 220px` rather than `50% + 110px` (SHAPE token gap 14; Proposed token set, SHAPE-14).

title: The content card is built six ways: radii from 12 to 36, five paddings, three border widths, three elevations (low)
block:
#### CONS-SHAPE-1 — The content card is built six ways: radii from 12 to 36, five paddings, three border widths, three elevations (low)

- **What happens.** The same role, a solid content card, is drawn as follows (Table SHAPE-4):
  - **Radii:** 12 (Larder), 16 (F260 Next up, Prayer ledger), 20 (build guide), 22 (shell, F260 Today), 28 (Kid Verse, Verses), 36 (TV panes).
  - **Padding:** 0, 14, 16×18, 18×16 or 20.
  - **Border:** 0 (Prayer's ledger), 1 px (`.ds`) or 1.5 px (F260).
  - **Elevation:** none (Prayer), `--e1` (Larder) or `--e2` (elsewhere).
  Even the `.ds` apps disagree with design.css's own `.card`, which is `--r-lg` 22, `--sp-5`, `--e2` (`apps/design.css:381-383`): Kid Verse and Verses override it to `--r-xl` 28 (`apps/kidverse.html:41, 61, 74, 95, 122`; `apps/verses.html:72`).
- **Code:**
  - the Larder: `.item` `var(--r-sm)` + `var(--e1)` (`apps/leftovers.html:71`);
  - F260: `.today` and `.hero`, 1.5 px borders, `--r-lg` / `--r` (`apps/f260.html:117, 100`);
  - Prayer: `.ledger{background:var(--gold-soft);border-radius:var(--r);padding:16px 18px}`, with no border and no shadow (`apps/prayer.html:151`);
  - the build guide: `border-radius:20px` (`template.html:234, 248`).
- **Expected.** One card recipe from design.css (radius, padding, border, elevation), used by every area, with variants only by role (grouped list, hero).
- **Why it matters.** Moving between apps, the same kind of surface changes its corner, weight and depth. The hub reads as separate web pages rather than one system.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/sheet-cards.png`; `cards-summary.json`; `remeasure.json → runs.boxes` (every card agrees).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/cards.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/cards-summary.mjs`, then read the `card ·` lines under `ipad-portrait`.
- **Related:** P2 VIS Shape (`audits/02-shell.md:5865`); the P3 Larder and F260 Shape rows (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:914`, `f260.md:774`).

title: Concentric corners are impossible by construction; at least 58 of 99 container/child pairs are off (low)
block:
#### VIS-SHAPE-1 — Concentric corners are impossible by construction; at least 58 of 99 container/child pairs are off (low)

- **What happens.**
  - **The root cause is in design.css.** `.card` is R22 with 20 px padding and a 1 px border, an inset of 21 (`apps/design.css:381-383`), and `.btn` is r16 (`:352`). Concentric would need r1, so every button in a card is 15 px off.
    - The re-measure read this in System and Midnight: Me `.card.glass` / `#syncnow` and Home `.gcard` / `.btn-soft`, R22 / 21 / r16 → want 1.
    - The draft's "want 2" is corrected to 1.
  - **The kid scale does not help.** It raises both radii by 6-8 px (`:283`) but not the padding, so kid cards stay off: the shell's kid Reminders card R28 / 21 / r28 (want 7), Verses kid R44 / 38 / r36 (want 6), and Kid Verse's story card R28 / 21 / `#story-say` r28 (want 7, off 21).
  - **Own-CSS areas repeat the pattern:**
    - the Larder's add bar R16 / 13 / r12 (want 3, off 9) on all four fields;
    - the build guide's build card R20 / 15 / r12, toolbar R16 / 11 / r12 and map box R20 / 11 / readout r16.
  - **New facets beyond P2/P3:**
    - in the park map: the sheet R24 / 23 / tabs r14 (want 1, off 13), the meeting bar R16 / 13 / field r10, the route card R18 / 18 / r12 and the amenity button R12 / 11 / r8;
    - the TV kiosk's Me card;
    - F260's Today card R22 / 19.5 / Done capsule r30 (want 2.5);
    - the who-pill R23 / 21 / avatar r14 (want 2) in Kid Verse and Verses.
  - **The count.** The rig's 55 of 95 is a floor, because its check skips pills and uses the top-left radius for all four corners (Table SHAPE-9). With F260's pairs and the park map's corrected pairs it is at least 58 of 99. Tally and Timer are not measured, not passing.
- **Expected.** House style: "an inner element's radius = outer radius minus padding." The shell's sheet (R36 / 20 / r16) and theme cards (R22 / 6 / r16) already do it.
- **Why it matters.** Mismatched nested corners are one of the clearest tells between the hub and first-party iPadOS surfaces, and design.css produces them by default.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/sheet-concentric.png`; `analyze.json → areas.*.concentric`; `verify.json` V1; `remeasure.json → runs.boxes` (`what: "conc …"` and `"concScan …"` entries); `audits/tools/phase4/measure/page-lib.mjs:472-492` (the rig's check).
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V1 (four pairs); `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/remeasure.mjs boxes` (per-corner scans with pills).
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 VIS "Cards are not concentric" (`audits/02-shell.md:5875`);
  - VIS-DOLLYWOOD-7 (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:736`);
  - VIS-KIDVERSE-8 (`audits/03-apps/kidverse.md:725`);
  - the Verses, Larder and Prayer Shape rows (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:582`, `leftovers.md:914`, `prayer.md:952`).

title: Nine content column widths, and only two apps use a layout token (low)
block:
#### CONS-SHAPE-2 — Nine content column widths, and only two apps use a layout token (low)

- **What happens.** Content columns are 360 (Tally's dial), 484-528 (Prayer, 33rem), 560 (Larder), 608 (Timer), 660 or 704 and then 1204 (F260, 44rem / 78rem), 688 (Kid Verse and Verses, the only users of `--max-read`), 788-880 and then 1200 (the shell), 1400 (the build guide) and full bleed (the park map) (Table SHAPE-3).

  - `.ds .container` and `.container-wide` exist (`apps/design.css:341-342`), and no area uses them.
- **Expected.** A small set of named column widths (for example narrow, read and wide), chosen by app type and shared with the shell.
- **Why it matters.** On the always-on iPad the family flips between apps constantly. A jumping content edge and phone-width columns on a landscape iPad look unplanned.
- **Evidence:** `verify.json` V2; `remeasure.json → runs.margins` (agrees ±1 px); `index.html:68, 84`; `apps/f260.html:44, 447`; `apps/leftovers.html:19`; `apps/prayer.html:50`; `apps/tally.html:40`; `apps/timer.html:13, 22, 48`; `apps/kidverse.html:22`; `apps/verses.html:23`; `template.html:233, 385`; screenshots `audits/screens/{leftovers/main,prayer/today,f260/today,tally/main,shell/home}-typical-ipad-landscape-light.png` and `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-typical-ipad-landscape-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V2 (e.g. ipad-landscape: leftovers 310/560, prayer 348/484, f260 22/1136, tally 410/360, shell 252/896).
- **Related:** VIS-PRAYER-6; VIS-HOME-3; the P3 Larder, Verses, Timer and Tally layout rows (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:913`, `verses.md:581`, `timer.md:479`).

title: The shell and the build guide keep the phone's 16 px margins on the iPad; F260 drops to 22 px in landscape, and its week stripes paint 7 px from the iPhone edge (low)
block:
#### VIS-SHAPE-2 — The shell and the build guide keep the phone's 16 px margins on the iPad; F260 drops to 22 px in landscape, and its week stripes paint 7 px from the iPhone edge (low)

- **What happens.**
  - **The shell.** `#views` pads with `--sp-4` at every width below 1024 px (`index.html:66-67`), so Home, Apps and Me sit 16 px from the edge of an 820 px iPad. Inside the same shell, the apps sit 66-230 px in.
  - **The build guide** also sits at 16 px on the iPad portrait and landscape.
  - **F260** is 80 px in on the iPad portrait and 22 px on the iPad landscape (its two-column layout).
  - **New (re-measure).** On the iPhone, F260's `.weeks{margin-left:-9px}` (`apps/f260.html:466`, at ≤ 480 px) and the week's 3 px left border (`:231`) hang the coloured stripes 9 px into the 16 px margin. The painted edge is 7 px from the screen edge, and the milestone rail's right edge is 14 px. On the iPad portrait the stripe starts at 67 against an 80 px text column.
  - Prayer's `.mark` buttons (margin −7) likewise paint at 15 px on the iPhone against a 22 px text margin.
- **Expected.** House style: 16-20 pt margins on the phone, wider on the iPad (for example 24-32 at regular width), with nothing painted inside the margin.
- **Why it matters.** On the primary device the shell looks like a stretched phone layout, while the apps inside it are inset. On the phone, F260's stripes nearly touch the screen edge.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/SHAPE/verify-margins-shell-ipad-portrait.png`; `verify.json` V2 (ipad-portrait shell 16/16; f260 80/80 against ipad-landscape 22/22); `remeasure.json → runs.margins` (iphone-pwa f260 left 7, right 14, `main#weeks.weeks > section#week-1`; ipad-portrait 67/78); `analyze.json → areas.dollywood.margins`; `audits/screens/dollywood/map-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`; `audits/screens/f260/today-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/verify.mjs` → V2; `node audits/tools/phase4/SHAPE/remeasure.mjs margins`.
- **Related:** P2 Layout & spacing, "the iPad keeps 16 px margins" (`audits/02-shell.md:5421, 5948`); the P3 F260 Layout row (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:773`). The painted-stripe facet is new.

title: The spacing rhythm splits the system in two: `.ds` areas are 98-100 % on the 4 px grid, own-CSS areas 34-84 % (low)
block:
#### CONS-SHAPE-3 — The spacing rhythm splits the system in two: `.ds` areas are 98-100 % on the 4 px grid, own-CSS areas 34-84 % (low)

- **What happens.**

title: Elevation has no role tokens and no upward level, so each role gets a different depth and the bars use literals (low)
block:

title: Prayer's toast wraps a short message onto two lines on the iPhone, because its centring caps it at half the viewport (low; new, found by P4-SHAPE-02's skeptics)
block:
#### VIS-SHAPE-4 — Prayer's toast wraps a short message onto two lines on the iPhone, because its centring caps it at half the viewport (low; new, found by P4-SHAPE-02's skeptics)

- **What happens.** `.toast{position:fixed;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);…max-width:92vw}` (`apps/prayer.html:254-257`). A fixed box with `left: 50%` and an auto width shrinks to fit within the remaining 50 % of the viewport, so the toast can never be wider than 215 px on a 430 px iPhone, whatever `max-width` says.
  - "Moved to the record." plus Undo therefore wraps onto two lines, in a 215×72.5 box.
  - On the iPad the same toast is 236×49, one line.
  - The shell's shared `.ds .toast` uses the same `left: 50%` centring (`apps/design.css:588`). **Measured after the completeness critic:** it wraps the same way, at a 215 px cap on the iPhone, in the shell, Kid Verse and Verses; that facet is filed and verified as P4-SHAPE-04 (Unresolved 3 is settled).
- **Expected.** A toast sized to its message up to the maximum width: one line for a short message.
- **Why it matters.** A two-line pill with a small action beside it is harder to read at a glance, and it is less like the iOS banner it imitates.
- **Evidence:** `verify-prayer-undo-target-1.json` (toast 215×72.5 on the iPhone PWA), `verify-prayer-undo-target-1-iphone.png`; `verify-prayer-undo-target-2.json` (73×215; skeptic 2 identified the cause); code `apps/prayer.html:254-257`, `apps/design.css:588`. This was not adversarially verified as a finding in its own right; both skeptics measured it while verifying P4-SHAPE-02.
- **Related:** none. A grep of the P2/P3 reports finds no record of the toast wrapping.
