title: Icon inks taken from `apps.json` or profile hex are never lifted for dark: kid tiles, Home card heads and accent icons fall under 3:1
block:
#### P4-ICON-01 — Icon inks taken from `apps.json` or profile hex are never lifted for dark: kid tiles, Home card heads and accent icons fall under 3:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium.
  - **Clause:** a measurable accessibility failure. Information-bearing non-text is below 3:1 on primary surfaces: the Apps grid, the kid Apps grid and the Home cards.
  - **Why not high:** every icon has an adjacent visible text label, so no adult flow breaks. The kid tile picture is the pre-readers' cue, which holds it at medium.
  - **Exposure:** Midnight and Forest. System resolves to Midnight at night, and the kitchen iPad stays open 24/7. In Parchment, two tiles are affected.
- **Areas:** shell (Apps grid, kid Apps grid, Home, kid Home, Chat); dollywood-live (selected tab, from the template).
- **What happens.** The inks are raw hex values set inline, and no palette can change them:
  - **Source of the inks.**
    - Tile glyphs are painted with the app's `apps.json` colour through `style="--tint:<hex>"` (`index.html:700`).
    - The Home card heads for Today's reading, In the fridge and Prayer get the same inline hex (`index.html:1165, 1176, 1188`).
    - `.ds .app-icon` paints `color: var(--tint)` (`apps/design.css:606-608`).
    - Where no `--tint` is set, it falls back to `--accent` (`apps/design.css:93`), which hub.js sets inline from the profile colour (`apps/hub.js:80`).
    - The park map strokes the selected tab with `var(--accent)` (`../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:429`).
  - **Midnight / Forest:**
    - Kid Apps grid (52.8 px glyphs): Larder 1.95 / 1.92, Prayer 2.84-2.87 / 2.82, Tally 2.93 / 2.88, park map 2.75 / 2.66. That is 4 of 7 kid tiles under 3:1; Timer 3.22, Verses 3.11 and Kid Verse 4.02 pass.
    - Adult Apps grid: 6 of 9 tiles at 1.95-2.93 in Midnight and 1.90-2.88 in Forest (F260, Larder, Prayer, Tally, build guide, park map).
    - Home card heads: Today's reading 2.29-2.30 / 2.25, In the fridge 1.95 / 1.92, Prayer 2.83-2.87 / 2.82-2.83.
    - Accent icons: the chat bot sparkle (Eli) 2.28-2.30 / 2.25; the park map's selected Nearby tab (Eli) 2.11-2.14 / 2.08-2.11; the kid "Let's play" sparkle (Ezra) 2.95 / 2.88. The investigator also measured Ezra's selected park-map tab at 2.70 in Parchment and 2.71 in Midnight.
  - **Parchment:** the Kid Verse tile 2.34-2.35 and the Timer tile 2.99.
  - **The contrast with the TV.** The TV board draws the same book and prayer meanings with theme tokens (`--tint:var(--slate|mocha|…)`, `index.html:1118-1125`), and they measure 4.86-6.16 in dark. On Home, the heads that use tokens also pass: Kids 7.89-8.01 and Reminders 6.08-6.16.
- **Expected.** Every icon on a tint reaches ≥ 3:1 in all five palettes, with app and person colours resolved through inks that have dark values.
- **Why it matters.** At night the pre-readers find their apps by the tile picture, and four of their seven pictures are below the non-text minimum. Adults lose the card-head cue on Home, though they keep the text.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator data: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/measure-midnight.json`, `measure-forest.json` and `measure-parchment.json` (surfaces `shell-apps`, `shell-kid-apps`, `shell-home`, `shell-chat`, `shell-kid-home`, `dollywood-live`), plus `below3.json`.
  - Investigator screenshots: `shot-home-heads-midnight-ipad.png`, `shot-tv-heads-midnight.png`, `shot-apps-grid-midnight-iphone.png`, `shot-apps-grid-parchment-iphone.png`.
  - Skeptic screenshots: `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1-kid-apps-midnight.png` (faint Larder, Prayer and Tally glyphs), `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-2-kid-apps-midnight-ipad.png`, `verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1-adult-home-midnight.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-dark.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs midnight shell-apps,shell-kid-apps,shell-home,shell-chat,shell-kid-home,dollywood-live`, then `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`. Read `declared` for the `.ticon` and `h2 > span.app-icon` items, and repeat with `forest` and `parchment`.
  - Skeptics: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/verify-icon-ink-hex-not-lifted-dark-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read `index.html:700`, `design.css:606-609` and `hub.js:80`, and the template's `:429`. Their own WebKit script set each theme as a person preference and confirmed `data-theme` and `data-scheme`. For each icon it recorded the computed ink and which inline `--tint`/`--accent` ancestor it came from, then hid the icon and took the median background from a CSS-scale shot.
    - Midnight: kid tiles 1.95 / 2.84 / 2.93 / 2.75; adult tiles 6 of 9 under 3:1; heads 2.30 / 1.95 / 2.83; chat 2.28; Let's play 2.95; Nearby tab 2.14; TV heads 4.86-6.08.
    - Forest: 1.92 / 2.82 / 2.88 / 2.66, adult tiles 1.90-2.85, heads 2.25 / 1.92 / 2.82, Nearby tab 2.11.
    - Parchment: Kid Verse 2.34, Timer 2.99.
    - In every theme the ink was the raw hex (for example `rgb(61,90,61)` = `#3D5A3D`).
  - **Skeptic 2** re-read the same lines plus the kid CTA (`index.html:1151`, no `--tint`, so it inherits `--accent`). Their own script set the theme through the API as eli and ezra and measured ipad-portrait Apps and Home plus the TV.
    - Midnight: adult tiles F260 2.30, Larder 1.95, Prayer 2.87, Tally 2.93, build guide 2.42, park map 2.75; kid tiles 4 of 7; heads 2.30 / 1.95 / 2.87; kid CTA 2.95; TV heads 4.91-6.16.
    - Forest: 1.92-2.88.
    - Light: Parchment 2.35 / 2.99, Hearth Kid Verse 2.76.
    - Rig check: the icon square is an opaque `color-mix` (`design.css:607`), so the missing backdrop blur does not change the result.
  - **Re-measure** (`remeasure.mjs`, band-sampled background):
    - Midnight: adult tiles 2.29 / 1.95 / 2.85 / 2.93 / 2.42 / 2.74 (6 of 9); kid tiles 1.95 / 2.85 / 2.93 / 2.75; heads 2.29 / 1.95 / 2.85.
    - Forest: adult tiles 2.25-2.87.
    - Parchment: Kid Verse 2.35, Timer 2.99.
    - TV: book 5.77, prayed 5.54.
    - All agree within 0.15.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The figures reproduce within 0.05 of the draft. The only second-decimal differences are kid Prayer 2.84-2.87, the Nearby tab 2.11-2.14 / 2.08-2.11, and Kid Verse in Parchment 2.34-2.35.
  - Only skeptic 1 re-measured the chat sparkle and the park-map tab.
  - The adult-tile facet in Midnight and the root cause (inline `--accent`, hex tints) are not new: Phase 2 recorded them without an ID (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846, 5883-5886`).
  - New in this finding: the kid grid (4 of 7), Forest, the Home card heads, the chat and kid sparkles, the park-map tab, the Parchment Kid Verse and Timer tiles, and the comparison with the token-tinted TV heads.
  - A qualifier from skeptic 2: theme tokens alone do not guarantee 3:1 in light. `var(--gold)` gives the Reminders head only 2.76 in Hearth (P4-ICON-03).
- **Related (not re-filed).** P2 VIS "accent and tile icons not lifted for dark" and "flat tiles with pale icons" (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846, 5883-5886`, no ID); the P2 rubric row (`:5423`).

title: The 20 % duotone never renders on sprite icons (`<use>`), so the one icon recipe renders two ways
block:
#### P4-ICON-02 — The 20 % duotone never renders on sprite icons (`<use>`), so the one icon recipe renders two ways

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. A decorative 20 % fill is missing; no information, flow or contrast is affected.
- **Areas:** shell (also the style guide, `docs/design.html`).
- **What happens.**
  - **Why the selector misses.** `.ds .icon .duo { fill: var(--tint); fill-opacity: .2; stroke: none }` (`apps/design.css:605`; the comment at `:604` states the intent) needs the `.duo` path to be a descendant of `.icon`. In the sprite, the `.duo` paths sit inside `<symbol>` in an unclassed hidden `<svg>` (`index.html:416-438`; 13 of the 21 symbols carry one). Inside the `<use>` instance there is no `.icon` ancestor, so the rule never matches. The `.duo` path inherits `fill: none` from `.icon` (`:602`) and is stroked a second time on top of the outline.
  - **Where the duotone does render.** Only inline SVGs get the tint: the 9 tile icons, `ICON_STAR` and `ICON_PIN` (`index.html:886-887`).
  - **Surfaces with no duotone:** the tab bar, the pill, the Reminders, Today's reading, In the fridge, Prayer and Around the house heads, chat, Me, and five of the six TV heads.
  - **Surfaces with the duotone:** the Kids head (adult Home), the Stars head (kid Home), the Me Kids' rewards head and the TV "Stars this week" head.
  - **Visibility.** The mix is subtle at 1× (a maximum channel delta of about 40), which explains why Phase 2 recorded the language as consistent.
  - **Style guide.** The guide's only icon sample also goes through `<use>` (`docs/design.html:243`, symbol at `:247`), so it never shows the duotone either.
- **Expected.** One recipe that renders the same through `<use>` and inline, or a spec without a duotone.
- **Why it matters.** It corrects two earlier statements:
  - P2's "OK — One icon language … a 20 % duotone" (`audits/02-shell.md:6005`) holds for inline icons only.
  - The Timer checker's "its duotone is not discernible at 16 px" (`audits/03-apps/timer.md:443`): the duotone is absent, not small.

  The house's one icon recipe does not render as specified on most of the shell.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/duo-sprite-webkit.json` and `duo-sprite-chromium.json` (`duoRendersViaUse: false`, `duoRendersInline: true`, light and dark); `duo-sprite-webkit.png` (the same `#i-home` at 192 px, hollow via `<use>` and tinted inline).
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-1-{webkit,chromium}.json` and `-webkit.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-2-{webkit,chromium}.json`, `-shipped.png` and `-inlined.png`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/duo-sprite.mjs webkit`, then again with `chromium`. Also `verify-duotone-missing-on-sprite-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** drew every real `svg.icon` on Home (light and dark), Apps, Chat, Me, kid Home and TV three times at 48 px, in WebKit and Chromium:
    - A: the shipped clone;
    - B: inline without `.duo`;
    - C: inline with `.duo`.

    In the region where C differs from B, the results were:
    - **`<use>` icons:** 0 of 20 on Home, 0 of 25 on Chat, 0 of 10 on kid Home and 0 of 13 on TV rendered the duotone. For example, the `#i-book` head had 384 of 454 fill pixels untinted.
    - **Inline icons:** every one rendered it (35 of 35 on Home; the TV Stars head included).
    - **Positive control:** the sprite geometry drawn inline always tinted.
  - **Skeptic 2** measured the icons in place, on shipped pages. They replaced each `<use>` with its symbol's content (A) and stripped `.duo` from the originally inline icons (B), against a noise baseline of 0 px, in both engines and both modes.
    - Home: 9 icons declare a duotone and 1 renders it (the inline Kids head). All 8 `<use>` icons changed by 81-250 px when inlined.
    - Me: 0 of 6.
    - TV: 1 of 6 (only the inline Stars head).
  - **Re-measure:** through `<use>` the `#i-home` interior stays pure `[255,255,255]`; drawn inline it is `[246,217,207]`. 13 of the 21 symbols carry `.duo`.
- **Corrected claim.** The mechanism and the fact that both engines agree are confirmed. Counts depend on the method, but the rule does not: every `<use>` icon renders 0 duotone and every inline icon renders it. The counts by method:
  - 75 declared / 31 rendered distinct icons (investigator, de-duplicated);
  - 108 / 54 raw instances in Hearth (investigator and re-measure);
  - 55 / 35 DOM-wide on adult Home (skeptic 1);
  - 9 / 1 visible on Home (skeptic 2).

  Corrections to the draft:
  - "TV heads never get it" is wrong for the TV "Stars this week" head, which is inline and does get it.
  - The Park head was not observed; it appears only on park days.
  - The style-guide sample is at `docs/design.html:243`, not `:244`.
  - The mix is subtle at 1×, not glaring.
- **Related (not re-filed).** P2 OK "One icon language" (`audits/02-shell.md:6005`) and the rubric row (`:5423`). No P2 or P3 ID records this defect.

title: `--gold` is used as icon ink on gold tints: six icons at 2.76-2.78:1 in Hearth, while the shell's `--gold-ink` override covers only two heads
block:
#### P4-ICON-03 — `--gold` is used as icon ink on gold tints: six icons at 2.76-2.78:1 in Hearth, while the shell's `--gold-ink` override covers only two heads

> **Overlap (assembly).** The Kid Verse week-strip star (gold on gold-soft, 2.78 in Hearth) is also listed among the non-text facets of P4-COLOR-01. It is one defect instance, counted here.

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a decorative or secondary non-text failure. Each heading icon repeats the text heading beside it. The earned Kid Verse day and the earned F260 milestone are also shown by the gold-soft fill, the border and full opacity.
  - **Exposure:** Hearth, which is also System by day.
- **Areas:** shell (Home, kid Home, Me, TV), kidverse, f260.
- **What happens.** Two recipes paint the base hue `--gold` (`#B4861B` in Hearth) on a gold tint.
  - **Recipe 1: `.app-icon` with `color: var(--tint)`** (`apps/design.css:606-608`) and `--tint:var(--gold)`, on a 22 %→8 % gold mix. Each measures 2.76-2.77, or 2.64-2.88 across the gradient:
    - the Reminders bell on Home (`index.html:1203`), kid Home (`:1153`) and the TV (`:1127`);
    - the Me "Kids' rewards" star (`:1272`);
    - the TV "Stars this week" star (`:1124`).
  - **Recipe 2: `--gold` on `--gold-soft`.** Each measures 2.78:
    - the Kid Verse week-strip star (`apps/kidverse.html:68`). The day number in the same element uses `--gold-ink` (`:67`).
    - F260's earned-milestone text glyphs ♥ ✓ ♪ ◐ (`apps/f260.html:196`).
  - **Not affected:** the adult Home Kids head and the kid Home Stars head. `index.html:199` sets `color: var(--gold-ink)` on them, and they measure 5.33-5.34.
  - **Other palettes:** Parchment 3.09-3.11 at the median (2.87 at the 22 % end), Frost 3.21-3.30 (2.97 at the 22 % end), Midnight and Forest 5.1-7.8.
- **Expected.** ≥ 3:1 for every gold icon in every palette. `--gold-ink` already exists in every palette (`apps/design.css:74, 124, 144, 164, 206`) and measures 5.32-5.37 on these backgrounds in Hearth.
- **Why it matters.** One ink repeats on the gold icons across the shell, the TV, Kid Verse and F260. The shell's own fix is applied in one place.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `measure-hearth.json` (surfaces `shell-home`, `shell-kid-home`, `shell-me`, `shell-tv`, `kidverse`, `kid-kidverse`, `f260`) and `below3.json`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-1.json` and `-tv.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-2.json`, `-2-parchment.json`, and crops including `-home-adult-reminders-bell.png`, `-home-adult-kids-card-head.png` (the passing `--gold-ink` head), `-me-adult-rewards-head.png`, `-tv-tv-stars-head.png` and `-kidverse-kid-days-on-star.png`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs hearth shell-home,shell-tv,shell-me,kid-kidverse,f260 && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`, then filter `below3.json` for theme `hearth` and fg `[180,134,27]`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-1.mjs`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-gold-icon-ink-hearth-2.mjs hearth` (and `parchment`).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** selected each target by selector and sampled every background pixel (min, median, max). They also repainted each text glyph red, then blue, to see whether the ink applies at all, and computed the ratio analytically from the tokens for all five palettes.
    - **Hearth:** bell 2.76 on all three surfaces; Me head 2.76; TV Stars 2.76; week-strip star 2.78; F260 ♥ ✓ ♪ ◐ 2.78 (the repaint changed 49-115 px, so the ink is really drawn).
    - **Passing:** the Home Kids and Stars heads, 5.33 / 5.34.
    - **Emoji:** ⛰ 📖 🔥 💯 ✝ changed 0 px when repainted, so they render as colour emoji.
    - **Analytic, gold on gold-soft:** Hearth 2.78, Parchment 3.11, Frost 3.30, Midnight 7.79, Forest 7.55.
  - **Skeptic 2** used the median background under each hidden icon in Hearth and Parchment.
    - **Hearth:** bell 2.76 (adult Home, kid Home, TV); Me head 2.76; TV Stars 2.76; week-strip star 2.78; F260 text glyphs 2.78.
    - **Passing:** the Home heads at 5.33-5.34.
    - **`--gold-ink` instead:** would measure 5.32-5.37 on the same backgrounds.
    - **Parchment:** 3.09-3.11, which passes.
  - **Re-measure:** bell 2.77 on Home, kid Home and TV; Me head 2.77; TV Stars 2.77; week-strip 2.78; F260 milestones 2.78; the Home Kids and Stars heads 5.34 (`--gold-ink`).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **Wrong location in the draft:** "Stars/Kids star heads 2.76 (Home, Me, TV)" is wrong for Home. The failing star heads are the Me Kids' rewards head and the TV Stars head only.
  - **⛰ is a rig artefact:** its "2.71" is not a gold-ink failure; it renders as a colour emoji.
  - **Parchment and Frost:** they fail only at the 22 % end of the gradient, which is not filed.
  - **Not a token gap:** `--gold-ink` exists in every palette. The defect is that `.app-icon` and these two rules use the base hue instead of the existing ink step. The draft's "add `--gold-ink`" is withdrawn.
- **Related (not re-filed).** The P2 Kid Verse tile at 2.77 in light (`audits/02-shell.md:5885`; its `apps.json` colour is the same `#B4861B`). VIS-F260-1 covers gold used as text (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:706, 805`), not the milestone glyphs.

title: The map compass's north needle is a fixed `#FF6B4A`: 2.24-2.75:1 in the three light palettes
block:
#### P4-ICON-04 — The map compass's north needle is a fixed `#FF6B4A`: 2.24-2.75:1 in the three light palettes

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a secondary information-bearing graphic below 3:1. North is also marked by a rotating "N" label at 4.37-4.77:1, so nobody is blocked.
  - **Exposure:** the park map in Hearth, Parchment and Frost (and System by day), for adult and kid profiles alike. In the build guide the button is dead (P3-DOLLYWOOD-10) and hidden below 700 px.
- **Areas:** dollywood-live, dollywood (generated). The fix belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:620`.
- **What happens.**
  - **The markup.** The north half of `#lv-north` is `fill="#FF6B4A"` as a literal attribute (`apps/dollywood-live.html:620`; identical at `apps/dollywood.html:620`, from `template.html:620`). It sits on the cream glass button (`var(--lv-glass-soft)`, `:417`).
  - **Measured:**

    | Palette | Contrast |
    |---|---|
    | Hearth | 2.70-2.75 |
    | Parchment | 2.24-2.29 |
    | Frost | 2.66-2.72 |
    | Midnight | 5.85-5.93 |
    | Forest | 5.76-5.83 |

  - **Against the grey south half** it measures only 1.13-1.41 in every theme.
  - **The other north cue.** A 9 px, weight 800 "N" in `var(--danger)` (`:418`) rotates with the button and reads 4.37-4.77 in the light palettes.
  - **Build guide.** The compass is hidden below 700 px by `[data-flavor=hub] .lv-northwrap{display:none}` inside `@media(max-width:699px)` (`apps/dollywood.html:313, 352`).
- **Expected.** The needle colour comes from a per-palette token at ≥ 3:1 on the control. `var(--danger)`, which the N label already uses, passes here.
- **Why it matters.** It is the colour cue for north on a rotated map, and it fails in the normal daylight themes. CLAUDE.md allows hex only for map colours, and this is control chrome.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `measure-{hearth,parchment,frost}.json` (surfaces `dollywood`, `dollywood-live`, `kid-dollywood-live`, selector `button#lv-north.lv-north > svg`) and `below3.json`.
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-compass-needle-hex-1.json` and `-1-parchment.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-compass-needle-hex-2.json`, `-2-webkit-parchment.png`, `-2-chromium-parchment.png` and `-2-webkit-midnight.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/dollywood-live/amenity-tap-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png` (the bottom-left disc).
- **Reproduction.**
  - Investigator: `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/measure.mjs parchment dollywood-live,dollywood && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-compass-needle-hex-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (WebKit; all six themes; dollywood-live on iphone-pwa and dollywood on ipad-portrait and iphone-pwa):
    - Method: rotation and transition were disabled, and 6 points inside the north half were sampled at device-pixel scale, with the button's background taken from a shot with the needle hidden.
    - The computed fill was `rgb(255,107,74)` in every theme.
    - Results: Hearth 2.75, Parchment 2.29, Frost 2.72, Midnight 5.85, Forest 5.76.
    - The build guide on iPhone has `display: none`.
    - The N label measures 4.41-4.77 in light and 6.32-6.37 in dark.
  - **Skeptic 2** (WebKit and Chromium; Chromium paints the real backdrop blur):
    - Method: eroded `isPointInFill` samples of the north and south halves.
    - WebKit: 2.75 / 2.29 / 2.72 / 5.85 / 5.76.
    - Chromium: 2.73 / 2.27 / 2.70 / 5.85 / 5.76.
    - Needle against the south half: 1.13-1.41.
    - N label: 4.37-4.77.
    - So this is not a blur artefact: the glass is nearly opaque.
  - **Re-measure:** 2.70 / 2.24 / 2.66 / 5.93 / 5.81 (iPhone PWA).
- **Corrected claim.** The draft's "the only cue for north" is wrong: the rotating N label is also a cue. The build-guide exposure is iPad and desktop only, and there the button is dead. The inline hex itself was already counted in P3 (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:908`); the new facet is the contrast measurement.
- **Related (not re-filed).**
  - P3-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-09 covers the compass behaviour.
  - P3-DOLLYWOOD-10 covers the dead build-guide button.
  - The hardcoded-colour row in `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:908`.
  - Both skeptics noted that the 9 px N label is below the 11 px floor, a text-size facet for the typography dimension.

title: In the `.ds` apps every icon's own `stroke-width` and `fill` attribute is dead: all compute 1.75, and the "filled" Prayer-warrior heart renders as an outline
block:
#### P4-ICON-05 — In the `.ds` apps every icon's own `stroke-width` and `fill` attribute is dead: all compute 1.75, and the "filled" Prayer-warrior heart renders as an outline

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. The stroke weights differ by 0.25-0.5 px, and one badge glyph draws as an outline instead of solid. No text, contrast, target or data is affected.
- **Areas:** kidverse, verses (both `<body class="ds">`: `apps/kidverse.html:144`, `apps/verses.html:99`).
- **What happens.**
  - **Why the attributes lose.** Any author CSS rule beats an SVG presentation attribute, and `.ds .icon { fill: none; stroke-width: 1.75 }` (`apps/design.css:602`) is such a rule.
  - **Stroke weights.** Each of these icons asks for its own weight and computes 1.75:
    - Verses' Not yet and Almost (`stroke-width="2"`) and Got it (`"2.25"`) (`apps/verses.html:113-115`);
    - Kid Verse's I heard it (`"2.2"`, `apps/kidverse.html:173`; kid view only);
    - the Story lover badge book (`"1.9"`, `:400`).
  - **The heart.** The Prayer-warrior heart is written `fill="currentColor"` (`:400`) but computes `fill: none` and draws a 1.75 outline.
  - **The star.** The badge star beside it is filled, because it has its own rule, `.ds .icon.star` (`:52`). The heart has no such rule.
- **Expected.** The markup and the rendering agree. Either the fill intent survives `.ds .icon`, or the dead attributes are removed.
- **Why it matters.** It corrects P3 Verses' "strokes 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 … mixed" (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:583, 617`). The rendered weights are uniform, and only the markup differs. The badge row pairs a filled star with an outline heart, against the code's intent.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/ICON/facets.json` (`attrStrokeWidth` vs `computedStrokeWidth`; `kidverse-ezra-heart`: `svgFillAttr "currentColor"`, `fill "none"`).
  - Skeptic 1: `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-1-{webkit,chromium}.json`, `-1-badges-ezra-shipped.png` and `-1-badges-ezra-attr-honoured.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-2.json`, `-2-badges-shipped.png` and `-2-badges-intended.png`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/facets.mjs`, then inspect `facets.json`. Also `verify-ds-icon-overrides-attributes-1.mjs` and `-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (WebKit and Chromium; Kid Verse as ezra and eli, Verses as eli after Show):
    - Every attributed icon computes 1.75px with `fill: none`, on both the `<svg>` and its shape.
    - A pixel test (copy the attributes into inline style so they win; noise 0 px) changed:
      - story-heard: 67 / 62 px
      - book: 59 / 125 px
      - heart: 130 / 134 px
      - Not yet: 94 / 93 px
      - Almost: 18 / 34 px
      - Got it: 50 / 42 px
    - Icons whose attribute already equals the rule changed 0 px.
    - The badge-row PNGs show an outline heart as shipped and a solid heart with the attribute honoured.
  - **Skeptic 2** (both engines):
    - The same computed values.
    - Control: with `body.ds` removed, each icon computes its own attribute (2px, 2.25px, 2.2px, 1.9px), and the heart fills.
    - Forcing the attributes changes 18-127 px per icon and 220 px on the heart (its ink ratio goes from 0.17 to 0.26).
  - **Re-measure:** Kid Verse attributes 1.75 / 1.9 / 2.2 and Verses 1.75 / 2 / 2.25 all compute 1.75px, for kid and adult. The `.bicon` heart computes `fill: none` with a 1.75 stroke.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The claim is accurate.
  - Attributes that already say 1.75 or `none` are redundant, not visibly dead.
  - In the seed data the Prayer-warrior badge is unearned (muted). The same rule draws it as an outline once it is earned.
  - The stroke differences are sub-pixel, so the heart is the only visible mismatch.
- **Related (not re-filed).** VIS-KIDVERSE-9 (labels repeat their icon; text −/+) is a different defect.

title: Eleven icon families; no app uses the shell's own set (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### CONS-ICON-1 — Eleven icon families; no app uses the shell's own set (investigator rating: medium)

- The shell (F1-F3) is one custom 1.75 recipe. Each app brings its own:
  - F260: Feather/Lucide-derived paths at 2 on 18 px, a 20-grid tick at 2.6, colour emoji, text glyphs and CSS chevrons.
  - The Larder: inlined Lucide at 2-2.4.
  - Prayer: hand drawn at 1.75-2.4.
  - Kid Verse and Verses: hand drawn, computing 1.75.
  - The Dollywood template: hand drawn at 2-2.6, plus text glyphs and emoji.
  - Tally and Timer: none.
- `<use href="#i-…">` appears only in `index.html` (30 uses of a 21-symbol sprite) and in F260's private 11-symbol sprite (`static.json`; the re-measure's static check).
- The same meaning is drawn in several ways (Table ICON-4):
  - "Done": 5 SVG paths at 5 computed weights, plus a text ✓ in 5 areas.
  - "Star": 4 ways. The SVG star head and the text ★ chips sit in the same Kids card (`index.html:913-916`).
  - "Add": 4 ways.
  - "Previous / next": chevrons and text −/+ inside F260 (`apps/f260.html:617-620` vs `:692-694`).
  - "Book": 5 drawings; "timer" 3; "map pin" 3.
- Rendered stroke for icons of the same job (14-26 px) runs 1.02-2.86 px. The shell renders 11 sizes (Table ICON-2).
- **Expected (house style):** "One open-source icon set … consistent stroke weight and optical size in every app."
- **Evidence:**
  - `static.json`, `rollup.json`, Tables ICON-2 and ICON-4.
  - `audits/screens/f260/milestones-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`: colour emoji, text ✎ and ♥, stroked printer and gear, text − and +, CSS chevrons and SVG ticks on one screen.

- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/static.mjs && node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`, then compare `strokeWidthsVbUnits`, `strokePxMin`/`strokePxMax` and `renderedSizesPx` per area.
- **Related (per-app mixes already noted, not re-filed):**
  - VIS-F260-12 and the F260 rubric row (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:775`).
  - VIS-KIDVERSE-9.
  - VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8.
  - The park map's icon-set row (`audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:778`).
  - Prayer (`audits/03-apps/prayer.md:953`) and Verses (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:617`).
  - P2 "Glyphs" (`audits/02-shell.md:5889`).

title: One drawing, several meanings (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-ICON-2 — One drawing, several meanings (investigator rating: low)

Several drawings carry more than one meaning (Table ICON-5):
- Flame = the activity feed in the shell, but a streak in F260.
- Heart = a memorised verse, the Prayer warrior badge and an **AED**.
- ⊕ = the Tally counter and Prayer's Add.
- × = close / remove and **delete the last PIN digit**; ✕ = ride closed.

- Sparkle = "Let's play", the chat assistant and the unknown-app fallback.
- Circular arrows = reload and Copy.
- The strollers amenity uses a shopping-cart emoji.
- The Guests head is a bare plus.

- **Expected:** one meaning per glyph across the hub. Table ICON-6 maps each meaning to a distinct Lucide or Phosphor name (for example `activity` vs `flame`, `heart-pulse` for AED, `delete` for the PIN backspace, `ban` for closed).

- **Related:** P2 ambiguous glyphs (`audits/02-shell.md:5889`), VIS-LEFTOVERS-9 and UX-PRAYER-5 (not re-filed). New: the cross-app collisions.

title: Text glyphs and colour emoji stand in for icons in six areas (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### VIS-ICON-1 — Text glyphs and colour emoji stand in for icons in six areas (investigator rating: low)

Glyphs render in the OS text font and emoji in the platform's colour set, so they take no token colour, weight or dark variant. Even the split between glyph and emoji depends on the platform: in the rig's WebKit, ⛰ and ✝ render as colour emoji, and repainting them changes 0 px (skeptic 1 of P4-ICON-03).

Where they appear:

| Area | Glyphs and emoji | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Shell | ★ ✓ | `index.html:916, 1065, 1068, 1169, 1187, 1358, 1478` |
| F260 | 12 glyphs and 6 emoji kinds | `apps/f260.html:603-620, 704, 1219-1232, 1510, 1586` |
| Tally | + − | `apps/tally.html:137-140` |
| Kid Verse | − + ★ ✓ | `apps/kidverse.html:160, 359, 369, 663` |
| Both Dollywood exports | 21 glyphs and 5 emoji | `apps/dollywood-live.html:584, 588, 621, 647, 961, 1285, 1532, 1564` |

F260's unearned milestones mix colour emoji at opacity .55 with grey text glyphs (✎ at 1.98-2.01 in the light palettes).

- **Expected:** control and status icons come from the one SVG set, and emoji are used only for faces.
- **Evidence:** `static.json` (`<area>.glyphs`, `<area>.emoji`); `audits/screens/f260/milestones-typical-iphone-pwa-light.png`; `measure-hearth.json` f260 `div.mi` items.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/static.mjs`, then inspect `static.json`.
- **Related:** VIS-F260-12, VIS-KIDVERSE-9, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8, `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:778` and `audits/03-apps/tally.md:675` (not re-filed). This entry adds only the cross-area count.

title: The design system has no icon tokens, size scale, weight rule, ink rule or shared sprite, and the style guide shows one glyph (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### GAP-ICON-1 — The design system has no icon tokens, size scale, weight rule, ink rule or shared sprite, and the style guide shows one glyph (investigator rating: medium)

What `design.css` has:
- `.icon` at 24 / 32 px with a 1.75 stroke (`apps/design.css:602-603`);
- the `.duo` fill (`:605`, broken through `<use>`, P4-ICON-02);
- `.app-icon` (`:606-609`);
- `.btn .icon` at 1.25em (`:371`), `.tab .icon` at 26 px (`:563`) and `.empty .icon` at 48 px (`:546`).

What is missing:
- **A size scale.** The shell renders 14-53 px in 11 sizes; F260 renders 16-64 px.
- **A stroke rule.** Nothing keeps the rendered stroke constant: it runs 1.02-3.85 px in the shell.
- **An ink rule for icons on a tint.** `.app-icon` paints the base `--tint` (P4-ICON-01, -03).
- **Dark values for app and person colours.**
- **Kid and TV icon sizes.** The kid tab icons stay at 26 px.
- **A sprite apps can load.** The sprite lives inline in `index.html` only.
- **A themed select chevron.** The chevron is `#7D6F62` in a data URI (`:449`). It passes at 3.34-4.75 but never follows the theme.

The style guide's Icons section is four copies of `#i-plus`, each on a hex `--tint` (`docs/design.html:241-247`).

- **Evidence:** the cited lines; `rollup.json` `renderedSizesPx`, `strokePxMin`/`strokePxMax`.
- **Reproduction:** `grep -n "icon" apps/design.css`; `sed -n 241,247p docs/design.html`; `node audits/tools/phase4/ICON/report.mjs`.

title: A custom shell set rather than one open-source set; Lucide and Feather paths ship without their licence notice (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### GAP-ICON-2 — A custom shell set rather than one open-source set; Lucide and Feather paths ship without their licence notice (investigator rating: low)

- **The shell set is custom.** The shell and tile icons are hand drawn, not Lucide or Phosphor.
- **Open-source paths ship without a notice.**
  - The Larder inlines Lucide ("Lucide glyphs, inlined", `apps/leftovers.html:148`).
  - F260's lock, book, book-open, edit-3, settings and chevron symbols match Feather / Lucide by visual inspection (`apps/f260.html:531-541`); they were not diffed against upstream.
  - Neither ships the ISC or MIT notice. A repo grep for Lucide, Feather, ISC and licence finds only that comment and the Dollywood 3D bundle's MIT header (`apps/dollywood.html:1744-1746`).
- **Clean on Apple assets.** No SF Symbols and no SF Pro are shipped.

title: The `--sheen-x` drift restyles the whole document on every scroll step; it costs more than the blur, and F260 drops frames for it
block:
#### P4-GLASS-01 — The `--sheen-x` drift restyles the whole document on every scroll step; it costs more than the blur, and F260 drops frames for it

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic (smoothness) and cost. No data is lost and no flow breaks. Home and Prayer keep 60 fps and pay in main-thread time; F260 loses 8-14 % of its frames on a fast desktop.
  - **Exposure:** every scroll of a document hub.js watches (the window, or the shell's `#views` via `hub.sheenFrom`, `index.html:662`), in the shell and in every app frame. Not under Reduce Motion (`apps/hub.js:442`), where the shell is blank anyway (P2-STAB-01).
- **Kind:** perf.
- **Areas:** shell, F260, Larder, Prayer, Verses, Kid Verse, Tally, Timer, build guide, park map (every document that loads hub.js).
- **What happens.**
  - **The write.** A scroll listener (`apps/hub.js:448`) and `hub.sheenFrom` (`:447`) schedule a rAF that computes `x` from the scroll fraction and, whenever the rounded value changes, calls `root.style.setProperty('--sheen-x', x + '%')` on `<html>` (`:445`). The value is rounded to 1 % over a 50-step range, so a long scroll writes up to once a frame.
  - **The restyle.** `--sheen-x` is an inherited custom property, so each write restyles every element in the document, whether or not it uses the value. The skeptics' trace: one `UpdateLayoutTree` per write over 5,572 elements in F260 (all 35 over 10 ms, up to 19.7 ms), 731 on Home, 164 in Prayer. A root custom property that nothing uses costs the same per write as `--sheen-x`, while the same write on one leaf element costs 3 µs.
  - **The same in WebKit.** Skeptic 2's forced-style micro-benchmark: a root write costs 1,897 / 11,677 / 483 µs (Home / F260 / Prayer) in Chromium and 8,553 / 79,813 / 2,210 µs in Playwright's Windows WebKit, against 3 µs and 0-10 µs on a leaf. Windows WebKit is slow in absolute terms; only the root-to-leaf ratio (221-7,981×) carries over.
  - **What it buys.** Every recipe surface repaints its accent radial at `var(--sheen-x)` (`apps/design.css:392`, and the hand copies). In F260 Today on the iPad, the only sheen-painted surface is the 159×52 `.switch` pill at the top (`apps/f260.html:57-58`, no blur); for most of the scroll no glass is on screen, and the drift still restyles about 7,700 elements.
  - **The cost** (Table GLASS-3): dropping only the writes cuts scroll CPU 31-57 % (re-measure 36-61 %) and main-thread time 2.0-4.1× in all 8 scrolling scenes, and removes every scroll-time recalc. Turning every `backdrop-filter` off changes scroll CPU by −19 % to +10 %, and does nothing for F260.
  - **F260's frames**, shipped vs sheen off: investigator 58.9 fps, p95 32.5 ms, 10.5 % over 20 ms vs 62.5 / 17 / 0 %; skeptic 1 about 61.7 / 24-25 / 8.1-9.1 % vs 62.5 / 17 / 0-0.3 %; skeptic 2 61.8-62 / 25-26 / 8.9-9.6 % vs 62.5 / 17 / 0 %; re-measure 60.2 / 26.5 / 12 % vs 62.5 / 18 / 4.2 %.
- **Expected.** The drift changes only the glass surfaces: a transform on a pseudo-element layer, or the value set on the few glass elements themselves. It never lives on `<html>`, and hub.js skips it in a document with no visible glass. A registered non-inherited `@property` on `<html>` is not enough (see Corrected claim).
- **Why it matters.** Scrolling is the most common gesture on the 24/7 iPad. The drift that makes the glass shimmer is the largest glass cost the rig found, and F260, the daily reading app, drops frames for it even on a fast desktop. The iPad's budget is tighter.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:439-453` (`:445` the write, `:447` `sheenFrom`, `:448` the listener); `apps/design.css:392`; `apps/f260.html:57-58`; `index.html:662`.
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/perf.json` (`scenes.<scene>.arms.scroll` A, B, C; `scenes.f260-today.layers` = `#tabbar`, `#pill` only).
  - Skeptics: `verify-sheen-restyles-whole-document-1.json`, `-1-run2.json`, `verify-sheen-restyles-whole-document-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-perf-home.json`, `remeasure-perf-me_chat-phone_prayer_f260.json`, `remeasure-perf-leftovers_kidverse_verses_tally.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/perf.mjs" --scene f260-today,shell-home,prayer-today --out <a new JSON file>`, then compare `arms.scroll.A.mean` with `.C.mean` and `.B.mean` per scene.
  - `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/verify-sheen-restyles-whole-document-1.mjs"` (trace of `UpdateLayoutTree` element counts per write, arms A, N, B, R).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote a script that does not reuse `perf.mjs`: Chromium, Eli, iPad portrait, F260 Today, Home and Prayer, its own bouncing rAF scroll, 5 s windows, two runs. Arms: shipped; sheen dropped through an own-property override on `documentElement.style` (a different mechanism from the investigator's prototype patch); all blur off; and `--sheen-x` registered with `inherits: false`. Saw 35-37 writes per 5 s in F260, each one `UpdateLayoutTree` over 5,572 elements; style 99-100 ms a second and p95 24-25 ms shipped, 0 ms and p95 17 ms with the sheen dropped; blur off and the registered property both left the drops in place.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate script (arms A, C, R in the order A C R A C R, 4 s windows) plus a forced-style micro-benchmark in Chromium and WebKit. Saw F260 style 97-101 ms a second vs 0, main 0.158-0.171 vs 0.048-0.058, 8.9-9.6 % of frames over 20 ms vs 0; Home and Prayer at 60 fps either way with main-thread time 3-4× higher shipped; the registered property gave 105-109 ms a second; and the whole-document restyle in WebKit as well.
  - **Re-measure:** agrees on direction and size (36-61 % CPU cut, main 2.3-4.1×, F260 drops with the sheen and not without). It disagrees on two draft figures, both corrected here: F260's sheen-off frames are 4.2 % over 20 ms, not 0 %, and the recalc range is 7-58 a second, not 15-58.
- **Corrected claim.** Each `--sheen-x` write on `<html>` restyles the whole document, in both engines. Dropping only those writes removes every scroll-time recalc and cuts scroll CPU 31-61 % and main-thread time 2.0-4.1×. The frame drops reproduce only in F260, the large document: p95 24-32.5 ms and 8-14 % of frames over 20 ms, against 17-18 ms and 0-4 % without the sheen. F260 has one sheen-painted pill (no blur), not "no glass". Registering `--sheen-x` as a non-inherited `@property` on `<html>` does not help in Chromium; the fix must keep the changing value off `<html>`. "Costs more than all the blur" holds on desktop Chromium; on the iPad, Core Animation composites the blur on the GPU, which the rig cannot measure.
- **Related (not re-filed).** P2-STAB-01 is the Reduce Motion crash in the same IIFE's `sheenFrom` call path, not its cost. No P2 or P3 item records the restyle.

title: The perf guard keys on the class pair `.card.glass`, so `.card.glass-strong` keeps a live blur in a scrolling page, and `.glass-lite` is used nowhere
block:
#### P4-GLASS-02 — The perf guard keys on the class pair `.card.glass`, so `.card.glass-strong` keeps a live blur in a scrolling page, and `.glass-lite` is used nowhere

- **Severity: low.** The two confirming skeptics rated it low; the refuting skeptic rated it info as a duplicate.
  - **Clause:** cost and consistency. No data, account or usability impact; whether the blurred card makes an iPad stutter needs a device.
  - **Exposure:** adults in Verses, whose trainer page scrolls. The gate's pairing form and PIN pad also keep the blur, but the gate never scrolls, so the guard's rationale does not apply there.
  - **Narrowed:** the tie-break skeptic confirmed it as a design-system gap rather than a bug, with areas narrowed to design.css and Verses. It keeps a P4 ID because the guard's own trigger (a live-blur card in a page that scrolls) is met.
- **Kind:** bug (the rule is scoped by class name, not role); reads as a design-system gap.
- **Areas:** shell (design.css), Verses. Related only: Kid Verse, Timer, Tally.
- **What happens.**
  - **The guard.** `.ds .card.glass { backdrop-filter: none }` (`apps/design.css:400`), commented "in-page cards paint the look without blurring what scrolls under them (blur in a scroller is what makes iPad glass stutter)" (`:399`). The escape hatch `.ds .glass-lite` (`:401`) is documented in CLAUDE.md ("use `.glass-lite` for the same on anything else").
  - **The control matrix** (skeptics 1 and 3, both documents): `card glass` → none; `card glass-strong` → `blur(18px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.02)`; `card glass-strong glass-lite` → none. The rule follows one class pair; the hatch works but has 0 users.
  - **Where it bites.** The Verses `#trainer` and `#done` are `.card.glass-strong` (`apps/verses.html:103, 119`). As Eli the document scrolls (1,988 px in a 692 px viewport on iPhone, 1,920 in 772 on iPad; a 200 px scroll attempt moved 200), so a live-blur card sits in exactly the page the guard exists for. The trainer measures 398×448 on iPhone and 688×380 on iPad. For Ezra the page does not scroll.
  - **Where it does not bite.** `#pairform` (`index.html:501`; 398×345 iPhone, 440×345 iPad) and `.pin-wrap` (`index.html:553`; 380×635) are `.card.glass-strong` with a live blur, but `#gate` never scrolls on iPhone Safari, iPhone PWA, iPad or desktop, and the card sits over the fixed welcome art. They are single static panes, outside the guard's rationale.
  - **Not guard misses.** Kid Verse's `.scene`, Timer's `#dial` and Tally's `.dial` are not `.card` (Tally's dial is hand-made glass, `apps/tally.html:45-51`), so no `.card` guard could reach them. They are VIS-KIDVERSE-8, VIS-TIMER-6 and VIS-TALLY-9.
- **Expected.** The guard follows the role: any recipe class on a `.card`, or any recipe surface inside a scroller, paints the look with no blur, and look-only content uses one class that apps actually adopt.
- **Why it matters.** The rule that should keep content cheap is one class name away from failing, and it fails on the Verses card. Every future card that picks `glass-strong` for its denser fill silently gets a live blur.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:388, 399-401`; `index.html:501, 553`; `apps/verses.html:103, 119`; grep: `glass-lite` 0 in `index.html` and `apps/*.html`, 1 in design.css.
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/layers.json` (`areas.shell.elements` pin-wrap and pairform, `areas.verses.elements` trainer and done).
  - Skeptics: `verify-guard-misses-glass-strong-1.json`, `-1-pairform-ipad.png`, `verify-guard-misses-glass-strong-2.json`, `verify-guard-misses-glass-strong-3.json`.
- **Reproduction.** `grep -n "card.glass\b\|glass-lite" apps/design.css; grep -c glass-lite index.html apps/*.html`; then `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/verify-guard-misses-glass-strong-3.mjs"` (control matrix, surfaces, scroll test).
- **Verified: 2 of 3 skeptics confirmed (tie-break).**
  - **Skeptic 1 (confirmed, low)** ran WebKit on iPad portrait and iPhone PWA over the gate, the PIN pad, Verses as Eli and Ezra, Timer, Tally and Kid Verse, reading each computed filter and size and injecting control elements. Saw the class-pair behaviour in every document, every surface live, and 0 `.glass-lite` in any DOM. Corrected the PIN pad to 380×635 and noted that the gate and the app bodies do not overflow at these sizes.
  - **Skeptic 2 (refuted, info)** ran WebKit on four devices, checking the guard match, real overflow and what sits behind each card. Found the gate never scrolls and the welcome art sits behind the card on 7 of 8 pairs. Judged the Verses and PIN-pad facets duplicates of VIS-VERSES-2 and `audits/02-shell.md:5867-5871`, and the rest an adoption note.
  - **Skeptic 3 (tie-break, confirmed, low)** re-ran the control matrix in the shell and the Verses frame, and measured scrolling. Found the Verses document does scroll for adults (the guard's trigger), which skeptic 2 had not tested, while the gate does not. Confirmed it as one narrowed cross-area item.
- **Corrected claim.** The guard is keyed to `.card.glass` (`apps/design.css:400`), not to the surface's role, and `.glass-lite` has 0 uses. The case that meets the guard's own trigger is the adult Verses trainer and done cards: a live `blur(18px)` in a document that scrolls. That instance is VIS-VERSES-2; the new facts are the class-bound rule across the system, the unused hatch and the scroll measurement. The pairing form and PIN pad are live blurs in a gate that never scrolls. Sizes depend on state: `.pin-wrap` measured 380×635 in all three skeptics' runs (the dataset's largest was 380×658); the trainer 688×380 on iPad in their runs (442 in the dataset's largest); the `#done` size (688×326) was not re-measured.
- **Related (not re-filed).** VIS-VERSES-2 (`audits/03-apps/verses.md:545`); the PIN pad in Phase 2's unnumbered "VIS — Liquid Glass on content" (`audits/02-shell.md:5867`); VIS-KIDVERSE-8, VIS-TIMER-6, VIS-TALLY-9.

title: Three live blurs sit under fills that hide them: Prayer's FAB, the park map's north button and the build guide's steps sheet
block:
#### P4-GLASS-03 — Three live blurs sit under fills that hide them: Prayer's FAB, the park map's north button and the build guide's steps sheet

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** cost, plus one cosmetic facet (the north button renders solid next to glass siblings). No flow, data or contrast is involved.
  - **Exposure:** Prayer's FAB on every Prayer screen; the north button on the park map and on the build guide at 700 px and wider (hidden below, `template.html:352`); the steps sheet on phones only.
- **Kind:** perf, with a visual facet.
- **Areas:** Prayer, park map, build guide.
- **What happens.**
  - **Prayer's FAB.** It shares the copied recipe selector `nav,.sheet,.fab,#kitchen .close` (`apps/prayer.html:285-297`), so it gets `blur(18px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.02)`, but `.fab { --g: var(--accent-deep) }` (`:300`) makes the fill opaque (light `color(srgb .223 .263 .395)`, dark `.600 .632 .738`, alpha 1). Removing only its blur changed 0 of 3,136 pixels (max diff 1-2) on iPhone and iPad, light and dark, while the nav beside it changed 1,696-5,296 pixels. The solid accent button is intended; the blur is a leftover.
  - **The north button.** `.lv-north` asks for the glass fill `var(--lv-glass-soft)` with `backdrop-filter: var(--lv-blur)` (`template.html:417`, specificity 0,1,0). The generic reset `[data-flavor=hub] button, … [data-flavor=live] button { background: var(--panel) }` (`:224`, 0,1,1) wins, so the fill computes to the solid surface (`rgb(255,252,248)` / `rgb(36,30,25)`, alpha 1) and the blur is wasted. The sibling `.fab` buttons beat the reset with `!important` (`:409`) and stay glass (`#lv-fit` and `#loc-btn` at alpha .62-.66). Inside the disc, removing the blur changes nothing but a 1 px re-raster of the rotated needle.
  - **The build guide's steps sheet.** On phones `.build` is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface) 96%, transparent)` over a live `var(--lv-blur)` (`template.html:359`, inside `@media (max-width: 699px)` from `:313`). Fully open it covers 430×824 (354,320 px²) on iPhone. About 4 % of the blurred map shows through: removing the blur changes 6.2-6.5 % of its pixels by at most 8-9/255. The solid sheet is intended (commit fe6041d, "solid steps sheet"); the blur was left behind.
- **Expected.** No `backdrop-filter` on an element whose fill is opaque or near-opaque. The north button either gets its glass fill back (so the blur has a job) or drops the blur.
- **Why it matters.** Pure cost with no look, and the steps sheet is the largest glass layer on the iPhone build guide. The north button also looks different from the glass buttons next to it for a reason nobody chose.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/prayer.html:285-297, 300, 303-305`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:215, 224, 313, 352, 359, 409, 417`.
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/opaque-blur.json` (`opaque[]`: `div#build.build` alpha 0.96, `maxVisArea` 354320; `button#fab.fab.on` alpha 1; `button#lv-north.lv-north` alpha 1; every other live layer in `all[]` is .42-.94).
  - Skeptics: `verify-opaque-fill-under-blur-1-chromium.json`, `-1-webkit.json`, `-1-chromium-subset.json`, `-1-chromium-light-dollywood-live-ipad-portrait-lv-north-{shipped,noblur}.png`, `-1-chromium-light-dollywood-iphone-pwa-build-{shipped,noblur}.png`; `verify-opaque-fill-under-blur-2.json`.
- **Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/opaque-blur.mjs"` (every live layer with the alpha range of its computed background); `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/verify-opaque-fill-under-blur-1.mjs" --engine chromium` (per-element blur-off pixel diff with a translucent control).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran WebKit and Chromium, iPhone PWA and iPad portrait, light and dark. For each target it read the computed fill, filter and matching rules, then took shipped, shipped-again and blur-off element screenshots and diffed them against a translucent control. Saw 0 changed pixels in the FAB and in the north disc, 6.2-6.5 % on the steps sheet, and found the `:224` vs `:417` specificity cause. WebKit's pixel arm was inconclusive (it paints no blur), its computed styles matched.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate WebKit probe (fills, filters, rects and every matching background rule; the steps sheet opened with two handle taps). Confirmed all three, the phone-only scope of the sheet rule, the specificity cause, and the intent behind the solid FAB and sheet.
  - **Re-measure:** the alphas agree exactly in both engines. It saw the steps sheet collapsed (430×118), so it did not reproduce the 354,320 px² area.
- **Corrected claim.** Prayer's FAB and the park map's north button run a live 18 px blur that adds nothing visible (0 changed pixels in the fill). The north button's solid fill is a specificity accident (`template.html:224` beats `:417`), not a design choice, so it also loses its glass look. The build guide's 96 % steps sheet on phones lets about 4 % of the blurred map through: near-invisible, not "never seen". Fixes for the Dollywood pair go in the sibling template.
- **Related (not re-filed).** VIS-DOLLYWOOD-6 is about glass that is too transparent, a different facet. `audits/03-apps/dollywood-live.md:358` and `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:425` cover the north button's behaviour, not its fill.

title: The TV board's only on-screen live blur is the Switch button, against the board's own no-blur rule
block:
#### P4-GLASS-04 — The TV board's only on-screen live blur is the Switch button, against the board's own no-blur rule

- **Severity: low.** The two confirming skeptics rated it low; the refuting skeptic rated it info.
  - **Clause:** cost and consistency on the always-on display, at a small size. Nothing breaks.
  - **Exposure:** every TV board, all day and night; also a kiosk iPad in landscape.
- **Kind:** perf and consistency.
- **Areas:** TV, shell.
- **What happens.**
  - **The rule.** The board's panes drop `backdrop-filter` on purpose: "the panes keep the glass recipe but drop backdrop-filter (the photo is already blurred, and a display runs 24 h)" (`index.html:125-127`, `:137`).
  - **The exception.** The Switch inside the hero pane is `class="btn btn-glass kiosk-switch"` (`index.html:1121`), so it keeps the recipe's live blur at the kiosk's `--blur: 28px` (`apps/design.css:285-288`), at opacity .7 (`index.html:104`). It is 107×44 at (612, 37) on the 1920×1080 board. It shares the hero pane with the clock, which is rewritten once a second; it sits directly above the clock glyphs rather than over them.
  - **The other blur.** The pull-to-refresh `#ptr` span (`index.html:376`) also computes a blur, parked off-screen at y = −56.
  - **The cost** (Table GLASS-4) is small and its size disputed: between crossfades the investigator measured +37 % (0.048 vs 0.035 cores) and the re-measure +44 % (0.075 vs 0.052); the skeptics, turning off only the Switch's blur, measured −2 %, +9 % and +6.7 % on the 1920 board (within noise) and +14-18 % on iPad landscape, where skeptic 3's 12 paired rounds gave GPU +16 % with a 95 % CI that excludes zero. The absolute difference is about 0.003 cores in the best-controlled runs.
- **Expected.** The Switch follows the board's look-only rule (`backdrop-filter: none`) like the panes around it.
- **Why it matters.** The TV runs all day. One small button is the only thing on the board keeping a live blur recomputed as the clock ticks beside it, against a rule the same file states.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `index.html:104, 125-127, 137, 376, 1121`; `apps/design.css:285-288, 388-396`.
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/perf.json` (`scenes.tv-board.arms.still` A 0.048, B 0.035; `scenes.tv-board.arms.fade`; `scenes.tv-board-ipad.arms.fade`); `layers.json` `areas.tv`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-tv-switch-live-blur-1-{tv-still,tv-fade,ipad-landscape-fade}.json`; `verify-tv-switch-live-blur-2.json`, `-2-tv.json`, `-2-ipad.json`, `-2-tv.png`; `verify-tv-switch-live-blur-3-tv.json`, `-3-ipad-landscape.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-perf-picker_tv_dlive.json`.
- **Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/verify-tv-switch-live-blur-3.mjs"` (arms A, S = Switch blur off, A2 = null control, ABBA over 13 rounds, windows 3.5 s after a forced crossfade).
- **Verified: 2 of 3 skeptics confirmed (tie-break).**
  - **Skeptic 1 (refuted, info)** isolated the Switch (arm S), added a null arm and ran 8 still reps and 5-6 crossfade reps on the TV and iPad landscape. Confirmed every code fact, but the cost did not reproduce: 0.0427 vs 0.0436 still, +5 % on crossfades, GPU about +8 %. Traced the +37 % to one 0.056 outlier in the investigator's two runs.
  - **Skeptic 2 (confirmed, low)** compared five arms over six rounds on both devices (A, S, `#ptr` only, both, all off). Saw A highest and S close to all-off: +9 % on the TV and +18 % on iPad landscape, at the noise floor.
  - **Skeptic 3 (tie-break, confirmed, low)** ran 12 clean paired rounds per device with an in-run null control and t-based 95 % CIs. TV: +0.0028 cores (+6.7 %), CI includes zero. iPad landscape: +0.0040 (+14 %), GPU +0.0033 (+16 %) with a CI of [+0.0014, +0.0052] while the control's GPU CI sat around zero.
  - **Re-measure:** 0.075 vs 0.052 still (+44 %) and +6 % with a crossfade, with about 50 % higher absolute CPU (machine load). It agrees with the investigator's ratio; the paired skeptic designs do not.
- **Corrected claim.** The Switch (`index.html:1121`) is the only on-screen element on the board with a live `backdrop-filter`, `blur(28px)` at opacity .7, inside panes that drop theirs for a 24 h display. That inconsistency is exact. Its idle cost is small: about +0.003 cores, statistically real on the iPad-landscape GPU (+16 %) and within noise on the 1920 board. The investigator's +37 % and the re-measure's +44 % come from short, few-run windows; the paired runs with a null control give +7-16 %. "Only live blur" should read "only on-screen live blur", and "over the ticking clock" should read "in the clock's pane".
- **Related (not re-filed).** P2-STAB-11 (the hidden board keeps running after Switch) is a different defect. Phase 2 noted only the Switch's opacity (`audits/02-shell.md:6076`).

title: Tally's five content-glass layers add 8-31 % to a burst of + taps, for a blur nobody can see
block:
#### P4-GLASS-05 — Tally's five content-glass layers add 8-31 % to a burst of + taps, for a blur nobody can see

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low, at the edge of info.
  - **Clause:** cost only, during a tap burst; nothing at idle, no dropped frames, no broken flow.
  - **Exposure:** anyone tapping + rapidly in Tally; kids most of all.
- **Kind:** perf (a measured facet of VIS-TALLY-9).
- **Areas:** Tally.
- **What happens.**
  - **The layers.** Tally's dial, +, −, Reset and the who kicker are all live glass (`apps/tally.html:45-51, 73-79, 98-104`), plus the shell's viewer bar: 6 visible layers, all `blur(18px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.02)`. The author accepted it on purpose: "Not inside a scroller, so backdrop-filter is fine" (`:95-97`).
  - **The backdrop.** Behind them is only the body's radial gradient wash (`background-attachment: fixed`); none overlaps the art watermark. The panes are fairly opaque (.84 on the dial, .66 on the buttons). Blur on vs off differs by a mean 2.4/255 over the dial and buttons, with 0.6 % of pixels differing by more than 10.
  - **The cost.** Each tap runs the pressed button's `scale(.94)` and box-shadow transition (`:80-82`), and the other blurred layers are recomposited while it animates. Glass on vs all blur off, for + tapped every 450 ms for 5 s: +26-31 % in both skeptics' runs, +21 % in the re-measure with Playwright `tap()`, +8-9 % with raw mouse clicks, +52 % in the investigator's single run (Table GLASS-4). The GPU gap (0.134 vs 0.074 in the investigator's run, about 0.10 vs 0.07 in the skeptics') did not appear in the re-measure (0.013-0.017 in both arms).
  - **What drives it.** Turning off only the two buttons' own blur saves almost nothing (0.152 vs 0.161). Turning off the press transition cuts the burst to 0.057-0.061 cores with glass still on, after which glass adds about 0.005-0.01.
- **Expected.** The content dial is solid, and controls over a static wash carry the look without a live blur (`.glass-lite` or a solid control fill).
- **Why it matters.** Kids tap + fast. On the iPad each tap pays to re-blur a flat wash that looks the same with or without the blur.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/tally.html:45-51, 73-79, 80-82, 95-104, 85, 112`.
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/perf.json` (`scenes.tally-kid.arms.taps` A 0.218, B 0.143; `arms.idle` 0.005 / 0.006).
  - Skeptics: `verify-tally-taps-glass-cost-1.json`, `-1-extra.json`; `verify-tally-taps-glass-cost-2.json`, `-2-A.png`, `-2-B.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-perf-tally.json`, `remeasure-perf-leftovers_kidverse_verses_tally.json`.
- **Reproduction.** `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/verify-tally-taps-glass-cost-2.mjs"` (arms A, B, T = button blur off, X = press transform off, N = both; four interleaved rounds).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran six arms over three rounds in Chromium as Ezra on iPad portrait (shipped; all blur off; frame blur off; press animation off; `#plus` blur off; animation and blur off), with CPU per process from CDP. Saw 0.158-0.169 vs 0.123-0.129 (+26-31 %), the shell's layers adding nothing, `#plus`'s own blur about 4 %, and the press animation the largest cost (0.061 with glass on). Count went 12 → 142 over 130 taps, so every tap landed.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate script (five arms, four rounds, order reversed on odd rounds), listed the live layers and what sits behind them, and diffed the pixels. Saw 0.161 vs 0.128 (+26 %, A above B in 4 of 4 rounds), 0.057 vs 0.052 with the press transform off, and a 2.43/255 mean pixel difference.
  - **Re-measure: disagrees on size.** 0.040-0.049 vs 0.037-0.045 (+8-9 %) with raw input, 0.076 vs 0.063 (+21 %) with the investigator's `tap()` method, and 24 vs 9-12 style recalcs a second between the investigator's session and its own, which points to extra work in that session (actionability polling or parallel browsers).
- **Corrected claim.** The glass premium on a Tally tap burst is real in direction but small and input-dependent: +8 % to +31 % across three independent measurements, not +52 %, and at most a few hundredths of a core. It comes from the other blurred layers being recomposited while the pressed button animates, not from the pressed button re-blurring itself, and the press transition costs more than the glass does. The blur over Tally's flat wash is nearly invisible (2.4/255). The recommendation stands; the size does not.
- **Related (not re-filed).** VIS-TALLY-9 (`audits/03-apps/tally.md:561`) owns the five content layers and the flat backdrop; only the measurement is new.

title: The glass recipe is re-typed 17 times in 5 source files, in three filter variants (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-GLASS-1 — The glass recipe is re-typed 17 times in 5 source files, in three filter variants (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.** Only the shell, Kid Verse, Verses and Timer use the shared classes. The gradient is copied by F260 3 times (`apps/f260.html:58, 385, 422`), Tally 3 (`apps/tally.html:46, 74, 99`), Prayer 1 block (`apps/prayer.html:285-297`), the Larder 1 (`apps/leftovers.html:38`) and the Dollywood template 9 per export (`template.html:215, 287, 290, …`). Timer restates the shadow stack (`apps/timer.html:36`).
- **Variants.** The filter appears as the full recipe, as `blur saturate(1.4)` without `brightness` (template `:298` menus, `:322` toolbar) and as `blur` only (`:299` map hint). Blur literals: `10px` (the toast, `apps/design.css:591`), `6px` (Prayer's veil, `apps/prayer.html:234-235`, and the park map's scale, `template.html:420`). A literal dark glass: `rgba(10,8,6,.42)` (`template.html:420`). F260 and the template have no `@supports not` fallback (Table GLASS-2).
- **The model already exists.** The template's local `--lv-glass`, `--lv-glass-soft`, `--lv-blur` and `--lv-glass-shadow` (`template.html:215`) are the only composite glass tokens in the codebase (Table TOK-F lists them too).
- **Expected.** The recipe is a small set of design.css tokens (or classes) that every area, including those without `.ds`, uses through `var()`.
- **Why it matters.** The next recipe change (reduced transparency, contrast, the sheen fix) has to be made in about 17 places, and the variants already disagree.
- **Evidence:** `audits/evidence/p4/GLASS/remeasure-code.json` (counts exact: f260 3, tally 3, prayer 1, leftovers 1, dollywood.html 9, dollywood-live.html 9; design.css 1).
- **Reproduction:** `for f in index.html apps/*.html; do echo $f $(grep -o 'var(--glass-spec)' $f | wc -l) $(grep -o 'saturate(1.4)' $f | wc -l); done`.
- **Related:** VIS-TALLY-9 (Tally's three copies); CONS-TOK-1 and Table TOK-F (local token vocabularies, 25 filter declarations).

title: Five areas put live glass on content in most screens, four keep it on the control layer, and Phase 3 scored both groups the same (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-GLASS-2 — Five areas put live glass on content in most screens, four keep it on the control layer, and Phase 3 scored both groups the same (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens** (Table GLASS-1, share of each area's screens with a visible live blur on content): Tally 100 % (dial, +, −, Reset), Kid Verse 100 % (scene card, Read buttons), Verses 89 % (trainer and done cards), Timer 87 % (the dial), the build guide 48 % (exaggeration control, north button). F260, the Larder, Prayer and the park map: 0 %.
- **Corrected from the draft.** The draft counted six areas, adding the TV (85 %) and the shell (37 %). The TV's share is entirely the TV picker's cards and the Switch, and the shell's includes the 9 picker cards; the house style names "the profile switcher" as a glass surface and the Switch is a control, so these shares mostly measure the rig's heuristic. The shell still has content glass in chat bubbles, the PIN pad card, the pairing form and the album × buttons (Phase 2, `audits/02-shell.md:5867`).
- **Scores.** Phase 3 gave Shape, depth & material 5 to all nine apps except the park map's 6 (`audits/03-apps.md:51-62`), so the four apps that place glass correctly scored the same as the five that do not.
- **Expected.** Content cards stay solid everywhere; glass stays on tab bars, toolbars, floating buttons, sheets and the profile switcher.
- **Why it matters.** In four apps glass means "this floats and controls"; in five it means "anything", so it stops telling the family what can be tapped.

title: The sheen's tilt drift never runs on iPad or iPhone (investigator rating: info)
block:
#### CONS-GLASS-3 — The sheen's tilt drift never runs on iPad or iPhone (investigator rating: info)

- **What happens.** hub.js registers the `deviceorientation` listener only when `DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission` is not a function (`apps/hub.js:449`). iOS and iPadOS Safari define that function, so on the target devices the sheen follows scroll only. CLAUDE.md says the sheen "drifts with scroll/tilt".
- **Expected.** Either document scroll-only, or ask for motion permission once from a user gesture (for example in Me).
- **Why it matters.** Minor, but the documented behaviour is not what the family's devices do. If the drift is kept, P4-GLASS-01 should be fixed first.
- **Evidence:** `apps/hub.js:449-451`; CLAUDE.md "Liquid glass". Not run on a device.

title: Glass on glass: the park map's ride card nests three live blurs, and Prayer's sheet blurs over a blurred full-screen veil (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### VIS-GLASS-1 — Glass on glass: the park map's ride card nests three live blurs, and Prayer's sheet blurs over a blurred full-screen veil (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - The park map's ride and coaster card `.pop` is live glass (`template.html:451`), and its sticky `.pop-head` and `.pop-act` are each live glass inside it (`:483`, `:486`): three nested layers (`perf.json` `scenes.dlive-ride-card.layers`: `#pop` 796×364, `pop-head` 794×70, `pop-act` 794×62). The coaster card on desktop covers 1,211,278 px², 93 % of the viewport (`layers.json` `areas.dollywood-live.heaviest[0]`).
  - Prayer's detail sheet (live `blur(18px)`) sits on `#veil`, a full-viewport `blur(6px)` scrim (`apps/prayer.html:234-235`), so the screen carries 1.71 viewports of blur (`layers.json` `areas.prayer.areaShare.max`).
- **Expected.** One glass layer over content: the card is one pane with look-only sticky rows, and the sheet's scrim is a plain `--scrim` without blur.
- **Why it matters.** Nested blurs muddy what is under them and multiply the cost on the screens families use at the park and in prayer.
- **Reproduction:** `node "audits/tools/phase4/GLASS/layers.mjs"`, then read `areas.dollywood-live.elements` (pop, pop-head, pop-act) and `areas.prayer.elements` (veil 1440×852 and sheet 1440×750).

title: The app viewer's bar is live glass in every app, but nothing ever passes beneath it (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### VIS-GLASS-2 — The app viewer's bar is live glass in every app, but nothing ever passes beneath it (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.** `#pill.topbar` (`index.html:407`) is the bar above every app: 1440×48 on desktop, live blur on every app screen (`layers.json`: page `div#pill.topbar` in every app area). It is a `flex: none` child above `#frame` in `#viewer`'s column (`index.html:326, 332, 334`), over `#viewer`'s flat `var(--bg)`, and the app scrolls inside the iframe below it. The blur only ever sees a solid colour. The comment at `index.html:333` states the choice: "a slim glass bar above the app, never over it — apps keep their own bottom navigation free". The desktop sidebar is the same: `#views` is padded 220 px past it (`index.html:83`).
- **Expected (house style).** Glass floats with content visibly scrolling beneath it, as in iOS 26 toolbars (the frame runs under the bar with a top inset), or the bar is a solid toolbar with no blur.
- **Why it matters.** It is the one piece of glass seen in every app, and it reads as a flat strip, not floating glass, while paying for a blur.
- **Reproduction:** `grep -n "#viewer {\|#frame {\|#pill {" index.html`.
