title: The selected tab, Prayer nav item and Timer preset are marked only by a 1.0-1.35:1 fill and a shift in hue: for David in the dark palettes and Kiara in the light ones, the selected tab's label differs from its neighbours by 1.02-1.08:1
block:
#### P4-ACCENT-01 — The selected tab, Prayer nav item and Timer preset are marked only by a 1.0-1.35:1 fill and a shift in hue: for David in the dark palettes and Kiara in the light ones, the selected tab's label differs from its neighbours by 1.02-1.08:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** a measurable accessibility failure on the primary navigation.
    - The only indicator of the current section is non-text below 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
    - The selected and idle colours differ by less than 3:1, with no second cue (1.4.1).
  - **Why not high:**
    - The page content and the tab's position still show where you are.
    - The label text itself passes (4.70+).
    - `aria-current` is set (`index.html:640`; Prayer's `aria-current="true"`), so VoiceOver announces the state.
  - **Exposure:** every person, in every theme, on every screen with the tab bar or Prayer's nav. The kiosk hides the tab bar (`index.html:78`). The worst cases are David in System dark, Midnight and Forest (1.05-1.08; System is Midnight at night), and Kiara in Hearth, Parchment and Frost (1.02-1.06).
- **Areas:** shell (the tab bar, and the desktop sidebar, which uses the same classes), prayer (bottom nav), timer (presets). The park map's sheet tabs are a weaker form: the fill is 1.12-1.30, but the label also changes luminance.
- **What happens.** In each component, selection changes only the ink hue and adds an `--accent-soft` fill:
  - **Tab bar.**
    - `.ds .tab` is `--muted` at weight 600 (`apps/design.css:559-560`), and `.tab.on` changes only the colour, to `--accent-deep` (`:564`).
    - The indicator `.tab-ind` is `--accent-soft`, 14 % of the accent into `--surface` (`:566-567`, `:87`).
    - The icon is the same `<use>` in both states (`index.html:396-399`), and `showTab` toggles only `.on` and `aria-current` (`:640`).
  - **Prayer nav.** `nav button` is `--muted` at 600; the current item gets `--accent-deep` on `--accent-soft` (`apps/prayer.html:276-281`).
  - **Timer presets.** `.presets .btn.on` gets an `--accent-soft` fill, a 45 % accent border and `--accent-deep` ink (`apps/timer.html:44`).
  - **Park sheet tabs.** An 18 % accent fill, the label changed from `--dim` to `--text`, and the icon in the raw accent (template `:428-429`).
  - **Measured** (skeptics, rendered):

    | Component | Fill against its neighbours or bar | Selected ÷ idle ink | Other cue | Below 3:1 |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | Tab bar | 1.09-1.25 (token 1.10-1.24, 56/56) | 1.02-2.03 (Table ACCENT-5) | none: weight 600, same icon | 49/49 and 42/42 |
    | Prayer nav, personal list | 1.11-1.23 | 1.05-2.03 (David dark 1.05-1.06) | none | 35/35 and 30/30 |
    | Prayer nav, Family list (`--teal-soft`) | 1.03-1.04 (runtime, heuristic) | teal, the same for everyone | none | — |
    | Timer preset `.on` | 1.09-1.24 against the idle chips (skeptic 2); 1.00-1.35 against the page, Kiara in Parchment 1.00 (skeptic 1) | 1.15-2.70 | a 45 % accent border, 1.10-1.58 (skeptic 1; skeptic 2 read 1.00-1.35) | 49/49 and 42/42 |
    | Park sheet tab | 1.12-1.30 | label `--dim` → `--text`: 2.75 light, 1.62 dark | raw-accent icon (P4-COLOR-02) | fill only |

- **Expected.** A selected state that can be seen without hue: an indicator of at least 3:1 against the bar or card, or a second cue such as weight, a filled icon or an underline. The house style asks for "Hierarchy through weight and size, not color alone" (`audits/HUB-AUDIT-PROMPT.md:50`) and says "Never rely on hue alone" (`:71-73`).
- **Why it matters.**
  - The tab bar is the navigation on every screen for every person.
  - A colour-blind adult, someone reading the kitchen iPad across the room, or a pre-reader relying on shape cannot tell which tab is current.
  - For David in dark, the selected and idle inks are also almost the same hue for a deuteranope (ΔE00 1.43), so neither luminance nor hue separates them.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:87, 559-567`; `index.html:78, 396-399, 640`; `apps/prayer.html:276-281`; `apps/timer.html:44`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:428-429` (read-only).
  - Investigator: `tokens.json` (`selection.rows`), `runtime-summary.json` (timer presets 84/84; Prayer nav 56/56 and 35/35), `tabbar-selected-dad-kiara.png`.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-selection-by-hue-only-1.json`, `-1-park.json`, `-1-shots.json`, `-1-system-dark-dad-shell.png`, `-1-system-light-kiara-shell.png`
    - `verify-selection-by-hue-only-2-{shell,timer,prayer}.json`, `-2-shell-dad-system-dark.png`, `-2-timer-kiara-parchment.png`
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-tokens.json` (indicator 56/56; ink 1.02-2.17 over 11 colours; David dark 1.06, deuteranopia ΔE00 1.43).
- **Reproduction.** All from `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/tokens.mjs --selection` prints the David row at 1.06 in the dark columns.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-selection-by-hue-only-1.mjs --themes system-dark,system-light --profiles dad,kiara --areas shell` prints `inkRatio` 1.05 (David, dark) and 1.06 (Kiara, light), with `pillVsBar` 1.11-1.13 and `weightOn` = `weightOff` = 600.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-selection-by-hue-only-2.mjs timer parchment kiara` records the selected "5 min" chip's painted fill as rgb(232,217,184), against the page at rgb(231,217,190) (about 1.00:1) and the idle chips at rgb(241,231,210). All are at weight 600.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read `design.css:560-567`, `index.html:640`, `prayer.html:281`, `timer.html:44` and template `:428-429`. They then wrote their own WebKit script on the iPhone PWA, setting each theme through `PUT /api/data/hub/theme` and localStorage and checking `data-theme` and `data-scheme`. It sampled 5 × 5 pixel medians at CSS scale, over 7 profiles × 7 keys for the shell and the Timer, 5 adults × 7 for Prayer, and a park pass.
    - The tab bar was below 3:1 in 49/49 cases (pill 1.11-1.24; ink 1.02-2.03; weight 600 in both states), the Timer in 49/49, Prayer in 35/35.
    - They found that the park tab's label changes luminance (2.75 light, 1.62 dark).
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate WebKit script on the iPad portrait. It recorded ink, weight, size, icon href and fill for the selected item and every sibling, then hid text and icons to sample the painted fill. It covered the tab bar (42 cases), the Timer (42) and Prayer (30), all below 3:1: pill 1.09-1.25, ink 1.02-2.03, identical weight, size and icon.
    - They found that the kiosk has no tab bar (`index.html:78`).
    - They checked P2 and P3 for duplicates and found none. VIS-TIMER-3 covers the chip's text contrast, not whether the state can be seen.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **The TV is dropped.** The kiosk hides the tab bar, so the "TV 1.02-1.04 in dark" figure describes no rendered surface.
  - **The rendered ink range is 1.02-2.03.** The draft's upper 2.17 is the TV colour and the swatches in token maths.
  - **Prayer's personal-list nav fill is 1.11-1.23.** The draft's 1.03-1.17 mixed in the Family list's teal fill.
  - **The park sheet tab is not hue only:** its label changes luminance, though still below 3:1.
  - **The Timer attribution:** the two skeptics sampled the fill and the border differently, and both are below 3:1.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - VIS-TIMER-3: the selected chip's text contrast.
  - U-TOK-1 (Tokens section): whether the tab bar meets 1.4.11, given that the label also changes colour. This defect settles it: it does not, because that label change is only 1.02-2.03:1.

title: The raw profile colour is used as small text in Prayer's Kitchen headings and the park map's walk times and distances; no single hex can pass in both schemes, so it fails for every adult in one scheme or the other
block:
#### P4-ACCENT-02 — The raw profile colour is used as small text in Prayer's Kitchen headings and the park map's walk times and distances; no single hex can pass in both schemes, so it fails for every adult in one scheme or the other

> **Pointer (merged at assembly) → P4-COLOR-02**, which owns the defect and its medium severity. This entry keeps the per-adult matrices, the proof that no single hex passes on both schemes, and the Kitchen heading measured on `--bg`.

- **Merge note.** This is the same defect as **P4-COLOR-02** (Colour section): the same rules and the same cause. Phase 5 should keep P4-COLOR-02 as the single ID. This entry adds:
  - the per-adult matrix (Tables ACCENT-4 and ACCENT-6);
  - the proof that no single hex can pass in both schemes;
  - the correct pair for the Kitchen headings, `--bg` (29/35 adult cells);
  - dropping the Prayer-initials facet.
- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** text a household member needs, below AA on a primary surface. That means the Kitchen view's section headings, and the park map's walk times and distances.
  - **Why not high:** these are secondary labels. Request titles, the ride name, the wait and the primary buttons use passing tokens (`--ink`, `--text`, `--accent-deep`).
  - **Exposure:**
    - The Kitchen view on adults' personal lists. On the Family list, `body.shared` rebinds `--accent` to teal (`apps/prayer.html:39`), and kids and the kiosk have no personal list.
    - The park map text on park days.
- **Areas:** prayer, dollywood-live (from the sibling template).
- **What happens.**
  - **The raw hex.** `apps/hub.js:80` sets `--accent` to the profile's raw hex in every scheme, and three text rules paint it:
    - `#kitchen .k-cat`: 13.5 px, weight 700, on `--bg` (`apps/prayer.html:359`);
    - `.lv-item .d small`, "under a minute": 11.5 px, weight 600, on the sheet's `--surface` (template `:440`);
    - `.lv-from b`, "110 ft from you": 13.5 px bold on an 18 % accent chip over the ride card (template `:524`).
    - P4-COLOR-02 also lists the mic icon (`:387`), the park tab icon (`:429`) and the route glyph (`:464`).
  - **Why no single hex can work** (skeptic 1).
    - For 4.5:1 on the Hearth card #FFFCF8, the ink's relative luminance must be at most 0.178.
    - For 4.5:1 on the Midnight page #1A1512, it must be at least 0.211.
    - The cap is below the floor. So any colour used raw as text fails in a light palette, a dark one, or both.
  - **Token maths** (Table ACCENT-4): on `--surface` 39/56 household cells fail (1.92-8.27); on `--bg` 43/56 fail (2.14-7.60), which is 29 of the 35 adult cells.
  - **Rendered** (skeptics and re-measure; per adult in Table ACCENT-6):

    | Element | Dark | Light |
    |---|---|---|
    | Kitchen heading | Eli 2.83; Elizabeth 3.66 | Elizabeth 4.44 (Hearth), 3.55 (Parchment). Eli passes (4.60 Parchment, 5.75 Hearth). Token maths: Mae and Mea 4.04-4.05 (Hearth), 3.23 (Parchment) |
    | Walk time, 11.5 px | David 2.14; Eli 2.57; Elizabeth 3.28-3.33; Mae 3.65; Mea 3.66 | Mae 4.41 and Mea 4.40 (Hearth); Kiara 3.22 (Hearth) and 2.69 (Parchment) |
    | "from" distance | David 1.79; Eli 2.08; Mae 2.81 | Mae 3.01; Eli 4.17; David passes at 4.90 |

- **Expected.** Person-coloured text uses the per-scheme ink, `--accent-deep` today. It reaches at least 5.34:1 on `--surface` and 4.71:1 on `--bg` for every colour in every theme (Table ACCENT-3). The raw hex is never a text colour.
- **Why it matters.**
  - The Kitchen view is the "big type for the counter" display, and its category headings give it its structure.
  - The park distances are read on a phone in sun and at dusk.
  - The failure is by construction, so a new guest's colour cannot avoid it.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:80`; `apps/prayer.html:39, 359`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:440, 524` (read-only; the same lines are in `apps/dollywood-live.html`).
  - Investigator: `tokens.json` (`raw-on-surface`, `raw-vs-bg`), `runtime-summary.json` (Prayer `.k-cat` 89/119; walk time 54/70), `dataset-accent.json` (`.lv-from > b` 47/47), `prayer-kitchen-raw-accent-eli-midnight-mom-parchment.png`, `park-nearby-raw-accent-eli-dad-dark.png`.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-raw-accent-as-text-1-{prayer,park}.json`
    - `verify-raw-accent-as-text-2-{prayer,park}.json`, `-2-kitchen-eli-midnight.png`, `-2-kitchen-mom-parchment.png`, `-2-nearby-dad-system-dark.png`, `-2-ride-card-eli-system-dark.png`
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-prayer.json`, `remeasure-park.json`, `remeasure-tokens.json`.
- **Reproduction.** From `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-raw-accent-as-text-2.mjs prayer midnight,parchment,system-light eli,mom` prints `.k-cat` for Eli at 2.83, 4.60 and 5.75, and for Elizabeth at 3.66, 3.55 and 4.44.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-raw-accent-as-text-2.mjs park system-dark,system-light eli,dad,christian` prints the walk time (David 2.14, Mae 4.41 light) and the ride card (Eli 2.08 / 4.17).
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/tokens.mjs` prints `raw-on-surface` failing 39/56 household cells.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read the four cited rules and confirmed they are in `apps/dollywood-live.html`. They then wrote a WebKit script that sets each theme through the API and localStorage and opens the screens with the Phase 1 area scripts. For each element it measures the computed ink against the median pixel under the box with the text transparent.
    - The Kitchen figures reproduced exactly: Eli 2.83 / 4.60 / 5.75; Elizabeth 28/28 failing.
    - The walk time reproduced exactly: David 2.14, Mae 4.41.
    - The ride card read 2.08 / 4.17 for Eli, not the dataset's 1.63-2.00 / 3.34-3.77.
    - No initials rendered.
    - They derived the luminance cap and floor above.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran a separate WebKit script with `L.reset` per theme; the first pass had carried the Mine / Family choice across themes. It covered the Kitchen on both lists for Eli and Elizabeth in 5 keys, and the park for Eli, David and Mae.
    - The Kitchen, the walk time and the ride card all reproduced; the ride card for David read 1.79 in dark.
    - The Family-list Kitchen is teal: 8.52-8.64 in dark and 4.35-4.37 in light.
    - 0 initials rendered in 10 Family-list runs.
    - The backgrounds are solid `--paper` and 0.94-alpha glass, so a real backdrop blur would not rescue the dark failures.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **The Prayer initials facet is dropped.** `.init` renders only for a name `hub.people()` does not know (`apps/prayer.html:1551-1555`), and only on the Family list (`:1558, 1571`), where `--accent` is already teal. It never paints a profile colour, so the raw-on-soft matrix (48/56) does not apply.
  - **The Kitchen headings sit on `--bg`, not `--surface`,** and are weight 700, not 600. The rendered values match the raw-on-bg maths, not raw-on-surface (Eli 2.83, not 2.57).
  - **The ride-card distance is 2.08 dark / 4.17 light for Eli** on the local rig. The dataset's 1.63-2.00 / 3.34-3.77 is a p10 over a translucent card over the map. Both fail, and the value moves with the card and map position.
  - **Mae's Kitchen was not measured** (U-ACCENT-1). For David and Mea the seed writes no personal list (`audits/tools/areas/prayer.mjs:66`), so their Kitchen headings are token maths only.
  - **Related (not re-filed):**
    - VIS-PRAYER-1 covers the gold and teal labels, not these.
    - The teal Family-list headings at 4.35-4.37 in light belong to P4-COLOR-01.

title: Me → Switch is pale ink on a white pill in every dark scheme: 1.99-2.49:1 for every adult (1.76-2.56 over all household colours)
block:
#### P4-ACCENT-03 — Me → Switch is pale ink on a white pill in every dark scheme: 1.99-2.49:1 for every adult (1.76-2.56 over all household colours)

> **Pointer (merged at assembly) → P4-COLOR-03**, which owns the defect and its medium severity. This entry keeps the per-adult rendered set.

- **Merge note.** This is the same defect as **P4-COLOR-03** (Colour section). Phase 5 should keep P4-COLOR-03 as the single ID. This entry's own contribution is the per-adult rendered set, with every adult measured by two skeptics and the re-measure, and the token check over all 56 household cells.
- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** text a household member needs, below AA on a primary control.
  - **Why not high:** Me is a secondary screen, the pill shape still reads as a button, and people can also switch from the picker. P2 rated the same reading medium.
  - **Exposure:** every dark key, including Hearth on a dark OS, where the dark token block applies (`apps/design.css:176-177`).
- **Areas:** shell. The TV is dropped (see the corrected claim).
- **What happens.**
  - **The rule.** `.ds .hero .btn-primary { background: rgba(255,255,255,.92); color: var(--accent-deep) }` (`apps/design.css:423`). In the dark palettes `--accent-deep` is 58 % accent + white (`:170, 191, 212`), so a pale label sits on near-white. `#switch` renders in the Me hero (`index.html:1252-1253`).
  - **Rendered:**
    - Mea 1.99-2.00, Mae 2.05, Elizabeth 2.07-2.08, Eli 2.29-2.31 and David 2.48-2.49, identical in Forest, Midnight, System dark and Hearth-dark.
    - The Colour skeptics add Kiara 1.76 and Ezra 2.11.
    - Light: 6.72-10.69 for the adults.
  - **Token maths:** 32/32 household dark cells fail (1.76-2.56). 8 of the 32 are Hearth-dark. Even against pure white the best case is 2.90.
- **Expected.** The hero action's label reaches at least 4.5:1 in every palette for every person's colour.
- **Why it matters.** Switch is how the shared iPad changes hands, and the kitchen iPad is in dark mode every evening.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:170, 176-177, 191, 212, 423`; `index.html:78, 626, 1252-1253`.
  - Investigator: `runtime-summary.json` (`button#switch` 20/35), `me-hero-dark-switch-mea-eli.png`.
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-hero-button-dark-every-adult-1.json`, `-1-niece-midnight.png`, `-1-eli-forest.png`, `-1-tv-midnight.png`
    - `verify-hero-button-dark-every-adult-2.json`, `-2-midnight-niece.png`, `-2-system-dark-tv.png`
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-me.json`.
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-hero-button-dark-every-adult-2.mjs midnight,forest niece,eli` prints Mea 1.99 and Eli 2.31.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote a WebKit script that opens `#me` for each adult and theme (the TV through a hash change), reads the computed colour of `#switch`, hides the label, and takes the median painted background. It reproduced all five adults in all four dark keys, computed ink equal to painted ink, and the light controls. They noted that P2 recorded only Eli's reading (2.30), as an investigator-only item.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate script that measures both the computed ink and the darkest glyph pixel against the painted background; the two agree exactly.
    - It covered 20/20 adult dark cases.

> **Merged here (assembly):** the Timer-arc facet of P4-DARK-01.

    - the Timer digits pass at 5.12+;

- **What happens.**

- **Expected.** Person-coloured graphics that carry information reach 3:1 against the surface they sit on, in every scheme and for every profile colour.
- **Why it matters.** Rings carry the time remaining, and the avatar ring is how a person's colour is seen next to their face. A kid's own rings fade on a light theme her parents may pick.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:496-498, 527-528`; `apps/timer.html:22, 29`; `index.html:351, 916`; `apps/prayer.html:416-419`.
  - Investigator: `runtime-summary.json`, `kids-chip-kiara-parchment.png`, `home-david-system-dark.png`.

    - `verify-raw-accent-graphics-light-and-apps-1.json`, `-1-kidverse.json`, `-1-kidchip-kiara-parchment.png`, `-1-timer-dad-dark.png`, `-1-prayer-kid-eli-dark.png`, `-1-park-tab-dad-dark.png`
    - `verify-raw-accent-graphics-light-and-apps-2-main.json`, `-2-park.json`, `-2-kidchip-parchment.png`, `-2-pill-kiara-parchment.png`, `-2-timer-dad-dark.png`

title: An admin recolour never reaches a person who is already signed in: their chrome and every open app keep the old colour until they next sign in
block:
#### P4-ACCENT-05 — An admin recolour never reaches a person who is already signed in: their chrome and every open app keep the old colour until they next sign in

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low; this section lowers it from the investigator's medium.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic, and triggered by a rare admin edit. No data is lost or misattributed, and no flow breaks.
  - **Exposure:** anyone who stays signed in after an admin changes their colour.
    - On a personal phone it lasts until they sign out.
    - On the shared iPad, the next sign-in fetches the new profile (skeptic 2), but the session also never returns to the picker by itself (P2-PROF-09, skeptic 1).
- **Areas:** shell, and every app through hub.js.
- **What happens.**
  - **Where the colour comes from.** `--accent` is `hub.profile.color` (`apps/hub.js:80`). `hub.profile` is read only from the stored session (`:105-111`).
  - **What refreshes the session:**
    - login and createPin (`:169, 173`);
    - a photo change (`:482, 488`);
    - an admin editing their own profile on the same device (`index.html:1684`).
  - **What does not.** No client calls `GET /api/me` (`worker/src/index.js:270`). Pulls never touch the session (`apps/hub.js:286-320`), and the frames' `storage` listener ignores `hub.session` (`:350-364`).
  - **Run** (investigator, Mae → #8C4F7A). The admin PUT returns 200 and the server's `/api/me` returns #8C4F7A. On Mae's iPad:
    - `--accent` stays #BC5A38 after a reload and after 35 s of pulls;
    - the Tally frame stays #BC5A38;
    - a fresh picker shows #8C4F7A.
- **Expected.** A colour change reaches every open session and frame within one pull, as other shared data does.
- **Why it matters.** The person's own chrome, hero and buttons show a colour the rest of the household no longer associates with them. After a reload, the feed on the same page already shows the new one.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:80, 105-111, 169, 173, 286-320, 350-364, 482, 488`; `index.html:1684`; `worker/src/index.js:270, 453-475`; `audits/00-inventory.md:457-458`.
  - Investigator: `recolour.json`, `recolour-mae-home-after.png`, `recolour-mae-tally-after.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-recolour-not-propagated-1.json`, `-1-home.png`, `-1-tally.png`; `verify-recolour-not-propagated-2.json`, `-2-home.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-recolour.json`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-recolour-not-propagated-1.mjs` runs Mae on the iPad in WebKit. It prints `--accent` as #BC5A38 at every step, 0 client `/api/me` requests, and the picker `--tint` as the new colour.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-recolour-not-propagated-2.mjs` runs David on the iPhone in Chromium.
  - Both change a profile colour on the local instance only.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** (Mae, iPad, WebKit, a different swatch #5B6FA8) read `--accent` inline and computed, `hub.profile.color`, the stored session, `hub.people()` and the feed `--tint` at six points: after `hub.pull()`, a visibilitychange, a reload, 35 s of pulls, `hub.profiles()`, and in the Tally frame.
    - The accent stayed #BC5A38 throughout, with 0 `/api/me` calls.
    - The feed changed after the reload (the server joins the colour), while `hub.people()` changed only when `hub.profiles()` was called.
    - A pre-signed rig device turned out to be a stale control (`lib/local.mjs:113`), so the picker was used instead.
  - **Skeptic 2** changed the person (David), device (iPhone PWA), engine (Chromium) and colour (#2E7D5B) and got the same pattern. The selected tab kept the old colour, and so did the Timer frame. They noted that name and kind come from the same stale session (U-ACCENT-3).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **"`hub.people()` and the feed do refresh" is half true.** The feed takes the new colour on the next reload. `hub.people()` changes only when something calls `hub.profiles()`. On a signed-in device, that is the picker, Add a guest, admin remove or purge, or a photo upload (`index.html:524, 1421, 1628, 1634`; `apps/hub.js:483, 489`).
  - **The investigator's "after a profiles refresh" step was forced by its own script.**
  - **"Two colours on one screen":** they are on the same page, but not in the same iPad viewport.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2-PROF-09: the shared iPad never returns to the picker.
  - The Phase 0 gap at `audits/00-inventory.md:457-458` (no ID).

title: With north-up pressed, the compass fills with the person's `--accent-deep`: its 9 px red "N" drops to 1.0-2.45:1 for every profile, and its red needle to 1.0-1.5:1 in dark
block:
#### P4-ACCENT-06 — With north-up pressed, the compass fills with the person's `--accent-deep`: its 9 px red "N" drops to 1.0-2.45:1 for every profile, and its red needle to 1.0-1.5:1 in dark

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low.
  - **Clause:** a secondary label and graphic on an optional map toggle. The compass shape, the ring and the rotation still show which way is north, and the button is unpressed by default (template `:620`, `aria-pressed="false"`).
  - **Exposure:** only while north-up is on, but then for every household profile in every theme (41 skeptic cases, all below 3:1).
- **Areas:** dollywood-live (from the sibling template).
- **What happens.**
  - **The fill wins on specificity.** `[data-flavor=live] button[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--accent-deep)}` (template `:225`, specificity 0,2,1) beats `.lv-north`'s glass (`:417`, 0,1,0) once the button is pressed (`:1595`).
  - **The glyphs are fixed red.** The "N" is `.lv-north b{font-size:9px;font-weight:800;color:var(--danger)}` (`:418`), and the needle is a literal `fill="#FF6B4A"` (`:620`).
  - **Neither changes with the person's colour, while the fill does.** Rendered, the pixel ratio equals the token ratio within 0.02 (Table ACCENT-6):

    | Glyph | Dark | Light |
    |---|---|---|
    | "N" | 1.01-1.37 (Eli 1.01, Kiara 1.37) | 1.28-2.45 (Kiara 1.28, David 2.45) |
    | Needle | 1.01-1.48 | Mae, Elizabeth, Mea, Ezra and Kiara 2.05-2.97; Eli and David pass at 3.44-4.27 |

- **Expected.** The north indicator stays at least 4.5:1 for the label, or 3:1 as a graphic, whatever the person's colour. The pressed state should not put a person-coloured fill under semantic glyphs.
- **Why it matters.** North-up is the orientation aid on a rotated park map. When it is switched on, its own label all but vanishes.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:225, 417-418, 620, 1595` (read-only; the same lines are in `apps/dollywood-live.html`).
  - Investigator: `dataset-accent.json` (`button#lv-north.lv-north > b`, 13/13).
  - Skeptics:
    - `verify-park-north-n-on-accent-1.json`, `-1-eli-system-dark.png`, `-1-eli-system-light.png`
    - `verify-park-north-n-on-accent-2.json`, `-2-eli-system-dark.png`, `-2-eli-system-light.png`, `-2-dad-system-light.png`
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/verify-park-north-n-on-accent-2.mjs --profiles=eli,kiara --themes=system-dark,system-light` prints `tokenRatioN` 1.01 / 2.15 for Eli and 1.37 / 1.28 for Kiara, with `tokenRatioArrow` alongside.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** confirmed the specificity chain and ran 15 cases: 5 adults in System light and dark, and Eli in five palettes. It resolved the computed background and N colours through a canvas.
    - 15/15 were below 3:1, at 1.01-2.45.
    - A pixel pass was contaminated by the needle overlapping the N's box, so the exact-paint ratios are reported.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran 26 cases: 7 profiles in System light and dark, plus Eli, Mae and David in four palettes. It hid the N and took the pixel median under its box, and checked that the glyph lies 100 % inside the 44 px circle.
    - 26/26 were below 3:1.
    - It added the needle facet.
    - It noted that the disc also rotates on the first tap (P3-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-09).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **It is broader than stated.** The draft had Eli only; it is every profile.
  - **Eli's light values are 1.88-2.15 in exact paint,** not the dataset's p10 1.39-1.45.
  - **The needle on the same fill is new here.** P4-ICON-04 covers the needle on the unpressed glass in light, and notes the N at 4.37-4.77 there.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P4-ICON-04: the needle, unpressed.
  - P3-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-09: the compass behaviour.
  - Table COLOR-3 row "Compass N", which defers the pressed state to this section.

block:
#### CONS-ACCENT-1 — Signed out, the accent falls back to Elizabeth's colour, so every PIN pad fills its dots and Continue in #8A6A4B (Midnight #CBA77E), whoever is signing in (investigator rating: low)

- **The rule.** `.pin-dots i.on` is painted with `--accent` (`index.html:58`). hub.js removes `--accent` while nobody is signed in (`apps/hub.js:81`), so `--accent: var(--mocha)` applies (`apps/design.css:86`). That is Elizabeth's exact hex.

Run `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/runtime.mjs --profiles signed-out --only shell:pin-entry --themes system-light,midnight --force`, then read `runtime/system-light/signed-out/shell--pin-entry.json`, or run `node audits/tools/phase4/ACCENT/remeasure.mjs pin`.

block:

block:

title: The profile colours are neither pastel nor distinct enough as fills: the soft fills are near-grey, and 6 of 21 household pairs sit under ΔE00 5 as fills (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### VIS-ACCENT-1 — The profile colours are neither pastel nor distinct enough as fills: the soft fills are near-grey, and 6 of 21 household pairs sit under ΔE00 5 as fills (investigator rating: medium)

- **The colours are mid-tones.** Every profile colour sits at OKLCH L 0.42-0.65: too dark to be a fill, too light and too grey to be an ink.

block:

title: Keyboard focus is invisible on every `.ds .btn`: 26 of 26 Tab stops change 0 pixels in the shell, TV, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses
block:
#### P4-TELL-01 — Keyboard focus is invisible on every `.ds .btn`: 26 of 26 Tab stops change 0 pixels in the shell, TV, Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium, the rating P2 gave the shell-only facet. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** a secondary flow broken or misleading. Keyboard use is a secondary input path in a touch-first household. The controls still work and can be reached; only the focus position cannot be seen. That fails WCAG 2.4.7.
  - **Exposure:**
    - Desktop Chrome or Edge keyboard users.
    - An iPad with a keyboard, but Safari moves Tab onto buttons only with "Press Tab to highlight each item" (or Option-Tab).
    - Keyboard use on the TV kiosk and in Kid Verse is unlikely: they add breadth, but little real-world impact.
- **Areas:** shell, tv, tally, timer, kidverse, verses.
- **What happens.**
  - Tabbing onto any `.ds .btn` makes it `:focus-visible`, and nothing changes on screen: the computed outline and box-shadow are the same focused and blurred.
  - Every such stop, per area:
    - shell: 10 (Open F260, Open the ledger, Open prayer, 4 round Done, Add, Refresh, Show more);
    - TV: `#kiosk-switch`;
    - Tally: Reset;
    - Timer: 8 (6 presets, Start, Reset);
    - Kid Verse: 4 (Say, Done, Story say, I heard it);
    - Verses: 2 (Say, Show).
  - Some controls outside the `.ds .btn` component do show a ring: the shell's reminder field, tab-bar tabs, theme cards and `#photo-btn`, Tally's − and +, and every F260 and Prayer stop. **Corrected after the completeness critic:** the Tab walk behind this sentence stopped at 14 stops per area. Walking every stop shows that any component which sets its own box-shadow loses the ring the same way: all 9 Apps-grid tiles, all 9 picker cards and the chat field are unringed (P4-TELL-07), and the `.ds .switch` and selected `.ds .seg button` are predicted to be (TELL Unresolved 12).
- **Cause.** `:focus { outline: none }` and `:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus) }` (`apps/design.css:313-314`, specificity 0,1,0) lose to:
  - `.ds .btn { box-shadow: var(--e1) }` (`:356`, 0,2,0);
  - `.ds .btn-soft/-ghost/-danger { box-shadow: none }` (`:362-364`);
  - the primary button's own inset shadow (`:361`).
  No `.ds .btn:focus-visible` rule exists in `design.css`, `index.html` or the four apps. The only app focus rule is Tally's `.tbtn:focus-visible` outline (`apps/tally.html:83`). The `--focus` token itself resolves to a visible ring: `color-mix(in srgb, <accent> 38%, transparent)`, 3 px (`apps/design.css:102`).
- **Expected.** A visible focus ring on every focusable control for keyboard users, as P2 asked for the shell.
- **Why it matters.** On a desktop, or an iPad with a keyboard, you cannot see where focus is in Timer, Kid Verse and Verses at all, and not on any of the shell's card buttons. One shared rule in `design.css` fixes every area.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `keyboard-ring.json`. Changed pixels: shell `.gcard .btn` 0/8,960; TV 0/8,128; Tally `#reset` 0/10,496; Timer `#go` 0/25,440; Kid Verse `#done` 0/37,232; Verses `#show` 0/27,280. Control group: F260 `#tabPlan` 532, Prayer `#listSwitch button` 516, Tally `#plus` 1,752. Images: `keyboard-timer-_go.png`, `keyboard-kidverse-_done.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-ds-btn-keyboard-focus-invisible-cross-area-1-{chromium,webkit}.json` with `-{chromium,webkit}-{timer,kidverse,verses,tally}.png`; `verify-ds-btn-keyboard-focus-invisible-cross-area-2-{chromium,webkit}.json` with `-2-webkit-light-timer.png` and `-2-chromium-light-kidverse-counterfactual.png` (all in `audits/evidence/p4/TELL/`).
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-ring.json`.
  - Code: `apps/design.css:102, 313-314, 355-356, 361-364`; `apps/tally.html:83`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-keyboard-ring.mjs` prints `timer #go {"tab":true,"fv":true,"changed":0,…}`, `kidverse #done … changed 0` and `f260 #tabPlan … changed 532`.
  - Full Tab walk: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-ds-btn-keyboard-focus-invisible-cross-area-1.mjs chromium` (or `webkit`).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote a script that walks every Tab stop, up to 14 per area, in Chromium and WebKit (desktop 1440×900, TV 1920×1080, System light; Eli, Ezra for Kid Verse, the kiosk for the TV). At each stop it compared the computed outline and box-shadow with the values after `blur()`, and pixel-diffed the box plus 8 px.
    - 26 of 26 `.ds .btn` stops matched `:focus-visible`; 0 changed their style; 0 changed any pixel. Same in both engines.
    - Non-`.ds` controls ring: the shell's `#remtext` 5,096 px, the tab-bar tabs about 1,460 px each, Tally − 1,192 and + 1,728, all 14 F260 stops and all 14 Prayer stops.
  - **Skeptic 2** pressed real Tab keys until each of the six named controls was the active element, in both engines and both schemes: 24 runs.
    - 0 changed pixels in all 24: shell 0/9,792, TV 0/8,908, Tally 0/11,424, Timer 0/27,048, Kid Verse 0/39,096, Verses 0/28,980. The Tally + control changed 1,727-1,848 px in all 4 runs.
    - Counterfactual: injecting `.ds .btn:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus) !important }` made the six change 593 / 1,011 / 621 / 4,619 / 5,734 / 4,972 px. The ring token paints; only the cascade drops it.
  - **Re-measure:** identical counts. 0 px on all six with `:focus-visible` true, and blurred-against-reblurred noise 0 on every crop. Control group 532 / 516 / 1,752.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The core claim holds in both engines and both schemes.
  - Two stop counts are corrected: Timer has 8 `.ds .btn` stops, all unringed, not "0/4". In the shell, all 10 `.ds .btn` stops are unringed; the 4 of 14 stops that ring are non-`.ds` controls, not "3/8".
  - Pixel totals depend on crop padding (Timer `#go` 0/23,864 at 8 px, 0/25,440 at 10 px).
  - The root cause and the shell facet are P2's existing item. This finding is the cross-area extension.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 "UX — Keyboard focus is invisible on buttons (medium)" (`audits/02-shell.md:5931`). P4-TOK-01: even where the ring does paint, `--focus` is under 3:1 against the surface. P4-TELL-07: the same cascade on the Apps-grid tiles, the picker cards and the chat field.

title: Twelve reachable form fields are under 16 px (build guide 6, park map 3, Larder 2, F260 1), so iOS zooms the page when they take focus
block:
#### P4-TELL-02 — Twelve reachable form fields are under 16 px (build guide 6, park map 3, Larder 2, F260 1), so iOS zooms the page when they take focus

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic and recoverable. The page zooms and the user pinches back; no data is lost and no flow is blocked.
  - **Exposure:** iPhone and iPad. The worst case is the park map's Search and rider-height filter on an iPhone at the park. The F260 field is on a rarely used restore sheet. The zoom itself follows from the measured sizes and is not rig-verifiable: `visualViewport.scale` stays 1 in desktop WebKit.
- **Areas:** dollywood, dollywood-live, f260, leftovers.
- **What happens.** iOS zooms the page when a text field or select under 16 px takes focus. The viewport correctly leaves zoom enabled: `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`, with no maximum-scale. The fields:
  - **Build guide, all 6 reachable** (on the iPhone once More is tapped): `select#cint` 13, `select#bmap` 15 (an invisible select laid over the basemap button, template `:337`), `input#q` 15, `select#hf` 12.5, `input#sc-plot` 13, `input#sc-in` 13.
  - **Park map, 3 reachable:** Search `input#q` 15, rider height `select#hf` 12.5, contour `select#cint` 14. `#bmap` 15, `#sc-plot` 13 and `#sc-in` 13 are in the DOM, but the live flavour hides `.toolbar` and `aside.side` with `display: none !important` (template `:386`). Only `#q`, `#tab-list` (holding `#hf`) and `#cint` are moved into the live sheet (template `:1591-1592`).
  - **F260:** `textarea#restoreText` 15 (`.modal textarea`, `apps/f260.html:399`), in the backup-restore sheet.
  - **Larder:** `select#size` 15 and `input#date` 15 (`apps/leftovers.html:52-53`), on every screen and in kid mode too.
  - **The other seven areas have none.** The shell's fields are 16, Prayer's 16.5, and Tally, Timer, Kid Verse and Verses have no fields.
  - The template's sizes come from `font: inherit` (template `:24`) inside 12.5-13 px labels (`:673, 676, 1009`).
  - Inside the viewer, iOS would zoom the whole shell page (not rig-verifiable).
- **Expected.** Every field at 16 px or more.
- **Why it matters.** Searching the park map or setting a rider height on an iPhone at the park zooms the page, and the user has to pinch back before the sheet fits again.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `tells-chromium.json` `desktop.fieldsUnder16`; `tells-webkit.json` `probe.fieldsUnder16`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-fields-under-16px-ios-zoom-1.json`, `verify-fields-under-16px-ios-zoom-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-tap.json`, `remeasure-usel.json`.
  - Code: `apps/leftovers.html:52-53`; `apps/f260.html:399`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:24, 337, 386, 673, 676, 1009, 1591-1592` (read-only).
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/tells-chromium.mjs dollywood-live` prints `f16:["select#bmap 15","input#q 15","select#hf 12.5","select#cint 14","input#sc-plot 13","input#sc-in 13"]`, the DOM list.
  - Reachability: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-fields-under-16px-ios-zoom-1.mjs` reports `totalUnder16 15`, `totalUnder16Reachable 12`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran WebKit on the iPhone PWA (430×932, touch) across all 11 areas. The script opens every pane that holds on-demand fields: the park map's Search and Style; the build guide's Listings, Layers, Scale and the phone More button; F260's restore sheet; the shell's chat and Add a guest.
    - 15 fields under 16 px are in the DOM, with every value as claimed. 12 can ever be rendered and focused.
    - The three park-map exceptions sit in containers the live flavour hides.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran WebKit on the iPhone PWA and the iPad portrait as Eli, with Kid Verse and a second Larder pass as Ezra.
    - The same 15 in the DOM on both devices; the Larder's two also apply in kid mode.
    - Every viewport meta allows zoom. No code comment calls the small sizes intentional. `text-size-adjust` (`apps/design.css:293`) does not prevent focus zoom.
    - Only the Larder facet was on record before (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:974`).
  - **Re-measure:** the identical 15-field DOM list at the same sizes, in Chromium and in WebKit on the iPad; 0 elsewhere.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - 12 reachable fields, not 15. The park map's `#bmap`, `#sc-plot` and `#sc-in` can never take focus.
  - Several fields appear only on demand: F260's restore text and the scale fields, and on the iPhone the build guide's `#q` and `#cint` (after More).
  - The Dollywood fix belongs in `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html`, because the pair are generated.
  - Whether iOS also zooms on its native date picker (Larder `#date`) is a device question. WebKit on Windows computes it as a text field.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P3 Larder §5 "Zoom on input focus" (`audits/03-apps/leftovers.md:974`), which is the Larder facet. VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8 (default form controls).

title: With a named dark theme on a light-OS device, every Hearth-based document paints paper-white Hearth until `hub.js` runs; the flash lasts as long as `hub.js` is late
block:
#### P4-TELL-03 — With a named dark theme on a light-OS device, every Hearth-based document paints paper-white Hearth until `hub.js` runs; the flash lasts as long as `hub.js` is late

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. No data is lost, the app stays usable and it settles in the right palette. It still goes against the house style's "no white flash" and against the code's own comment, "applied synchronously so there is no flash" (`apps/hub.js:59`), so info would be too low.
  - **Exposure:** narrow. The service worker serves `hub.js` cache-first (`sw.js:10, 45-48`). Apps inside the shell load the same `apps/hub.js` URL the shell has already fetched (`index.html:440`), so an HTTP-cached copy also covers them. On the rig, a warm reload through the service worker gave 0-1 Hearth frames. The flash needs an uncached or revalidated `hub.js` while a dark theme is already stored in `localStorage`:
    - a context the service worker does not control;
    - a service-worker cache evicted while `localStorage` survives;
    - a slow service-worker start on a real iPad (not verifiable here).
    A truly first visit has no stored theme, so it takes the separate server-pull path, not this one.
- **Areas:** shell, tv, f260, leftovers, prayer, tally, timer, kidverse, verses. The Dollywood pair do not flash: their HTML is baked with `data-theme="dark"` (`apps/dollywood.html:2`).
- **What happens.**
  - Setup: light OS, and Midnight stored both in `localStorage` `hub.theme` and in the person row.
  - While `hub.js` has not run, `<html>` has no `data-theme` and no `data-scheme`, so `design.css` resolves the Hearth `:root` tokens. The body is `rgb(247, 242, 235)` (`--bg` `#F7F2EB`).
  - The shell and the TV show a full paper-white screen. F260 shows its whole Plan page on light paper. Tally paints its light-palette wash (mean luminance 0.28 against a settled 0.04).
  - When `hub.js` runs, the page switches to Midnight: `rgb(26, 21, 18)`.
- **Cause.**
  - The palette is set only by `applyTheme()` in `hub.js` (`apps/hub.js:74-82`, called at `:112`).
  - Every document loads `hub.js` at the end of `<body>`: `index.html:440`, `apps/f260.html:777`, `apps/leftovers.html:133`, `apps/prayer.html:573`, `apps/tally.html:142`, `apps/timer.html:73`, `apps/kidverse.html:180`, `apps/verses.html:149`.
  - No `<head>` script in any of the eight files applies the stored theme.
  - `theme-color` is keyed to the OS scheme (`index.html:8-9`) until `syncThemeColor()` runs (`index.html:656`), and the manifest's `background_color` is the light `#F7F2EB` (`manifest.json:9`).
- **Expected.** The first paint of every document uses the person's stored palette. That needs a synchronous `<head>` bootstrap from `localStorage` `hub.theme` that sets `data-theme`, `data-scheme` and `theme-color`.
- **Why it matters.** A family member who picked a dark palette for the evening gets a full-screen paper-white frame whenever `hub.js` is slow to arrive.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `flash-chromium.json` (B-400 flashes in 9 areas; A-0, A-400 and B-0 none), `flash-chromium-{shell,f260,tally,…}-B-400.png`, `flash-webkit.json`, `flash-webkit-f260-B-400.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-named-theme-cold-load-flash-1-{chromium,webkit}.json`, `-1-chromium-shell-held.png` (a plain paper-white screen), `-1-webkit-f260-held.png` (F260 laid out in Hearth), `-1-chromium-tally-held.png`; `verify-named-theme-cold-load-flash-2-{chromium,webkit}.json`, `-2-chromium-shell-d150.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-flash.json`.
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:59, 74-82, 112`; the eight script tags above; `index.html:8-9, 656`; `manifest.json:9`; `sw.js:10, 45-48`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/flash.mjs chromium f260` prints `f260 B-400 {… "flash":true … "brightest":{"ms":~204,"lightShare":0.952,…}}` and `B-0 … "flash":false`.
  - Hold test: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-named-theme-cold-load-flash-1.mjs chromium hold`.
  - Delay sweep: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-named-theme-cold-load-flash-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote a script with no code shared with `flash.mjs`.
    - Hold test, Chromium and WebKit, all 9 areas: it held `hub.js` open with no reply and read the document's state and screenshot 900 ms after the trigger. `data-theme` and `data-scheme` were unset, the body was `rgb(247, 242, 235)`, `--bg` was `#F7F2EB`, and the screenshot's mean luminance was 0.83-0.89 (Tally 0.282). Released, every document turned Midnight (0.022-0.074; Kid Verse 0.275). With an immediate `hub.js`, Midnight showed on the first read. In WebKit the shell and TV pass the computed-style check, but they cannot be screenshotted while held, because Playwright waits for fonts.
    - Timing test, Chromium, +400 ms: see Table TELL-4. +0 ms: no flash anywhere.
  - **Skeptic 2** used a different method: an init script logging every rAF tick's body background and a MutationObserver on `data-scheme`, with `hub.js` delayed 0, 50, 150 and 400 ms, for the shell, F260 and Tally in both engines.
    - Hearth ticks before `data-scheme` was set: Chromium 0 / 3-4 / 10-11 / 26 at the four delays; WebKit 1 (1-8 ms) / 4 / 10 / 25-26.
    - A warm reload through the service worker: 0-1 ticks.
    - It confirmed that no `<head>` sets the theme, and that the flash contradicts `apps/hub.js:59`.
  - **Re-measure:** in all 9 areas the body first paints `rgb(247, 242, 235)`, then Midnight. The build guide goes dark to dark. DOM durations were 404-504 ms at +400 ms.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The mechanism and the area list hold. Each document flashes for as long as `hub.js` is late, starting at about one frame of delay.
  - The per-area durations in the draft (305-597 ms) do not reproduce as area properties. Read Table TELL-4 as "about 0.4-0.5 s at +400 ms".
  - The line references are `apps/hub.js:74-82` and `:112`, not 77-85 and 111.
  - The "first visit" exposure wording is wrong; see Exposure.
  - 0.883 is the shell's frame mean; `#F7F2EB` itself has a relative luminance of 0.893.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 web tell #6 (`audits/02-shell.md:5923`), which ran only System on a dark OS.
  - P2-VIS-03: the steady-state mismatch, Hearth on a dark OS, caused by `design.css:176`.
  - P2 PWA-GAP-4: the manifest and the missing startup image.
  - The DARK section's `theme-color` staleness finding.

title: On a desktop with classic scrollbars, grey OS bars paint on the hub's scrollers (15 px on `#views` and each app document, 10 px on F260's side column and the build guide's chip strip), and under Midnight on a light OS the track is a white stripe
block:
#### P4-TELL-04 — On a desktop with classic scrollbars, grey OS bars paint on the hub's scrollers (15 px on `#views` and each app document, 10 px on F260's side column and the build guide's chip strip), and under Midnight on a light OS the track is a white stripe

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. No flow breaks and no text contrast is involved; even the white stripe is a mismatch, not unreadable content.
  - **Exposure:** desktop browsers that use classic scrollbars: a Windows PC, or a Mac with a mouse. The iPad and iPhone use overlay bars. Chrome or Edge on Windows 11 with overlay or Fluent scrollbars may paint thinner bars, or show them only on hover; headless Chrome still reserves 15 px of layout.
- **Areas:** shell, f260, leftovers, prayer, dollywood, dollywood-live, kidverse, verses. The TV only reserves the gutter (see the corrected claim). Tally and Timer do not overflow.
- **What happens.** With Chromium's classic scrollbars (Playwright's `--hide-scrollbars` removed):
  - **Shell:** `main#views` paints a 15 px bar. The track is `rgb(252, 252, 252)` beside the `rgb(247, 242, 235)` paper, with a grey thumb.
  - **F260:** `.side` is 10 px (`scrollbar-width: thin`, `apps/f260.html:450`), plus a 15 px bar on the document.
  - **Build guide:**
    - `#chips` is a 10 px horizontal bar with a tinted thumb and arrow buttons. Its `::-webkit-scrollbar { height: 6px }` is ignored because `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-color` are also set (`apps/dollywood.html:240-241`).
    - `#tab-list` and `#b-list` are 15 px each, and the document 15 px.
  - **Park map:** the sheet's `.lv-body` is 15 px once the sheet is open.
  - **Every other scrolling app document** paints its own 15 px bar inside the viewer: Larder, Prayer, Kid Verse, Verses.
  - **Under Midnight on a light-OS desktop:**
    - The page is `data-theme=midnight`, `data-scheme=dark`, but the computed `color-scheme` is still `light dark`, so the track stays `rgb(252, 252, 252)` beside a `rgb(35, 27, 21)` page. The result is a white 15 px stripe down the right edge of a dark theme.
    - With System on a dark OS the track is `rgb(44, 44, 44)`, which matches.
    - The cause is `color-scheme: light dark` declared once on `:root` (`apps/design.css:15`), with nothing tying it to `data-scheme`.
- **Expected.** Scrollbars styled for the theme: thin, tinted or hidden on chrome; hidden on horizontal chip strips; and following the resolved scheme, not the OS.
- **Why it matters.** On a Windows PC, or a Mac with a mouse, the hub shows grey OS scrollbars on its navigation layer, and a white stripe under the dark palettes. Earlier phases passed this tell because the rig hid every bar.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `scrollbars.json`, `scrollbar-shell-main-desktop.png`, `scrollbar-leftovers-main-desktop.png`, `scrollbar-dollywood-main-desktop.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-classic-scrollbars-on-chrome-1.json`, `-1-shell-views.png`, `-1-tv.json`, `-1-tv.png`; `verify-classic-scrollbars-on-chrome-2.json`, `-2-shell.png`, `-2-shell-midnight-light-os.png`, `-2-dollywood.png`, `-2-f260.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-scroll.json`.
  - Code: `index.html:66, 130`; `apps/design.css:15`; `apps/f260.html:450`; `apps/dollywood.html:240-241, 316-317`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/scrollbars.mjs shell f260 dollywood` prints `main#views(chrome) v15 h0 sw=auto`, `div.side(chrome) v10 h0 sw=thin`, `div#chips.chips(chrome) v0 h10 sw=thin`.
  - The Midnight track: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-classic-scrollbars-on-chrome-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran two Chromium launches through the rig.
    - With Playwright's default arguments, every scroller measures 0 px, which confirms the rig artefact.
    - Without `--hide-scrollbars` it measured the widths above and sampled the gutter pixels. The shell's grey thumb is visible in `-1-shell-views.png`.
    - For the TV, a crop of the right edge shows only the backdrop. `#views` overflows by 8 px (1,088 against 1,080) and reserves 15 px, but the fixed `.tv-bg` layer (`index.html:130`: `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 0`) paints over the gutter.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran installed Chrome with and without the flag.
    - Same widths, including `#b-list`.
    - The chip strip draws a 10 px tinted bar with arrow buttons (`-2-dollywood.png`).
    - It set each theme through the API and `hub.theme` and sampled the track: Hearth on a light OS `rgb(252, 252, 252)` against `rgb(243, 238, 227)`; Midnight on a light OS `rgb(252, 252, 252)` against `rgb(35, 27, 21)`; System on a dark OS `rgb(44, 44, 44)`.
  - **Re-measure:** a fresh Chromium launch without the flag and a generic scan of every overflow box gave identical widths, plus `#b-list` 15 px.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **TV:** no bar paints. It shows a 15 px layout offset on the right.
  - **What counts as chrome:** `#views` and the app documents are content scrollers, where native apps also show a bar under classic scrollbars. The bars that sit on chrome are F260's `.side`, the build guide's `#chips`, `#tab-list` and `#b-list`, and the park map's `.lv-body`.
  - **Partly met already:** F260's side column and the chip strip already use thin bars, and the chips have a tinted thumb on a transparent track. What is left is the 10 px width (the chips were meant to be 6 px) and a chip strip that should be hidden.
  - **The white track** under a dark palette on a light OS is a dark-mode adaptation bug. Skeptic 2 measured it under Midnight; Forest should behave the same but was not measured. It shares its root cause with the native-controls finding in the DARK and COLOR sections (`color-scheme` fixed at `apps/design.css:15`).
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P2 web tell #9 (`audits/02-shell.md:5926`).
  - P3 `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:885` ("6 px"); P3 `audits/03-apps/f260.md:830` ("no capture paints it"); P3 `audits/03-apps/prayer.md:1013` (the sheet bar on desktop).
  - The DARK and COLOR native-control finding (same `color-scheme` cause).

title: The build guide first paints an empty section-chip strip, then its map drops 44-48 px when the chips arrive (CLS 0.119-0.128 on a cold open through the hub)
block:
#### P4-TELL-05 — The build guide first paints an empty section-chip strip, then its map drops 44-48 px when the chips arrive (CLS 0.119-0.128 on a cold open through the hub)

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic. The workspace drops once, about 150-200 ms after first paint, in a secondary adult app. No data, flow or control is affected.
  - **Exposure:** every open of the build guide. On the family's usual iPad path (tapping the tile, in WebKit), the drop lands before the viewer's fade-in becomes visible.
- **Areas:** dollywood (build guide). The park map hides `.chips` in its live flavour (template `:386`).
- **What happens.**
  - The section-chip row is an empty `<div id="chips">` in the exported HTML (`apps/dollywood.html:578` = template `:578`). The main inline script fills it (template `:1120`), and that script runs after the multi-megabyte payload (template `:682`) and the parser-blocking external `hub.js` (`apps/dollywood.html:684`).
  - The page paints first with the strip 10 px tall and the workspace top at 252 px. About 100-200 ms later, 13 chips are inserted, `.chipwrap` grows to 54 px, and the workspace and map drop to 296 px.
  - Chromium's layout-shift API scores this at 0.1185 (largest shift, `div.workspace` 235→283) and 0.119-0.128 in total, but only on a cold open through `index.html` with the hash `#dollywood`. It scores 0.0001 when the tile is tapped and when the file is opened standalone, although the geometry is the same on every path.
  - The "862 px" listing-control move is at y 1,587→2,449, below a 1,180 px viewport, and is the same standalone.
- **Expected.** A stable layout. The chip row should reserve its final height before the chips arrive; content never jumps.
- **Why it matters.** The map, which is the point of the page, jumps as the guide opens. That is a tell the house style bans.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `loading.json` `areas.dollywood.cls`, `loading-dollywood.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-build-guide-cls-in-viewer-1-{chromium,chromium-cpu4,webkit,frames-cpu6}.json`; `verify-build-guide-cls-in-viewer-2-{chromium,webkit}.json` and `-2-chromium-early.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-cls.json` (0.1185; largest shift 0.1185 at 202 ms, `div.workspace 235->283`).
  - Code: `apps/dollywood.html:2, 578, 684`; template `:386, 578, 682, 1120` (read-only); `index.html:327-329` (the viewer's 360 ms opening animation).
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/loading.mjs dollywood` prints `dollywood {"cls":0.1283,…}`; `loading.json` has the largest shift `{"t":213,"v":0.1185,"src":["div.workspace 235→283"]}`.
  - All paths: `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-build-guide-cls-in-viewer-2.mjs`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed** (both corrected the cause).
  - **Skeptic 1** ran Chromium in the viewer and standalone, with the pull held and with 150 ms latency, twice each. It recorded layout-shift entries and a rAF geometry trace (workspace top, `#chipwrap` height, chip count, `data-flavor`, theme). It repeated this with 4× CPU throttling and in WebKit (geometry only).
    - Viewer: largest shift 0.1185 at 184-214 ms; total 0.1186 held, 0.1283 at 150 ms. Standalone: 0 or 0.0001.
    - But the geometry is the same in both: the empty strip (10 px) at first paint, then 13 chips at about 170-240 ms (54 px), and the workspace from 252 to 296 px. `data-flavor` is already `hub` in the first sample.
    - WebKit shows the drop in both paths: viewer 264→296 at 249-292 ms, standalone 252→296 at 196-231 ms.
    - With 4× throttling: viewer 0.139-0.142, standalone still 0.0001.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran 4 Chromium arms × 3 runs and 3 WebKit arms × 2, logging chip count, strip height and workspace top on every frame, with the viewer's opacity on the same clock.
    - Cold hash open: 0.1283 / 0.1283 / 0.0001 held; 0.1283 / 0.1186 / 0.1283 with no added latency. Tile tap: 0.0001 ×3. Standalone: 0.0001 ×3.
    - The frame records show the same 44 px drop on every arm. Standalone first contentful paint (88-116 ms) comes before the fill (169-215 ms).
    - WebKit: standalone painted the empty strip 2/2 times. A tile tap showed the chips in place on the first frame 2/2 times. A cold hash open painted the empty strip once in 2, at viewer opacity 0.
  - **Re-measure:** 0.1185 from the same largest shift (2 shifts recorded, against the investigator's 3).
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The jump is real, but it belongs to the app's own load order, not to the hub path.
  - The hub flavour is not applied late: `data-flavor="hub"` is baked into the HTML (`apps/dollywood.html:2`).
  - The held first pull plays no part: the same shift occurs with 150 ms latency.
  - "0.0001 standalone" reflects how Chromium's API counts shifts on that route, not a stable layout.
  - The fix belongs in the sibling template: reserve the strip's height (for example `[data-flavor=hub] .chips { min-height: 54px }`), or build the chips before `hub.js` loads.
  - The draft's token gap, "hub flavour applied before first paint", is dropped: that is already true.
- **Related (not re-filed):**
  - P3 dollywood §5 "Layout shift as data loads" (`audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:886`). That row covers chip labels changing from 0/N to 7/9 after the pull, not the empty strip.
  - MOTION's Table MOTION-6 and GAP-MOTION-1 record this area as 0.0001 with an 862 px move. This finding corrects both readings.

title: The design system's only overscroll reset is set on `body`, where it has no effect, in every document
block:
#### P4-TELL-06 — The design system's only overscroll reset is set on `body`, where it has no effect, in every document

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** cosmetic, a native-feel tell. A bounce would reveal canvas colours close to the page colour (ratios 1.00-1.24 where measured).
  - **Exposure:** the documents that actually scroll their viewport. At 430×932 those are F260 (4,885 px of overflow), the build guide (8,143), Kid Verse (1,420), Verses (1,104), Prayer (743) and the Larder (297). Tally, Timer, the park map, the shell page and the TV have 0 px. The shell and the TV scroll inside `#views`, which already sets `contain` (`index.html:66`).
- **Areas:** f260, dollywood, kidverse, verses, prayer, leftovers. The rule is inert in all 11 documents; these six are where it would matter.
- **What happens.**
  - `apps/design.css:304` sets `overscroll-behavior: none` on `body`. The `html` rule (`:293`) sets none.
  - In the rig-v2 raw data, all 3,625 documents where the rig read the value show `html` auto and `body` none.
  - `body` is never a scroll container. In the apps, `html` overflow is visible, so body's overflow propagates to the viewport. In the shell and the TV, body is fixed with overflow hidden (`index.html:21`).
  - The viewport takes `overscroll-behavior` from the root element only; body's value is not propagated. So the rule does nothing.
  - On a synthetic page, an iframe scrolled past its end chains 1,200 px to its parent with no rule, and also with `body { overscroll-behavior: none }`. It chains 0 px with the rule on `html`.
  - By the specification, iOS will rubber-band these app documents.
  - What a bounce would reveal is fine where measured: canvas against content-edge ratios are 1.00-1.24 in the shell, F260, Prayer, the build guide, Kid Verse and Verses, in System light, System dark and Midnight (`tells-webkit.json` `over`). Tally's saturated wash would show 3.74:1 or 5.10:1 against the canvas if it ever bounced, but Tally does not scroll.
- **Expected.** The overscroll rule on `html`, so the design system's intent actually applies: `none` stops the local bounce too, `contain` only stops chaining.
- **Why it matters.** P2 passed this tell "in code" on the strength of this declaration, and six P3 app reports cited it as working. The declaration guards nothing.
- **Evidence.**
  - Investigator: `overscroll-body.json`; `from-raw.json` `overscroll`; `tells-webkit.json` `over`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-overscroll-reset-on-body-inert-1.json`, `verify-overscroll-reset-on-body-inert-2.json`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-over.json` (1,200 / 1,200 / 0 px).
  - Code: `apps/design.css:293, 304`; `index.html:21, 66`; `apps/dollywood.html:372, 451` (the template's `contain` on `.bmain` and `#pop`).
- **Reproduction.** `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/verify-overscroll-body.mjs` prints `body {… "computed":{"html":"auto","body":"none"…},"chained":true}` and `html {… "chained":false}`.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1.**
    - Part A: it opened all 11 areas on the iPhone PWA in Chromium and WebKit and read the computed values, whether body is a real scroll container, the viewport overflow, and every element with a non-auto value.
      - Chromium: `html` auto and `body` none in all 11. `bodyIsScroller` false in every document. The only non-auto elements are the shell's `#views`, the build guide's `.bmain` and the park map's `#pop` (all `contain`).
    - Part B: a synthetic page with five arms, including `design.css`'s own base block read from disk. Chromium: no rule 1,200; the `design.css` block 1,200; plus `html { none }` 0; `html { contain }` 0; body as the real scroller 0.
    - The rig's WebKit (Playwright 26.6 on Windows) returns `CSS.supports('overscroll-behavior', 'none') = false`, and all five arms chain 1,200 px. That engine cannot test the property.
  - **Skeptic 2** ran its own four-arm synthetic test in both engines, with the same Chromium result (1,200 / 1,200 / 0 / 0), and probed the real documents on the WebKit rig. It confirmed which documents scroll, which fit, and that body never scrolls.
  - **Re-measure:** 1,200 / 1,200 / 0 px on its own synthetic page.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - Right in substance, with three qualifications:
    - "Computed in every document over 3,662 jobs" is the rig's helper output over the 3,625 documents where it read a value. It is not a WebKit computed value, because this WebKit build does not implement the property.
    - The iOS consequence rests on the specification plus Chromium's behaviour, not on a WebKit or iOS measurement.
    - Only six documents actually scroll their viewport (see Exposure).
  - `contain` on an app document would still allow the local bounce inside the iframe; only `none` stops it.
  - A small Phase 3 side error: `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:883` says there is "no `overscroll-behavior` on html or body". The Dollywood pair load `design.css` (`apps/dollywood.html:683`), so body computes `none` there too, to no effect.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 web tell #7 (`audits/02-shell.md:5924`), which this overturns. The P3 rows `audits/03-apps/f260.md:828`, `kidverse.md:843`, `leftovers.md:973`, `prayer.md:1011`, `tally.md:690` and `timer.md:499`.

title: Keyboard focus is invisible on every Apps-grid tile and every profile-picker card, and the chat composer removes its own ring (added after the completeness critic)
block:
#### P4-TELL-07 — Keyboard focus is invisible on every Apps-grid tile and every profile-picker card, and the chat composer removes its own ring (added after the completeness critic)

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium. Not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** the same as P4-TELL-01: a secondary flow broken or misleading. The controls still work and can be reached by Tab; only the focus position cannot be seen, which fails WCAG 2.4.7. It is not low, because the picker and the Apps grid are where every keyboard session starts.
  - **Exposure:** desktop keyboard users, or an iPad with a hardware keyboard and Safari's "Press Tab to highlight each item" setting. Touch never triggers `:focus-visible`, so touch use is unaffected.
- **Areas:** shell.
- **What happens.**
  - A real Tab walk on the desktop (1440×900) reaches all 9 `.tile` buttons on the Apps grid and all 9 `.pcard` cards on the picker. Every one matches `:focus-visible`, but its computed box-shadow and outline are the same focused and blurred, and its box plus 8 px changes 0 pixels.
  - The chat field `.chat-form .input` is `:focus-visible` with a computed box-shadow of `none` and 0 changed pixels; only the caret shows.
  - On a device with no stored last profile (as in the rig), the picker puts focus on the first card at load (`index.html:541`) with no mark. On a device that has one, focus lands on the `.last` card, which already carries the static 2 px "Welcome back" ring (`index.html:47`). That ring is not a focus style: it stays on that card while Tab moves focus to unmarked cards, so the only ring on screen marks the wrong card.
  - Control group: the four tab-bar tabs change about 1,450-1,480 pixels when focused, in both engines and both schemes, and the six theme cards and `#photo-btn` ring too.
- **Cause.** The shared ring is `:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus) }` (`apps/design.css:314`, specificity 0,1,0). Each of these components sets its own box-shadow, which wins:
  - `.tile { … box-shadow: var(--e1) }` (`index.html:221-224`, 0,1,0, later in the cascade than `design.css`, which `index.html:17-18` links first);
  - `.ds .glass-strong` on `.pcard` (`apps/design.css:388-398`, 0,2,0);
  - `.chat-form .input:focus { box-shadow: none }` (`index.html:264`, 0,3,0, after `.ds .input:focus` at `apps/design.css:446`), and `.chat-form .input { border: 0 }` (`index.html:263`) hides the accent border that `.ds .input:focus` sets.
  - The same cascade predicts that the `.ds .switch` (inset shadow, `apps/design.css:456`) and the selected `.ds .seg button` (`apps/design.css:467`) lose the ring as well. Neither skeptic's Tab walk reached them, so that stays a prediction (Unresolved 12).
- **Expected.** Every focusable control shows a visible ring (at least 3:1) under `:focus-visible`, whatever its resting shadow, including the picker, which is the entry point on a desktop.
- **Why it matters.** On a desktop, or an iPad with a keyboard, you cannot see which profile you are about to open or which app, at the two places every session starts. It also corrects P4-TELL-01's statement that controls outside `.ds .btn` show a ring: that holds for the tabs, the theme cards, `#photo-btn`, the reminder field and the apps' own controls, not for these three components.
- **Evidence.**
  - Critic: `audits/evidence/p4/CRITIC/focus-other-components.json` (screen `#apps`: 9 × `BUTTON.tile` with `fv: true`, `styleChanged: false`, `pixelsIdentical: true`; picker: 9 × `BUTTON.pcard.glass-strong`, the same; tabs and theme cards `styleChanged: true`).
  - Skeptic 1: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-focus-invisible-tiles-picker-cards-chat-1-1.json`, with `-1-1-apps-focused.png` / `-1-1-apps-unfocused.png`, `-1-1-picker-focused.png` / `-1-1-picker-unfocused.png` and the control group `-1-1-me-focused.png` / `-1-1-me-unfocused.png`.
  - Skeptic 2: `audits/evidence/p4/CRIT/verify-critic-focus-invisible-tiles-picker-cards-chat-1-2-chromium-light.json` and `-1-2-webkit-dark.json`, with `-1-2-chromium-light-apps-focused.png`, `-1-2-chromium-light-apps-forced-focused.png`, `-1-2-chromium-light-chat-focused.png`, `-1-2-chromium-light-chat-forced-focused.png` and the WebKit-dark equivalents `-1-2-webkit-dark-apps-focused.png`, `-1-2-webkit-dark-apps-forced-focused.png`, `-1-2-webkit-dark-chat-focused.png`, `-1-2-webkit-dark-chat-forced-focused.png`.
  - Code: `index.html:17-18, 41-50, 221-224, 263-264, 541`; `apps/design.css:102, 313-314, 388-398, 446`.
- **Reproduction.**
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/CRITIC/focus-other-components.mjs | grep -E 'tile|pcard'` prints 18 lines with `"fv":true`, `"styleChanged":false` and `"pixelsIdentical":true`.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-focus-invisible-tiles-picker-cards-chat-1-1.mjs` (Chromium and WebKit, light and dark, baseline-first pixel diff) and `node audits/tools/phase4/CRIT/verify-critic-focus-invisible-tiles-picker-cards-chat-1-2.mjs` (with the forced-ring counterfactual).
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** screenshotted every target with nothing focused, then pressed real Tab keys (Alt+Tab in WebKit) until each target had focus, and compared computed box-shadow, outline and decoded pixels (a channel change above 8) against that baseline. Chromium and WebKit, light and dark, on the typical seed:
    - Apps grid: 9 of 9 tiles `:focus-visible`, 0 changed style, 0 changed pixels (largest channel difference 0-2, noise), in all four runs.
    - Picker: 9 of 9 cards, the same, in all four runs. On load focus is on the first card (Eli) with `:focus-visible` true and no visible ring.
    - Chat: `#chat-in` `:focus-visible`, computed box-shadow `none`, 0 changed pixels, in all four runs.
    - Control group: all four tab-bar tabs change style and about 1,450-1,480 pixels (channel difference 41-67), so the method detects a real ring.
  - **Skeptic 2** walked real Tab presses on the picker, `#apps`, `#chat` and `#me` in Chromium light and WebKit dark, compared each stop focused and after `blur()` against a re-shot noise baseline (box plus 10 px, tolerance above 8 per channel), and ran a counterfactual with `box-shadow: var(--focus) !important` injected on the same stops:
    - Picker 9 of 9, tiles 9 of 9 (the wide F260 tile and eight small ones) and `#chat-in`: `:focus-visible` true, style unchanged, 0 changed pixels, in both engines.
    - Counterfactual: the picker cards change 2,124-3,009 px, the tiles 1,521-3,334 px and `#chat-in` about 6,500 px. The token would paint a ring; the cascade removes it.
    - The Me walk reached no `.switch` or `.seg` stop.
- **Corrected claim.** As filed, with two nuances from the skeptics: focus starts on an unmarked card only when no last profile is stored (otherwise on the `.last` card, whose static ring then misleads as Tab moves on), and in the chat field the accent border from `.ds .input:focus` is also defeated by `border: 0`, so only the caret is left; that is a weaker facet than the tiles and cards. "Byte-identical" crops hold with the critic's method; with a baseline-first method Chromium PNG bytes sometimes differ, but the decoded pixels differ by at most 2 per channel.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P4-TELL-01 (the same WCAG 2.4.7 failure on `.ds .btn`; one shared, outline-based focus rule fixes both), P4-TOK-01 (even where a ring paints, `--focus` is under 3:1), P4-COLOR-05 (the chat field's own boundary is 1.1-1.45:1), P2 "UX — Keyboard focus is invisible on buttons" (`audits/02-shell.md:5931`), which tested only `.ds .btn`. For the scorecard this is counted in the `hearth-shared` Native feel base with P4-TELL-01 (same mechanism and exposure; no cell changes).
- **Token gap.** A `--focus-ring` applied through one shared rule that uses `outline`, not `box-shadow`, so a component's own shadow cannot cancel it (for example `:where(.ds, body) :is(button, a, input, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ink); outline-offset: 2px }`). This extends TELL token gap 2, which already asks for an outline-based ring no component resets; the colour is P4-TOK-01's.

title: Selectable chrome and callout suppression follow the `.ds` boundary exactly (investigator rating: low)
block: #### CONS-TELL-1 — Selectable chrome and callout suppression follow the `.ds` boundary exactly (investigator rating: low) - **What happens.** - Controls computing `-webkit-user-select: text` on the main screen (WebKit, iPad portrait): F260 all 190 (re-measure 192), Larder all 9 (15), Prayer all 29 (19), build guide all 54 (57), park map all 13 (15). The shell's 4 of 14 are the tab bar. - Controls computing `-webkit-user-select: none`: Tally 3/3, Timer 8/8, Kid Verse 4/4, Verses' 2 buttons. Verses' 16 status chips stay selectable. - Over every rig screen, the selectable share is 100 % in the five apps without `.ds`, 0 % in Tally and Timer, and 47-60 % in the shell, TV, Kid Verse and Verses (Table TELL-3). - `-webkit-touch-callout` is NOT FOUND IN CODE in any of the 11 documents, `design.css` or `hub.js` (re-measure scanned the long Dollywood lines as well). - Draggable `` on the main screens: shell 13, TV 7, Kid Verse 2, and 1 each in F260, Tally, Timer and Verses. - A double-click selects the app titles "F260", "The" (Larder) and "Dollywood". It selects no button label. - **Cause.** The only reset is `.ds .btn { user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none }` (`apps/design.css:355`). Tally and Timer set it on `body` themselves (`apps/tally.html:22`, `apps/timer.html:10`). F260, the Larder, Prayer and the template have no `.ds` and no rule. - **Expected.** One base rule outside `.ds` makes all chrome unselectable and callout-free. - **Why it matters.** On an iPad or iPhone, a long press on a Done, week or chip button can raise the selection loupe or an image callout (needs a device). It happens exactly in the apps that keep their own CSS. - **Evidence:** `tells-webkit.json` (`probe.userSelect`, `dblclick`, `imgsDraggable`); `from-raw.json` (`userSelectTextShare`); `static.json` (`counts.touchCallout` 0); `remeasure-usel.json`, `remeasure-static.json`. - **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/tells-webkit.mjs f260 tally` prints `f260 {"controls":190,"us":{"text":190}…}` and `tally {"controls":3,"us":{"none":3}…}`. - **Related (not re-filed):** P2 "UX — Chrome is selectable and images are draggable (low)" (`audits/02-shell.md:5936`), the shell facet. VIS-F260-12 (`audits/03-apps/f260.md:720`). This item is the cross-area pattern.

title: Three confirmation idioms; 14 of 20 native dialog call sites are reachable in the shell and the Dollywood pair (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-TELL-2 — Three confirmation idioms; 14 of 20 native dialog call sites are reachable in the shell and the Dollywood pair (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - 20 native call sites (Table TELL-6). 14 are reachable in the shipped UI: shell 9, build guide 2, park map 3.
  - A run in WebKit raised and dismissed 9 of them.
  - F260 confirms in an in-app modal (`confirmModal`, `apps/f260.html:1756`), and Prayer in an inline `ask()` panel (`apps/prayer.html:1089`).

  - P2 "UX — Native `confirm()` dialogs and no undo (low)" (`audits/02-shell.md:5902`), which owns the shell's 9.

title: Light themes open the build guide on a near-black frame (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### VIS-TELL-1 — Light themes open the build guide on a near-black frame (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.**
  - With a light OS and the System theme, and `hub.js` immediate (scenario C), the build guide shows about 240 ms of dark frames (mean luminance 0.23-0.30) before it settles light (0.545).
  - Cause, part 1: `"dark": true` in `apps.json:9-10` makes the shell add `.dark` to the viewer (`index.html:722`), and `#viewer.dark` is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--slate) 12%, black)` (`index.html:331`).
  - Cause, part 2: the exported HTML is baked with `data-theme="dark"` (`apps/dollywood.html:2`), so the template paints its dark default until `hub.js` sets `data-scheme`.
  - The park map shares both the flag and the template. Its scenario-C run showed no dark frame: its light frames were the viewer's 360 ms fade over a light Home (`index.html:327`). So this item is measured for the build guide only.
- **Expected.** The loading tint follows the resolved scheme.
- **Why it matters.** It is a flash in the other direction: a black frame in a light house.

title: No app uses a skeleton, and `hub.js` gives apps no "pulled" signal to know when to show one (investigator rating: low; the same gap as CONS-MOTION-4)
block:
#### GAP-TELL-1 — No app uses a skeleton, and `hub.js` gives apps no "pulled" signal to know when to show one (investigator rating: low; the same gap as CONS-MOTION-4)

- **What happens.**
  - 900 ms into a cold open, all 11 areas have 0 skeletons, 0 spinners and 0 infinite animations (re-measure agrees, at 905-918 ms).
  - What they show instead is in Table TELL-5: final wording, placeholder values ("0", "5:00", "…") or a blank page (Verses, 0 characters).
  - `.ds .skeleton` (`apps/design.css:539-544`) is used only by the shell's picker, feed, reminders, admin and chat.
  - The only spinners are pull-to-refresh (`index.html:76-77`) and the park map's locating ring (`apps/dollywood-live.html:406-407`). Both are appropriate.
- **Expected.** A skeleton recipe with stable heights that apps can reuse, and a per-scope "pulled" flag in `hub.js`.
- **Why it matters.** It explains why every area improvises its loading state, the root of several P2 and P3 loading defects.
- **Evidence:** `loading.json` `loadingAt900`; `loading-verses.png`; `loading-shell.png`; `static.json` `counts.skeleton`; `remeasure-cls.json` `at900`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/TELL/loading.mjs verses prayer` prints `verses {… "load":{"sk":0,"sp":0,"inf":[],"lt":[],"len":0}}` and `prayer {… "len":52}`.
- **Related (not re-filed):** MOTION's CONS-MOTION-4 files the same missing primitive: treat the two as one item in Phase 5. Also P2-VIS-07, P2-SYNC-15, P3-TALLY-07, P3-LEFTOVERS-05, P3-VERSES-07 and UX-F260-5.
