block:
#### P4-COLOR-01 — In the light palettes, apps ink text and icons with the mid-tone hues and the semantic aliases, not the `-ink` tokens: gold text at 2.03-3.47:1, olive, terra and teal text at 3.6-4.45:1, and today rings, the F260 chapter bar and the earned star at 2.48-2.96:1

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** needed text below AA on primary surfaces of daily flows: F260's Today kickers, pace and streak; Prayer's "not prayed in N days" and "Answered recently"; the build guide's list counts. The rule makes that at least medium.
  - **Why not high:** these are secondary labels, counts and states. The main content and primary actions use other tokens: the reading title, Done, and the prayer titles.
  - **Exposure:** the three light palettes. Hearth is the System default by day, so the default experience is affected. Midnight, Forest and System dark pass at 6.2:1 or better.
- **Areas:** f260, prayer, dollywood (build guide), dollywood-live (park map), leftovers, kidverse; shell for graphics only (the Home fridge bars and the gold tile icon, from the rig). The Timer's three mid-tone occurrences are its blinking 0:00 and belong to CONS-COLOR-1.
- **What happens.**
  - **The system's rule.** Each hue family has a mid tone, a `-soft` fill and an `-ink`. The `-ink` pairs pass everywhere, at 5.37-10.35:1 on their fill. The style guide states the rule: "Text always uses the `-ink` variant on a soft background" (`docs/design.html:95`).
  - **The aliases point the wrong way.** `--ok`, `--warn`, `--danger` and `--info` point at the mid tones, not the inks (`apps/design.css:80-83`).
  - **The apps ink with the mid tones or the aliases:**
    - **F260:** gold for the chapter count, "This week" and "MV" (per VIS-F260-1). Its own key reads "olive = done, gold = journal + memory verses, terra = streak" (`apps/f260.html:11-12`), and the book groups use `--g-law: var(--gold)` (`:23`).
    - **Prayer:** `.cold` in terra (`apps/prayer.html:106`); `.ans .when`, `.ledger b`, `.recall b` and `.warn` in gold (`:146, 153, 156, 311`); `.err` in terra (`:230`); the calendar's today ring in gold (`:165`).
    - **Larder:** `.err { color: var(--danger) }` (`apps/leftovers.html:63`).
    - **Build guide and park map:** `.oi .n{color:var(--ochre)}` (template `:68`), where both hub flavours set `--ochre: var(--gold)` (template `:212`).
    - **Kid Verse:** star icons in `--gold` (`apps/kidverse.html:63, 68, 76`); its text uses `-ink`.
    - **Shell:** the `.bar` gradient on a gold `--tint` (`apps/design.css:534`) and the tile icon in the app's `--tint` (`:608`).
  - **Token maths** (Table COLOR-5), in Hearth / Parchment / Frost:

    | Mid tone | On `--bg` | On its own `-soft` |
    |---|---|---|
    | Gold | 2.96 / 3.24 / 3.47 | 2.78 / 3.11 / 3.30 |
    | Olive | 4.04 / 4.07 / 4.34 | — |
    | Terra | 4.05 / 4.06 / 4.33 | — |
    | Teal | 4.35 / 4.37 / 4.25 | — |

  - **Rendered** (skeptic 2, in Hearth / Parchment / Frost):

    | Element | Colour | Contrast |
    |---|---|---|
    | F260 `#chCount` "343", 21 px/700 | gold | 2.71 / 2.97 / 3.18 |
    | F260 "NEXT UP" kicker, 12 px/800 | olive | 3.78 / 4.04 / 4.15 |
    | F260 `.hero-pace`, 13.5 px | olive | 4.08 / 4.27 / 4.45 |
    | Prayer `.ledger b` "Answered recently" | gold | 2.78 / 3.11 / 3.30 |
    | Prayer `.recall b` | gold | 2.96 / 3.24 / 3.47 |
    | Prayer `.cold` "not prayed in 33 days" | terra | 4.05 / 4.06 / 4.33 |
    | F260 heatmap today ring (graphic) | gold | 2.62 / 2.83 / 3.09 |
    | Kid Verse earned star (graphic) | gold on gold-soft | 2.78 / 3.11 / 3.30 |

    On the same Kid Verse screen, the kicker in `--gold-ink` reads 5.72 / 6.53 / 6.61. In Midnight every item above reads 6.95-9.21.
  - **Rig:**
    - Gold as text: 19,307 occurrences, min 2.03. The build guide's list counts `div.oi > span.n` account for 16,682 of them, at 2.03 p10 / 3.17 median.
    - Olive, terra and teal as text: 1,356 occurrences at 3.6-4.45, and 2.42 for the Timer's blinking 0:00.
    - Error lines: F260 `#passErr` 3.76, Prayer `#f-titleErr` 4.1, Larder 4.27.
    - Graphics: the F260 chapter bar against its track 2.48-2.95; the Home fridge bars 2.27-2.99; the gold tile icon 2.39-2.81.
- **Expected.** Text and icons on paper, surface or soft fills use the `-ink` tokens: at least 4.5:1 for text, and at least 3:1 for icons and graphics. Mid tones are used only for fills that carry no text, and even then reach 3:1 against the surface.
- **Why it matters.** This one token confusion is behind most of the light-theme failures in F260, Prayer, the build guide and the park map (Table COLOR-2: 57.9 %, 6.7 %, 28.4 % and 40.5 % in Hearth). It also puts "today", progress and stars under 3:1, and for pre-readers colour and position are the only cues.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:80-83, 534, 608`; `docs/design.html:95`; `apps/f260.html:11-12, 23`; `apps/prayer.html:106, 146, 153, 156, 165, 230, 311`; `apps/leftovers.html:63`; `apps/kidverse.html:63, 68, 76`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:68, 212` (read-only).
  - Investigator: `audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/palette.json`, `components.json` (gold-text, mid-text), `spot.json` (f260-gold-text), `nontext-summary.json`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-mid-tone-semantic-as-ink-1.json`, `-1-f260.png`, `verify-mid-tone-semantic-as-ink-2.json`, `-2-f260-hearth.png`, `-2-prayer-hearth.png` (all in `audits/evidence/p4/COLOR/`).
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/dollywood/aerial-mix-typical-desktop-light.png`, `audits/screens/f260/behind-typical-desktop-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** All from `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep -A7 '^system-light'` prints gold onBg 2.96 / onSoft 2.78, olive 4.04 / 3.78, terra 4.05 / 3.64, and teal 4.35 / 3.98, with ink/soft 5.37-7.61.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/spot.mjs` prints f260-gold-text p10 2.71 and 2.78.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-mid-tone-semantic-as-ink-2.mjs` prints the rendered table above.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** parsed the tokens of all five palettes from `design.css` and computed base on bg, surface and soft, and ink on soft. They then ran WebKit (iPad portrait, System light, Eli) and found every visible text whose computed colour equals a resolved mid tone. For each, they hid all text and took p10 and median over the element's first line box.
    - The token pairs matched to 2 dp.
    - F260: "343" 2.71, "THIS WEEK" 2.78, "TODAY" and "NEXT UP" 3.78, "12-day streak" 3.92, streak "12" 4.09, "On pace…" 4.08.
    - Prayer: "not prayed in 33/31 days" 4.05 / 4.29.
    - Nothing visible on the Larder's first screen: `.err` only shows on an error.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote their own `design.css` parser and a WebKit run, setting the theme through the API and localStorage. They opened F260, Prayer, the Larder and Kid Verse in System light, Parchment, Frost and Midnight, read the computed colour and opacity chain, and pixel-sampled the background with text hidden.
    - They obtained the rendered table above, which matches the investigator's figures exactly.
    - They confirmed intent from `docs/design.html:95`: the apps break the system's own rule, so this is not by design.
    - Not seen in the typical seed, because each needs a particular state: `#passErr`, Prayer `.err`, Larder `.err`, `.ans .when`.
- **Corrected claim.** Right as a cross-area, root-cause finding, with four refinements:
  - It is a light-palette defect only.
  - Most per-app text instances are already filed: VIS-F260-1 (the same 2.71 / 2.97 / 3.18), VIS-PRAYER-1 (2.78-3.47), P3-LEFTOVERS-15, VIS-LEFTOVERS-2 and VIS-KIDVERSE-2. What is new:
    - the token-level cause, with one token and lint fix that covers all the apps;
    - the build guide's gold `.oi .n` numbers (P3 wrote "Everything else measured passes", `audits/03-apps/dollywood.md:859`);
    - the F260 olive and terra kickers, pace and streak;
    - Prayer's terra `.cold`;
    - the non-text cases: the F260 today ring and chapter bar, the Prayer today ring, and Kid Verse's earned star.
  - On `--surface` cards the Parchment olive, terra and teal pass (4.61-4.96). The failure is on the page and on the soft fills; gold fails everywhere in light.
  - Kid Verse shows the right pattern for text only: its star icons use `--gold`. VIS-VERSES-3 (white on an olive fill) is only loosely related.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-F260-1, VIS-PRAYER-1, P3-LEFTOVERS-15, VIS-LEFTOVERS-2, VIS-KIDVERSE-2.

title: Six rules ink with the raw profile colour where the AA-safe `--accent-deep` already exists: Prayer's kitchen headings are 2.83:1 in every dark palette, the park map's walk times and distances 1.79-2.57:1 in dark, and in light the same text fails for Mae, Mea, Elizabeth and Kiara
block:
#### P4-COLOR-02 — Six rules ink with the raw profile colour where the AA-safe `--accent-deep` already exists: Prayer's kitchen headings are 2.83:1 in every dark palette, the park map's walk times and distances 1.79-2.57:1 in dark, and in light the same text fails for Mae, Mea, Elizabeth and Kiara

> **Merged here (assembly):** P4-ACCENT-02 and the text facets of P4-DARK-01 are pointers to this ID.

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** needed text below AA on primary surfaces: the Kitchen view's section headings (a wall display) and the park map's walk times and distances.
  - **Why not high:** in each view the main content keeps a passing ink. Request titles use `--ink`, distances in feet use `--text`, and the turn instruction is bold `--text`. The failing elements are labels and cues, and nothing is lost or unusable.
  - **Graphics:** the selected-tab icon and the route glyph fail 3:1, but the pressed tab also has a tinted fill and a `--text` label, so that facet alone would be low. The mic icon is marginal, at 2.93-2.95 against 3.
  - **Exposure:**
    - The Kitchen view is on Prayer's personal list. On the Family list, `body.shared` rebinds `--accent` to teal (`apps/prayer.html:39`) and the heading reads 8.52.
    - The park map text shows on park days.
    - The dark facet hits every colour except Kiara's. The light facet hits Mae, Mea, Elizabeth and Kiara, depending on the palette.
- **Areas:** prayer, dollywood-live. The same template rules are exported into `apps/dollywood.html`. The shell's own raw-colour uses (the ring arc, tile icons) are P2's.
- **What happens.**
  - **The raw hex.** `apps/hub.js:80` sets `--accent` to the raw profile hex in every scheme.
  - **The safe ink already exists.** `design.css` derives `--accent-deep` per scheme: 72 % + black in light, commented "filled buttons, text on soft — AA on paper for every family colour" (`apps/design.css:89`), and 58 % + white in dark (`:170, 191, 212`). Prayer already uses it for `#pray .cat` (`apps/prayer.html:334`), and so does the template in six places (template `:225, 244, 329, 453, 458, 462`).
  - **Six rules use raw `--accent` instead:**
    - `#kitchen .k-cat` at 13.5 px/700 (`apps/prayer.html:359`);
    - the `.micbtn` icon (`:387`);
    - the pressed park tab's icon (template `:429`);
    - the walk time `.lv-item .d small` at 11.5 px/600 (template `:440`);
    - the "from" distance `.lv-from b` (template `:524`);
    - `.lv-route-head svg{stroke:var(--accent)}` (template `:464`). This last rule beats `.lv-turn svg{stroke:currentColor}` (`:458`) at equal specificity, so the route glyph paints the raw colour on its own `--accent-deep` tile. That is a cascade bug, and it fails in light too.
  - **Measured** (skeptics' rendered values unless marked):

    | Element | Dark | Light |
    |---|---|---|
    | Kitchen heading (Eli) | 2.83 in Midnight, Forest and System dark (#4F5D8C on #1A1512) | Eli 5.75 in Hearth. Token maths on the Hearth `--bg`: Mae 4.05, Mea 4.04, Elizabeth 4.44 (David 6.91 passes) |
    | Mic icon (3:1) | 2.93 in Midnight and System dark, 2.95 in Forest (computed colour only) | 5.23 in Hearth |
    | Walk time, 11.5 px | Eli 2.57, David 2.14, Elizabeth 3.28 (Forest) | Kiara 3.22 (Hearth), 2.69 (Parchment). Token maths on `--surface`: Mae 4.41 and Mea 4.40 (Hearth); Mae and Mea 3.67, Ezra 3.95, Elizabeth 4.03 (Parchment). Eli 6.27 |
    | "from" distance, 13.5 px | Eli 2.08, David 1.79. Rig minimum 1.63 (Hearth on a dark OS) | Eli 4.17 in Hearth (rig 3.34-3.77) |
    | Selected tab icon (3:1) | Eli 1.70-1.75, David 1.49-1.52, Elizabeth 2.11 (Forest) | Kiara 2.44-2.45 (Hearth), 2.25 (Parchment); Eli 4.33-4.5 |
    | Route glyph (3:1) | Eli 2.50, David 2.76 | Eli 1.52 in Hearth |

  - **Token maths, raw colour on the Midnight surface:** TV 1.95, David 2.14, Eli 2.57, Elizabeth 3.33, Ezra 3.40, Mae 3.65, Mea 3.66, Kiara 4.99. The existing `--accent-deep` reaches 5.60-8.62 on the dark surface and 6.25-9.48 on the dark page, for every profile.
- **Expected.** Person-coloured text and icons use the per-scheme ink, which is `--accent-deep` today, reaching at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for icons against `--bg`, `--surface` and `--surface-2` in every palette. The route glyph keeps `currentColor` (`--on-accent`) on its tile.
- **Why it matters.** The Kitchen view is the counter display, often read in dark mode. On the park map, the walk times and the selected tab are how a parent navigates a crowded park on a phone at dusk.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/hub.js:80`; `apps/design.css:89, 170, 191, 212`; `apps/prayer.html:39, 334, 359, 387`; `../dollywood-build-project/scripts/template.html:429, 440, 458, 464, 524` (read-only; the same rules are in `apps/dollywood-live.html`).
  - Investigator: `spot.json` (prayer-kitchen-kcat), `spot-prayer-kitchen-midnight.png`, `midnight-park-nearby-raw-accent.png`, `palette.json` (`profiles.*.themes.*.rawOnSurface`), `audits/evidence/p4/measure/failing-pairs/dollywood-live.json`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-raw-accent-ink-no-dark-lift-1-{tokens,prayer,park}.json`, `-1-prayer-kitchen-midnight.png`, `-1-park-nearby-midnight.png`, `verify-raw-accent-ink-no-dark-lift-2.json`, `-2-kitchen-midnight.png`, `-2-park-dad-midnight.png`.
  - Re-measure: `remeasure-tokens.json` (the light facet).
- **Reproduction.** All from `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/spot.mjs` prints the line "prayer-kitchen-kcat midnight/lightos": p10 2.83, median 2.83.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-raw-accent-ink-no-dark-lift-1.mjs tokens prayer park` prints the table above.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/remeasure.mjs tokens` prints the light raw-colour values.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** re-read the cited rules and the `--accent-deep` lifts, then wrote a three-part WebKit script:
    - **tokens:** every palette and every seed colour.
    - **prayer:** the Kitchen view on the Mine and Family lists. The computed colour and a text-hidden pixel median agree.
    - **park:** the park seed at a real clock, with geolocation placed inside the park. It covered the pressed Nearby tab icon, the walk time, `.lv-from b` after tapping a ride, and the route glyph after `routeTo()`.
    - The token maths reproduced exactly. They measured the kitchen heading, the Family-list rebind (8.52) and the park values in the table.
    - They found the route-glyph cascade bug and the light failure of the "from" distance (4.17).
    - The mic button is `hidden` in the rig (no speech recognition), so its value is computed colour only.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote a separate WebKit script that reuses none of the investigator's code. It opened the real Prayer kitchen, the add sheet's mic, and the park map with `setMe()` inside the park, then read the computed ink and sampled the rendered background with text and SVG hidden. It also computed the token maths for all 8 colours in all 5 palettes.
    - Its measurements match the table, including Elizabeth in Forest (3.28 and 2.11) and Kiara in light.
    - The backgrounds were solid (rendered equals computed), so this is not a glass artefact.
    - It established that `--accent-deep` already passes: 5.3:1 or better for every profile in every palette, except Kiara on the Parchment well at 4.12.
    - The David and Mae kitchen runs timed out on `#moreBtn`; token maths covers them.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **The capability exists.** This is a consistency bug: six rules use raw `--accent` where `--accent-deep` exists and is used by the same files. The investigator proposed a new `--accent-ink`; the token gap is a documented ink role and a lint rule, not a missing token.
  - **The light facet is wider than "Kiara only".** It is Mae, Mea, Elizabeth and Kiara, depending on palette (re-measure; skeptic 2).
  - **The Kitchen defect is on the personal list only.**
  - **The route glyph is a cascade bug,** failing in light at 1.52 as well.
  - **"Shell" is dropped from the areas.** The shell instances are P2's.
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 VIS "The accent and tile icons are not lifted for dark" (`audits/02-shell.md:5840-5846`): rings, tile icons and the badge in the shell. VIS-PRAYER-1 covers other elements.
  - **Merge note:** the DARK and ACCENT investigators measured the same rules (their drafts' DARK-3, ACC-01 and ACC-02). The aggregator should keep one ID.

title: Me → Switch is pale ink on a white pill in every dark scheme: 1.76-2.48:1 for every household profile and the guest, the kids included
block:
#### P4-COLOR-03 — Me → Switch is pale ink on a white pill in every dark scheme: 1.76-2.48:1 for every household profile and the guest, the kids included

> **Merged here (assembly):** P4-ACCENT-03 is a pointer to this ID.

- **Severity: medium.** Both skeptics rated it medium; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** text a household member needs, below AA on a primary control. Switch is the only control on Me for handing the shared iPad to someone else (`index.html:1282`), and adults and both kids use it.
  - **Why not high:** the label is one word on an obvious pill, so it can still be found. Me is a secondary screen, and P2 rated the same reading medium.
  - **Exposure:** every dark scheme. That is System on a dark OS, Midnight, Forest, and Hearth chosen on a dark-OS device (which takes the dark tokens, `apps/design.css:176-177`). Light passes.
- **Areas:** shell. The TV is dropped: see the corrected claim.
- **What happens.**
  - **The rule.** `.ds .hero .btn-primary { background: rgba(255,255,255,.92); color: var(--accent-deep) }` (`apps/design.css:423`). In light, `--accent-deep` is 72 % + black and passes. In dark it becomes 58 % + white (`:170, 191, 212`), a pale tint, while the fill stays near-white.
  - **Where it renders.** The Me hero draws `#switch` for every kind of profile (`index.html:1252-1253`). In the shell, only `#switch` uses the rule.
  - **Rendered** (both skeptics, WebKit, iPad portrait):

    | Profile | Scheme | Contrast | Ink on fill |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Kiara | Midnight, 19 px | 1.76 | #D4B97B on #F9F6EE |
    | Mea | Forest or System dark | 1.99 | — |
    | Mae | Midnight or System dark | 2.05 | — |
    | Grandma Jo (guest) | System dark | 2.07 | — |
    | Ezra | System dark, 19 px | 2.11 | #76B5B0 on #EDF5F4 |
    | Eli | Midnight, System dark and Forest | 2.29 | #99A1BC on #F1F2F6 |
    | David | Forest | 2.48 | #8E9F8E on #F0F2F0 |

    Light controls: Kiara 5.26-5.29, Ezra 7.06, Eli 8.68.
  - **Token maths.** The re-measure and skeptic 2 give 1.76-2.56 over the seeded colours and swatches; the TV's colour is highest at 2.56. Skeptic 1's own maths gives 1.82-2.70, and 1.91-2.90 even on pure white. The three computations differ in method, and none reaches 3:1.
- **Expected.** A button on the hero keeps at least 4.5:1 in both schemes. In dark, either the fill flips to a deep tint with a pastel ink, or the ink uses a token that is safe on a fixed light fill.
- **Why it matters.** Switch is how the shared iPad changes hands. The worst case is a kid's own colour: Kiara's label is 1.76:1.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:89, 170, 176-177, 191, 212, 423`; `index.html:626, 1252-1253, 1282`.

"The TV: 2.59" and the `tv` area are dropped: the kiosk cannot open Me (`index.html:78, 626`), so that reading is rig-only.

That item already named `design.css:423` and said the Switch "needs its own dark value". This defect is its adversarially verified form, widened to both kids, the guest and every dark theme key. section: Contrast of every text/background pair in use (COLOR)
title: The chosen theme never sets `color-scheme`, so UA-painted controls follow the OS: F260's week-note Copy button reads 1.01-1.12:1 with a dark palette on a light-OS device, and 1.11-2.92:1 the other way round
block:
#### P4-COLOR-04 — The chosen theme never sets `color-scheme`, so UA-painted controls follow the OS: F260's week-note Copy button reads 1.01-1.12:1 with a dark palette on a light-OS device, and 1.11-2.92:1 the other way round

> **Merged here (assembly):** P4-DARK-03 is a pointer to this ID.

- **Severity: low.** Skeptic 1 rated it medium and skeptic 2 low; this section lowers it from the investigator's medium.
  - **Clause:** the one failure established in both engines is a default `<button>`: F260's week-note Copy, a secondary control that VIS-F260-5 already records as unstyled. Under the design-system clause a secondary failure is low.
  - **What would make it medium:** the Larder size select, the build guide's selects and the park map's selects sit on primary surfaces. But both skeptics agree those failures reproduce only in WebKit on Windows, which paints its own fill over any author background, even `background:red`. Chromium paints the author background, at 11.2-15.0:1.
  - **Raise to medium** if an iPad or iPhone shows the Larder select unreadable (Unresolved 1).
  - **Exposure:** anyone whose chosen palette's scheme differs from the device's Appearance: Midnight or Forest on a light-OS device, or Parchment or Frost on a dark-OS device. Themes follow the person to every device (`apps/hub.js:96-104`).
- **Areas:** f260 (confirmed). Larder, build guide and park map for the select facet (unresolved). The shell is not affected: its only select, `#pkind`, is `.ds .select` with `appearance: none` (`index.html:1667`; `apps/design.css:448`).
- **What happens.**
  - **The cause.** `apps/design.css:15` fixes `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root`, and it is the only `color-scheme` declaration. `applyTheme` sets `data-theme` and `data-scheme` but never `style.colorScheme` (`apps/hub.js:74-82`). So the UA paints control parts in the OS scheme, while their text takes the theme's `--text` through `button, input, select, textarea { … color: inherit }` (`apps/design.css:311`).
  - **Why the Copy button is exposed.** The week-note footer's Copy (`apps/f260.html:1297`) has no author rule: only `.jr .jft button` exists (`:333`), and F260's base rule sets `color: inherit` (`:45`).
  - **Measured** (both skeptics and the re-measure; computed root `colorScheme` is "light dark" in every case):

    | Theme / OS | WebKit | Chromium | With `colorScheme` = `data-scheme` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Midnight, light OS | 1.06 (fill #F4F4F4) | 1.01 (fill #EFEFEF) | WebKit 10.7; Chromium 4.58 |
    | Forest, light OS | 1.12 | 1.07 | 10.12; Chromium **4.33** |
    | Parchment, dark OS | 1.11 (fill #343434) | 2.58 (fill #6B6B6B) | 12.51; 11.97 |
    | Frost, dark OS | 1.25 | 2.92 | 14.14; 13.53 |
    | Hearth, light OS (control) | 13.65 | — | — |
    | Midnight, dark OS (control) | 10.7 | — | — |

  - **Checkboxes** paint in the OS scheme (a white box in Midnight). That is cosmetic: the box stays visible.
  - **The select facet.** In WebKit the Larder `#size` and the build guide's `#bmap` / `#hf` read 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.11 / 1.25. In Chromium the same selects read 14.16 / 13.19 / 11.21 / 15.02, because they declare an author background (`apps/leftovers.html:52-53`; template `:29`).
- **Expected.** Every UA-painted control follows the chosen theme. Each theme block declares its `color-scheme`, and hub.js applies the resolved scheme at runtime, so control text stays at least 4.5:1 in every palette on any OS Appearance. The Copy button also needs the missing `.jft` rule: with the scheme fixed, Chromium still reads 4.33 in Forest.
- **Why it matters.** Someone who picks Midnight on the kitchen iPad left in light Appearance gets a blank Copy in F260, and, if the select facet holds on iOS, blank pickers in the Larder and the build guide.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:15, 311, 448`; `apps/hub.js:74-82, 96-104`; `apps/f260.html:45, 333, 1297`; `apps/leftovers.html:52-53`.
  - Investigator: `native-controls.json`, `midnight-f260-week-note-copy-button.png`, `midnight-build-guide-view-menu-selects.png`, `native-controls-webkit-midnight-lightos.png`, `native-controls-chromium-parchment-darkos.png`.
  - Skeptics: `verify-native-controls-ignore-theme-1.json`, `-1-webkit-f260-midnight-lightos.png`, `-1-chromium-f260-midnight-lightos.png`, `-1-webkit-larder-midnight-lightos.png`, `verify-native-controls-ignore-theme-2-{webkit,chromium}.json`, `-2-webkit-midnight-lightos.png` (the red-background select painted white is the artefact proof), `-2-chromium-midnight-lightos.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/native-controls.mjs both` prints per engine, theme and OS mode. For example: `webkit/midnight-lightos #pb …→#f4f4f4 1.06` and `chromium/midnight-lightos #pb …→#efefef 1.01`.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-native-controls-ignore-theme-1.mjs both` gives the real-control table with the `colorScheme` counterfactual.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** measured real app controls only, with no injected probes: the Larder `select#size`, the F260 week-note Copy (week 38, with the vault opened on the local database with a throwaway passcode) and the build guide's `#bmap` / `#hf`. The run covered six theme and OS cases in each engine. It read the computed colour and `color-scheme`, sampled the rendered fill with the text hidden, then set `documentElement.style.colorScheme` to `data-scheme` and measured again.
    - Every number for the real controls matched.
    - Their first pass sampled the week-1 note, which sits inside a collapsed week; they corrected it to week 38.
  - **Skeptic 2** measured the Larder's `#size` and `#date` plus three probes: a default button with F260's Copy CSS, a select with an inline `background:red`, and a checkbox. Text and fill were taken from pixel diffs, in both engines, with the same counterfactual.
    - The button failed in both engines, and the counterfactual fixed every case.
    - WebKit painted even the red select white.
    - The date input honours its author background in both engines.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **The root cause and the default-button facet are confirmed in both engines.** Setting `colorScheme` from `data-scheme` fixes WebKit, and fixes Chromium except Forest, which reaches 4.33. The Copy also needs VIS-F260-5's styling.
  - **The select facet is not established.** It is a WebKit-on-Windows behaviour until a real device shows it.
  - **"Shell" is dropped** from the areas.
- **Related (not re-filed):** VIS-F260-5 (the unstyled Copy, low), VIS-LEFTOVERS-5 and VIS-DOLLYWOOD-8 (default controls look generic, low). None of these records the theme-versus-OS scheme mismatch or the contrast. P2-VIS-03 is a different mechanism (the CSS media query).
  - **Merge note:** the DARK investigator's draft (DARK-1) reports the same cause.

title: The Home reminder and Chat fields are identified only by a 2.5-2.8:1 placeholder and a 1.1-1.45:1 boundary in every theme, and each app draws placeholders in a different ink
block:
#### P4-COLOR-05 — The Home reminder and Chat fields are identified only by a 2.5-2.8:1 placeholder and a 1.1-1.45:1 boundary in every theme, and each app draws placeholders in a different ink

- **Severity: low.** Skeptic 1 rated it medium and skeptic 2 low; this section lowers it from the investigator's medium.
  - **The core is already filed.** The placeholder-only reminder and chat fields are Phase 2's low item (`audits/02-shell.md:5802-5805`), ruled under the same rule.
  - **Each field has a nearby cue:**
    - the reminder field sits under the "Reminders" card heading, beside its + button;
    - the Chat field is the only control on the Chat tab, next to Send;
    - the pairing-code field sits under its sheet title.
  - **The new facets are secondary:** the boundary measurement, the seven-theme sweep and the cross-app inconsistency.
  - **Skeptic 1's case for medium:** a daily control on a primary surface whose only identification fails both thresholds. It is recorded for Phase 5, which should reconcile P2's item with this one.
- **Areas:** shell (`#remtext`, `#chat-in`, `#rotcode`); f260 (`#pass1`, `#pass2`); prayer, dollywood and dollywood-live for the UA-grey facet; leftovers as the counter-example.
- **What happens.**
  - **Three shell fields have no label or aria-label:** `#remtext` (`index.html:1204`), `#chat-in` (`:387`) and `#rotcode` (`:1649`). The `.ds` placeholder colour is `--muted-decor` (`apps/design.css:445`), which the token's comment reserves for "placeholders, dividers, decorative only" (`:48`). The palette assumes a placeholder is never a field's only name.
  - **Placeholder contrast.** `#remtext` reads 2.66 in Hearth and System light, 2.70 in Parchment, 2.49 in Frost, 2.79 in Midnight and System dark, and 2.67 in Forest (both skeptics). `#chat-in` reads 2.46-2.83.
  - **Boundary.**
    - `#remtext`'s border (`--line`) reads 1.20-1.45 against its fill and card by computed colour (skeptic 1), and 1.17-1.27 as a rendered band (skeptic 2). The field fill equals the card fill (1.00).
    - `#chat-in` is borderless and transparent by design (`index.html:263`). The field people see is the glass composer `#chat-form`, which reads 1.07-1.12 against the page in all 7 keys. This is provisional because the rig paints glass without blur; the field is visible mainly by its shadow.
  - **Across apps there is no shared placeholder rule:**
    - Larder `#name`: `--muted` (`apps/leftovers.html:50`), 5.34-5.60. Passes.
    - F260 `.rf-f` and journal search: `--muted` (`apps/f260.html:182, 359`). Passes.
    - F260 `#pass1` / `#pass2`: aria-label only, under the title "Unlock journal". UA #A9A9A9: 1.74-1.77 in the light palettes, 7.21-7.24 in the dark ones. Parchment reaches 1.35 in the rig.
    - Prayer `#f-title` / `#f-for` / `#f-phone`: UA grey, 2.14-2.30 in light and 6.32 in dark. Each has a visible `<label for>` (`apps/prayer.html:480-489`), so the grey is only a hint.
    - Build guide `#q`: UA grey, 2.30 in Hearth, 7.01 in Midnight.
- **Expected.** Every field has a visible label, or its placeholder reaches at least 4.5:1 when it is the only name. Each field has a boundary of at least 3:1. One `::placeholder` rule in `design.css` applies everywhere, through tokens only, so F260 and Prayer keep their layouts and ids.
- **Why it matters.** The reminder and Chat fields are daily controls. For grandparents and in glare they read as blank bars. The same role is drawn in three different inks across the hub.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `index.html:263, 387, 1204, 1396, 1399, 1649`; `apps/design.css:48, 445`; `apps/leftovers.html:50`; `apps/f260.html:182, 359`; `apps/prayer.html:480-489`.
  - Investigator: `spot.json` (remtext-placeholder), `components.json` (placeholder-ds, placeholder-ua), `nontext-summary.json` (`input#remtext.input`, `input#chat-in.input`).
  - Skeptics: `verify-unlabelled-fields-unidentifiable-1.json`, `-1-chatform.json`, `-1-chatform-<theme>-<mode>.png`, `verify-unlabelled-fields-unidentifiable-2.json`, `-2-remtext-{system,midnight,frost}-lightos.png`, `-2-chatin-system-lightos.png`, `-2-f260pass-system-lightos.png`, `-2-prayer-system-lightos.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/shell/home-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/spot.mjs` prints "remtext-placeholder" p10 2.66 (system), 2.49 (frost) and 2.79 (midnight).
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-unlabelled-fields-unidentifiable-2.mjs` gives the rendered placeholder and boundary per theme.
  - `ONLY=chatform node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-unlabelled-fields-unidentifiable-1.mjs` gives the composer pane.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** ran 7 theme keys in WebKit as Eli. For each field it read the computed `::placeholder` colour, the fill, the border, the composited ancestor background, and whether a visible `<label>` exists; a second pass pixel-sampled `#chat-form`. It reproduced the placeholder and boundary ranges, then found:
    - the guest name and PIN fields are labelled (`index.html:1396, 1399`);
    - Prayer's fields are labelled;
    - F260 has `::placeholder` rules;
    - `#chat-in`'s "1.0" is a borderless input;
    - the core is a P2 item.
  - **Skeptic 2** measured rendered pixels, not tokens. For the placeholder it diffed screenshots with the placeholder set and emptied; for the boundary it compared the border band with the bands just outside and inside. It covered the same fields plus F260 `#pass1` and Prayer `#f-title`.
    - It confirmed the ranges and the same five corrections.
    - It added that iOS Safari's UA placeholder grey may differ from WebKit's #A9A9A9.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - **Two daily fields, plus the pairing-code field, rely on a `--muted-decor` placeholder.** The claim that fields are unlabelled everywhere is dropped: the guest and Prayer fields are labelled.
  - **The UA-grey facet is limited** to F260's passcode fields (which are aria-labelled), Prayer (labelled) and the build guide's search, and to the light palettes.
  - **`#chat-in`'s boundary is its composer bar.**
  - **This builds on P2's low items and does not replace them.**
- **Related (not re-filed):** P2 UX "The reminder and chat inputs are labelled only by placeholders" (low; `audits/02-shell.md:5802-5805`); the pairing-code sheet's placeholder-only fields (`audits/02-shell.md:1063-1064`); `#chat-in` (`audits/02-shell.md:3640, 4435`).

title: `--muted` is validated only on paper and cards: 4.45:1 on Hearth wells, 4.37 on Parchment wells, 4.49 on F260's New Testament paper, and about 4.0-4.2 on its New Testament wells
block:
#### P4-COLOR-06 — `--muted` is validated only on paper and cards: 4.45:1 on Hearth wells, 4.37 on Parchment wells, 4.49 on F260's New Testament paper, and about 4.0-4.2 on its New Testament wells

- **Severity: low.** Both skeptics rated it low; it is not raised or lowered.
  - **Clause:** every affected string is secondary (blurbs, counts, captions, hints, a step pill) and misses AA by 0.01-0.13. The rule makes a secondary failure low.
  - **Control labels:** Prayer's unpressed Mine/Family segment and F260's 11 px HEAR buttons are control labels. They are already covered at medium by VIS-PRAYER-1 and VIS-F260-1.
  - **What this defect adds** is the shared token cause.
- **Areas:** shell, kidverse, prayer, dollywood, f260.
- **What happens.**
  - **The token and its validation.** `--muted` is annotated "AA on paper and cards (4.9:1)" (`apps/design.css:47`). The system itself puts it on `--surface-2`, documented as "sunken wells, inputs" (`:43`).
  - **The style guide's check misses these pairs.** Its contrast list checks muted on bg and on surface, and text on surface-2, but not muted on surface-2 or any `color-mix()` surface (`docs/design.html:291-293`). `scripts/test-design.mjs:109-110` therefore cannot catch it.
  - **On wells:**
    - theme-card blurbs; Kid Verse badge hints ("prayed on 5 days", Ezra); Prayer's category counts and unpressed "Family" segment; the build guide's "step 8 of 9" pill;
    - they read 4.45 in Hearth and 4.37 in Parchment, and pass in Frost at 4.55.
  - **On F260's New Testament paper.** `body.nt` mixes 7 % teal into `--bg` (`apps/f260.html:30-33`), switched on from week 31 (`:1500`, so it is on at the demo date).
    - Hearth captions read 4.49 on #E7EAE3: ".sub", day labels, ring numbers, HEAR buttons. Skeptic 2 found 58 of 68 undimmed `--muted` items failing.
    - Parchment (4.56-4.58) and Frost (4.54) pass.
    - The New Testament wells (`--sunk`, `:32`) come to about 4.10 / 4.00 / 4.20 by token maths, the worst pair. The reflection field did not render in the skeptics' runs.
  - **Kid Verse "Also this week"** reads 4.46 p10 / 4.53 median only when scrolled into the top band of the fixed gold wash (`apps/kidverse.html:13-18`). Unscrolled it reads 4.85-4.90 and passes.
  - **Rig:** muted-on-well 476 occurrences, theme-card blurbs 456, F260 NT captions 2,874.
- **Expected.** Every text token is validated against every surface it can sit on, wells and `color-mix()` surfaces included, and holds at least 4.5:1.
- **Why it matters.** Each instance is small, but it is one token pair repeated across five areas. On F260 in Hearth it is the single largest cause of failing captions.
- **Evidence.**
  - Code: `apps/design.css:43, 47`; `apps/f260.html:30-33, 1500`; `apps/kidverse.html:13-18`; `docs/design.html:291-293`; `scripts/test-design.mjs:109-110`.
  - Investigator: `palette.json` (`themes.*.mutedOnSurface2`), `components.json` (muted-well, theme-blurb, f260-nt-muted).
  - Skeptics: `verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-1.json`, `-1-kidverse-hearth-also-desktop-scrolled-viewport.png` (4.46), `-1-kidverse-hearth-also-desktop-viewport.png` (4.9), `verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-2.json`, `-2-f260-hearth.png`.
  - Phase 1: `audits/screens/f260/behind-pace-typical-desktop-light.png`, `audits/screens/kidverse/kid-reading-typical-desktop-light.png`.
- **Reproduction.** From `cd "C:/Users/ex_bo/OneDrive/Claude Related/App Hub"`:
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep 'muted on bg'` prints system-light … s2 4.45 and parchment … s2 4.37.
  - `node -e "import('./audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.cr('#75675B', m.mix('#F7F2EB','#137F77',.93))))"` prints 4.49.
  - `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/verify-muted-on-wells-and-derived-surfaces-2.mjs` prints the rendered values.
- **Verified: 2/2 skeptics confirmed.**
  - **Skeptic 1** wrote their own token parser and WebKit run, taking text-hidden 1x screenshots with p10 and median per element. It covered the shell theme cards (Hearth, Parchment, Frost), F260 as Eli in Hearth, Kid Verse as Ezra on the iPad and desktop (scrolled and unscrolled), and Prayer's counts. They also sampled pixels straight from the Phase 1 capture.
    - The blurbs read 4.45 / 4.37 / 4.55, Prayer's counts 4.45 / 4.37 and F260 in Hearth 4.49.
    - Kid Verse read 4.90 unscrolled and 4.46 / 4.53 scrolled; the Phase 1 capture's pixels read 4.45-4.53.
    - They found every per-surface instance already filed, and corrected the `body.nt` line numbers.
  - **Skeptic 2** wrote their own parser with float WCAG maths and a WebKit run in the three light palettes. It walked every visible, undimmed text whose computed colour equals `--muted`, and composited the background chain.
    - Its values match skeptic 1's.
    - It attributed about 59 of VIS-F260-1's 150 Hearth items to the NT paper, from P3's `contrast.json`: 150 in Hearth against 91 in Parchment and Frost.
    - It found the gap in the style guide's check list.
    - It could not reproduce Kid Verse's 4.45, because its DOM composite ignores gradients; a 10 % gold mix gives 4.45.
- **Corrected claim.**
  - The `body.nt` rule is at `apps/f260.html:30-33`, not `:24-27`.
  - The NT paper accounts for about 59 of VIS-F260-1's 150 Hearth items, not "most". The rest fail in every light palette, from opacity dimming and gold ink.
  - Kid Verse's 4.45 depends on scroll position.
  - The NT wells, not the paper, are the worst pair.
  - Every per-surface instance is already filed. New here: the shared token cause, the `body.nt` attribution and the style guide's missing pairs.
- **Related (not re-filed):** the P2 VIS table's 4.45 theme-card-blurb row (`audits/02-shell.md:5814`), VIS-KIDVERSE-1, VIS-PRAYER-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-5 and VIS-F260-1 (whose checker already noted that the 4.49 items overstate how the page looks, `audits/03-apps/f260.md:707-708`).

block:
#### CONS-COLOR-1 — "Past", "done" and "not yet" are shown by dimming text with opacity, differently in every app: 1.46-3.5:1 (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens.** There is no AA-safe tertiary or "done" ink, so each app dims text with its own opacity:

  | Where | How | Measured |
  |---|---|---|
  | F260 past weeks | opacity .6 (`apps/f260.html:235`) | 2.21-2.88; their check discs (white on 60 % olive) 2.24-2.81 |
  | F260 unearned milestones | opacity .55 (`apps/f260.html:193`) | 2.01-2.59 |
  | Build guide done steps | opacity .55 plus strike-through (`apps/dollywood.html:101`) | 1.99-3.5 |
  | Park map rows filtered out for a kid's height | `.lv-item.noride{opacity:.55}` (template `:508`) | the 20 px/800 wait minutes at 1.46-1.54, below 3:1 even as large text (new); ride numbers at opacity .75, 1.73-1.79 p10 (median 3.2-3.36) |
  | TV board | "not read yet" faces | 2.05-3.1 |
  | Timer | time's-up 0:00 blinks to opacity .65 (`apps/timer.html:38-39`, `steps(2)`) | 2.42, under 3:1 even as large text (new) |
  | Home hero kicker | opacity .85 (`apps/design.css:417`) | P2 |

- **Expected.** One tertiary or "done" ink that passes AA, and no opacity on text. A state change shows through ink plus a glyph (a check, a strike-through), not through transparency.
- **Why it matters.** Dimmed states are most of the hub's failing text occurrences (F260's past weeks alone are 16,277), and each app picked its own value.
- **Evidence:** `components.json` (f260-past, f260-milestone, dw-done, dw-min, tv-dim, timer-blink); `remeasure-raw.json` (the Timer's 0:00 in `devices/timer/done-typical-desktop-light-system`); `audits/screens/dollywood-live/waits-kid-typical-desktop-light.png`; `audits/screens/f260/behind-typical-desktop-light.png`; `audits/screens/timer/done-typical-desktop-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/components.mjs | grep -i 'opacity\|wait tiles\|not read'`.
- **Related:** VIS-F260-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-1, VIS-DOLLYWOOD-LIVE-8.

section: Contrast of every text/background pair in use (COLOR)
title: The person's colour becomes ink through four recipes, and only `--accent-deep` is guaranteed (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-COLOR-3 — The person's colour becomes ink through four recipes, and only `--accent-deep` is guaranteed (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-6):
  - **Raw `--accent` / `--tint`** fails in both schemes: 1.49-2.93 in dark, and 2.25-4.41 in light for four colours (P4-COLOR-02; P2 for the shell).
  - **`--accent-deep`** passes on every surface, and fails only on the hero's fixed white fill (P4-COLOR-03).
  - **`--tint-ink` = 70 % colour + `--text`** (`index.html:955, 1070`) gives feed names at 4.22 for David in dark, 4.04 in Forest, 3.85-4.01 for the TV, and 4.03 for Kiara in Parchment (new; P2 recorded David).
  - **The app-tile `--tint`** reads 1.95-2.81 (VIS-COLOR-1).
- **Expected.** One per-scheme person-ink pair, derived in one place and contrast-checked, used by every area.
- **Why it matters.** Profile colours are editable in the admin panel, and guests pick from swatches. Only an ink derived with a contrast floor can guarantee that a new colour passes. Today, whether a colour passes depends on which recipe an area happened to use.
- **Evidence:** `palette.json` (`profiles.*.themes.*`); `parchment-home-feed-names.png`; `audits/evidence/p4/measure/failing-pairs/shell.json` (`div.fwho` Parchment #8F6A1B 4.03).

section: Contrast of every text/background pair in use (COLOR)
title: Semantic colours are neither consistent between areas nor unmistakable (investigator rating: low)
block:
#### CONS-COLOR-4 — Semantic colours are neither consistent between areas nor unmistakable (investigator rating: low)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-7):
  - **The aliases reach four files only:** the shell, the Larder, the Timer (`--danger` only) and the Dollywood template (`--ok`, `--danger`). The draft's "only the Larder and the shell" was corrected by a grep.
  - **F260 and Prayer map meaning to hue families their own way.** The template adds a literal traffic-light set: #1E8A4C / #C77A00 / #C8391F / #6A6259.
  - **A finished Timer shows the destructive red.** Mae's running ring is the same hex as `--danger` in Hearth.
  - **Success against destructive** (olive against terra) has a luminance ratio of 1.00 in all three light palettes. Under deuteranopia they are ΔE 4.0-5.1 apart (the re-measure gets 4.2 in Hearth, a difference in the simulation variant). Success against info is only ΔE 8.0-8.7, even with normal vision.
  - **The soft chip fills** are within ΔE 6.5 of each other, and the park map's green and red bands are 1.18:1 in luminance.
  - **Four household colours are semantic colours:** Mae = `--danger`, Ezra = `--info`, Kiara = `--warn`, Mea = `--ok` (P2 VIS, `audits/02-shell.md:5786-5790`).
  - **The house pastels do not solve it alone:** Mint against Bubblegum is deutan ΔE 3.4 as fills and 2.0 as inks.
- **Expected.** One semantic set used everywhere, drawn from the pastel family with AA inks:
  - success, warning, destructive and info;
  - separated by lightness (success against destructive at a luminance ratio of 1.3 or more);
  - always paired with a glyph;
  - never reused as a profile colour.
- **Why it matters.** The house style requires semantic colours that stay unmistakable. Today their meaning changes from app to app, and red against green is carried by hue alone.
- **Evidence:** `semantic.json`; `apps/design.css:80-83`; `apps/f260.html:11-12`; `apps/prayer.html:106, 230, 311`; `apps/timer.html:36-38`; template `:495-496, 501`; `worker/seed.sql:4-11`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/semantic.mjs`.
- **Related:** VIS-PRAYER-10; P2 VIS "Profile colours double as the semantic colours".

section: Contrast of every text/background pair in use (COLOR)
title: The fills and tiles sit at about a third of the house chroma in all five palettes, two house hues are missing, and dark cards barely lift off the page (investigator rating: medium)
block:
#### VIS-COLOR-1 — The fills and tiles sit at about a third of the house chroma in all five palettes, two house hues are missing, and dark cards barely lift off the page (investigator rating: medium)

- **What happens** (Table COLOR-8):
  - **Soft fills.** They sit at the pastels' lightness (L 0.87-0.94, against 0.876-0.953) but at about a third of their chroma (C 0.008-0.070, against 0.057-0.093). Parchment's gold-soft, at 0.070, is the only exception. `--accent-soft` for the ten swatches is 0.004-0.047.
  - **Tiles.** They run pale to paler, a 22 % → 8 % tint over the surface (`apps/design.css:606-608`), instead of pastel to saturated. The icon ink is the raw app colour: Kid Verse's gold is 2.39-2.81 in light (new), and the Larder's and F260's are 1.95-2.33 in dark (P2).
  - **Hues.** Six earth families span hues 42-274°. Bubblegum (354°) and Lavender (303°) have no counterpart, and Sky (252°) and Periwinkle (278°) collapse into one slate.
  - **Other gradients.**
    - The hero runs within one hue, from 70 % white through the accent to `--accent-deep` (`apps/design.css:412`), and stays pale in dark (P2-VIS-06).
    - The page wash mixes two hues, the accent at 10 % and gold at 6 % (`:70-71`; the draft cited `:67-68`).
    - The `.bar` fill starts at 75 % tint + white (`:534`). That is why the bars read 2.27-2.99 against their tracks.
  - **Neutrals.**
    - Hearth's page is warm paper (H 77, C 0.011) at the lightness of iOS #F2F2F7 (H 286). Parchment is tan (L 0.89, C 0.039). Frost alone matches iOS.
    - In dark, the card-to-page step is 1.10-1.12, against iOS's 1.23, and the well is darker than the page (1.04).
- **Expected (house style).**
  - Pastel fills at C ≈ 0.055-0.095, with a deep ink of the same hue.
  - Tiles running pastel to saturated within one hue, with an AA ink.
  - All eight house hues available for profiles and chips.
  - Grouped grey with white cards in light; near-black with a card elevated 1.2:1 or more in dark.
- **Why it matters.** This is the house style's central colour rule, and the main reason every area scores 3-5 on Colour & palette.
- **Evidence:** `palette.json` (`themes.*.softChroma`, `houseFillChroma`, `neutrals`), `tiles.json`, `audits/evidence/p4/measure/nontext/shell.json` (`span.app-icon.ticon > svg.icon`), `audits/screens/shell/apps-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`, `audits/screens/shell/home-typical-ipad-portrait-light.png`.
- **Reproduction:** `node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/palette.mjs | grep 'soft C\|house fill chroma'; node audits/tools/phase4/COLOR/tiles.mjs`.
- **Related:** P2 VIS "The earthy Hearth palette, not the house pastels" (`audits/02-shell.md:5778-5785`), which measured Hearth and Midnight only. This extends it to Parchment, Frost and Forest and to the tiles.
  - **Merge note:** the ACCENT draft's ACC-10 covers the profile-colour side.
